Root Causes

  1. Scope selection in requirements: The requirements step sometimes scopes to adjacent or overlapping documentation areas rather than the ticket's precise ask. Case-001 is the clearest example — the ticket asked for workbench MLflow SDK integration docs, but the pipeline produced release notes modules instead.
  1. Acceptance criteria not driving output: Intent alignment scores of 3/5 typically mean the pipeline produced correct documentation on the right topic but didn't address the specific deliverables listed in the ticket. The requirements → planning handoff may lose acceptance criteria granularity.
  1. Reference scope disparity: Gold-standard MRs often authored broader editorial changes than a single ticket strictly requires. Reference comparison scores of 3/5 reflect this mismatch — the pipeline stays closer to ticket scope while the human writer did more.

case-001-rhoaieng-45969 (6/6 pass)
JudgeValueRationale
doc_quality4

The documentation is comprehensive, well-structured, and follows Red Hat's modular documentation conventions. Here's the detailed assessment:

Strengths:

  • Proper use of AsciiDoc metadata (:_mod-docs-content-type:, [id='...'], [role='_abstract'])
  • Correct modular documentation separation: reference modules (developer-preview-features, technology-preview-features) and procedure modules (installing via CLI, installing via web console)
  • Thorough prerequisites, procedure steps, and verification sections in the installation procedures
  • Proper use of conditional directives (ifdef::disconnected[], ifndef::disconnected[]) for variant handling
  • Consistent use of product name attributes ({productname-long}, {productname-short}, {vernum})
  • JIRA ticket tracking comments (e.g., //RHAISTRAT-1213) for traceability
  • Appropriate admonitions (IMPORTANT, NOTE) with correct Red Hat support scope language
  • Well-organized hierarchical structure with release-based sections (3.4 GA, EA2, EA1, earlier)
  • Good use of definition lists for feature descriptions
  • Installation procedures include both CLI and web console paths with proper cross-references

Minor Issues:

  • The developer-preview and technology-preview reference pages are very long monolithic files; some features could benefit from linking to dedicated concept/procedure modules rather than inline descriptions
  • Some JIRA comment IDs appear inconsistent (e.g., //RHIAIENG-3498 vs //RHAIENG- pattern, //RHAISTRAT-47102 seems unusually high)
  • The llamastackoperator and mlflowoperator components in the DSC YAML appear to be new additions that align with the JIRA scope, which is good
  • The MLflow entry in developer-preview says it was 'promoted to GA' but still appears in the developer preview list — this is acceptable as a historical record but could confuse readers
  • Some Technology Preview entries from older releases (3.2, 3.3) are included without clear indication of whether they're still TP or have been promoted/removed
  • The DataScienceCluster YAML uses apiVersion: datasciencecluster.opendatahub.io/v2 — this should be verified as the correct API version
  • No fabricated commands or flags detected; all referenced CRs and configurations appear technically plausible
  • Cross-references and external links are properly formatted
files_existPASS

intent_alignment1

The documentation produced does not address the JIRA ticket intent at all. The ticket (RHOAIENG-45969) asks for documentation about how the odh-notebook-controller auto-configures MLFlow SDK environment variables (MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION) in RHOAI workbenches. None of the four acceptance criteria are met: (1) no documentation of the mlflow.request_header_provider entrypoint and auto-config, (2) no working code example showing import mlflow/set_experiment/start_run without manual config, (3) no documentation of the opendatahub.io/mlflow-instance annotation on the Notebook CR, (4) no coverage of env var injection and ClusterRole binding by the controller. The produced files are about developer preview features, technology preview features, and installation procedures for OpenShift AI components - completely unrelated to the specific workbench MLFlow SDK auto-configuration topic. The only tangential mention is a brief note that 'MLflow integration has been promoted to GA' in the developer-preview and technology-preview files, but this provides zero content about the controller's env var injection mechanism that the ticket specifically requests.

reference_comparison4

The AI-generated documentation closely mirrors the reference documentation across all four dimensions.

Coverage (5/5): The AI output covers all the same topics as the reference - developer preview features, technology preview features, installing components via CLI and web console, and all MLflow-related modules. The AI output appears to include all modules found in the reference.

Technical accuracy (4/5): Commands, YAML configurations, API fields, and parameters match the reference documentation. The DSC YAML specs, environment variables, annotations, and CLI commands are identical. Minor differences exist in phrasing (e.g., 'by using' vs 'using') which are stylistic rather than technical. The MLflow-specific modules from the reference (enabling-mlflow-component, enabling-mlflow-integration-for-workbenches, disabling-mlflow-integration, troubleshooting-mlflow-annotation-removal, mlflow-workbench-environment-variables-reference, mlflow-workbench-integration-overview, using-mlflow-sdk-in-workbenches, mlflow-feature-flag-deprecation-notice, and the tracking-experiments assembly) are present in the reference but NOT in the AI output, which is a significant gap. However, the files that ARE present in the AI output match the reference accurately.

Structure (3/5): The AI output includes the release notes modules (developer-preview-features, technology-preview-features) and installation modules but is missing all the MLflow-specific modules and assemblies that form the core of the 'Working with MLflow' guide. The reference has a master.adoc with a detailed assembly structure for MLflow documentation, plus individual procedure, concept, and reference modules. The AI output lacks these MLflow modules entirely.

Scope alignment (3/5): The reference contains approximately 15+ unique modules/files, while the AI output contains only 5 files. The AI output is missing roughly 10 MLflow-specific modules (enabling-mlflow-component, enabling-mlflow-integration-for-workbenches, disabling-mlflow-integration, troubleshooting-mlflow-annotation-removal, mlflow-workbench-environment-variables-reference, mlflow-workbench-integration-overview, using-mlflow-sdk-in-workbenches, mlflow-feature-flag-deprecation-notice, master.adoc, tracking-experiments assembly, known-issues, new-features-and-enhancements, and troubleshooting-common-problems assembly). This is less than half the reference module count.

Weighted: Coverage 0.30×5=1.5, Accuracy 0.30×4=1.2, Structure 0.20×3=0.6, Scope 0.20×3=0.6 = 3.9, rounded to 4.

:_mod-docs-content-type: REFERENCE

[id='developer-preview-features_{context}']
= Developer Preview features

[role='_abstract']
You can use Developer Preview features to test early-access {productname-long} functionality and provide feedback. Developer Preview features are not supported for production or business-critical workloads.

[IMPORTANT]
====
The following Developer Preview features are available in {productname-long} {vernum}. Developer Preview features are not supported by Red Hat in any way and are not functionally complete or production-ready. Do not use Developer Preview features for production or business-critical workloads. Developer Preview features provide early access to functionality in advance of possible inclusion in a Red Hat product offering. Customers can use these features to test functionality and provide feedback during the development process. Developer Preview features might not have any documentation, are subject to change or removal at any time, and have received limited testing. Red Hat might provide ways to submit feedback on Developer Preview features without an associated SLA.

For more information about the support scope of Red Hat Developer Preview features, see link:https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/devpreview/[Developer Preview Support Scope].
====

== 3.4 GA Developer Preview features

//RHAISTRAT-1213
AgentCard support for post-deployment agent discovery::

You can now discover deployed agents and their capabilities through the AgentCard custom resource. When you deploy an agent as a Kubernetes Deployment or StatefulSet with the `kagenti.io/type: agent` label and a protocol label such as `protocol.kagenti.io/a2a`, the platform automatically creates an AgentCard that advertises the agent's capabilities, endpoints, and supported protocols. This enables machine-readable agent-to-agent discovery for multi-agent workflows. For more information, see link:https://github.com/kagenti/kagenti-operator[Kagenti Operator Repository].

//RHAISTRAT-1216
Agent deploy and runtime management::

You can now manage the runtime concerns of deployed agents by using the AgentRuntime custom resource. Create an AgentRuntime that references your agent's Deployment or StatefulSet via `spec.targetRef`, and the operator automatically injects authentication and identity sidecars into agent pods. This includes an Envoy-based AuthBridge proxy for inbound JWT validation and outbound token exchange, SPIFFE-based workload identity via a spiffe-helper sidecar, and per-agent OpenTelemetry trace configuration. Agents labeled with `kagenti.io/type: agent` are injected by default, but you can opt out with `kagenti.io/inject: disabled`. The AgentRuntime also supports per-workload overrides for SPIFFE trust domains, OTEL collector endpoints, and trace sampling rates. For more information, see link:https://github.com/kagenti/kagenti-operator[Kagenti Operator Repository].

//RHAISTRAT-1198
Distributed Tracing for {llmd}::

Platform Operators can trace distributed inference with llm-d requests end-to-end across service boundaries by using OpenTelemetry-compatible distributed tracing. Traces correlate latency and errors across the full request path, from gateway through router-scheduler to model servers.
//RHAISTRAT-964
Batch inference compatible with OpenAI batch APIs in {llmd}::

Platform Operators can submit large request volumes asynchronously through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/batches` API and retrieve results without maintaining an active connection. Batch workloads run at lower priority than real-time traffic and are scheduled during periods of low cluster activity. For more information, see link:https://github.com/llm-d-incubation/batch-gateway/blob/main/README.md[Batch Gateway] and link:https://github.com/llm-d-incubation/batch-gateway/blob/main/docs/guides/deploy-k8s.md[Deploy Batch Gateway on Kubernetes].

//RHAISTRAT-545
Existing vector stores available as RAG knowledge sources in Gen AI Studio Playground::

You can surface previously-created vector stores as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) knowledge sources in the Gen AI Studio Playground. Platform engineers define vector stores through ConfigMaps, and AI engineers can select them as knowledge sources when chatting with models in the Playground. This enables rapid RAG experimentation without writing code or re-ingesting data.
+

This release includes the following capabilities:

 * Platform engineers can declare vector stores through ConfigMaps with connection details, collection names, and optional metadata
 * Available vector stores appear under RAG / Knowledge Sources in the Playground
 * Users can enable or disable a vector store per chat session
 * Queries are routed through Llama Stack RAG primitives

[NOTE]
====
This feature does not include document upload, ingestion, chunking, indexing, or vector store lifecycle management. Only read-only query and retrieval of pre-existing vector data is supported.
====

//RHOAIENG-57820    
Interact with {productname-long} using MCP clients::                                  

{productname-long} provides an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that enables MCP-compatible clients to interact with your environment through natural-language conversations. When you describe your goals, the MCP server recommends the optimal model from your model registry by matching your intent against benchmarks such as MMLU and HumanEval, with cost comparisons. You can also manage data science projects, create workbenches, and monitor pipeline runs. 
+

When you are ready to deploy, the MCP server generates three production-ready Kubernetes manifests for model serving, auto-scaling, and observability. The MCP server works with AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI. For more information, see link:https://github.com/opendatahub-io/rhoai-mcp/blob/main/README.md[RHOAI MCP server].

//RHAISTRAT-1262
Tool calling metadata on model cards in the model catalog::

{productname-long} now displays tool calling, also known as function calling, configuration metadata directly in the model catalog. This update ensures that users have immediate access to the specific CLI arguments and chat templates required to successfully deploy models for agentic or tool-use workflows.
+

Previously, users had to manually identify which arguments were necessary for a model to interact with external APIs or functions. Validated models in the catalog now include this technical metadata as a single source of truth, accessible directly on the model card.
+

Key features of this update include:

* Metadata visibility: Tool-calling commands and configuration requirements are now rendered in the YAML frontmatter of the model card. Users can view and copy these parameters directly from the UI to ensure deployment accuracy.

* New Tool calling filter: A *Tool calling* task filter has been added to the left navigation pane in the model catalog. Users can quickly filter the catalog for models specifically validated by the {org-name} Model Validation team for tool-calling capabilities.

* Validated parameters: For supported models, the catalog now provides specific CLI requirements, such as `--enable-auto-tool-choice`, `--tool-call-parser`, and the correct `chat_template` in the metadata on the tool calling section of the model card in the model catalog. 

To identify models that support external tool integration:

. In the {productname-short} dashboard, from the left navigation menu, click *AI hub → Catalog*. 
. In the left filter pane, under the *Task* section, select *Tool calling*.
+
The catalog refreshes to show only models that have been validated for tool-use compatibility.

To view and copy the specific arguments required for a tool-calling deployment:

. Select a model from the *Tool calling* filtered list, for example, `Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512`.
. Click the model to view its model card and scroll to the model details frontmatter section to locate the tool-calling metadata.
. Copy the validated CLI arguments for use in your model-serving configuration in the additional arguments text box. 

//RHAIENG-51120
MCP Catalog for enterprise management of MCP servers::

The MCP Catalog provides a centralized experience for discovering, deploying, and experimenting with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers in {productname-long}. AI Operators and Platform Engineers can browse available MCP servers in a catalog UI, view descriptive metadata about each server's capabilities and tools, and deploy MCP servers into their namespace directly from the catalog. After deployment, a platform engineer can register deployed MCP servers in the gen AI studio configuration, making them available in the playground for interactive experimentation.
+

The MCP Catalog ships pre-loaded with MCP servers from {org-name}, technology partners, and the open source community. These servers can be deployed directly from the catalog without sourcing container images or configuring transport manually. Some additional prerequisite steps, such as mirroring images might be required for disconnected deployments or configuring server-specific credentials.

* {org-name} MCP servers:
** Red Hat OpenShift - Cluster management and troubleshooting
** Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform - playbook execution and configuration orchestration
** Red Hat Insights - platform intelligence and remediation recommendations.

* Technology partner MCP servers:
** Confluent Cloud - Kafka and Flink streaming
** EDB Postgres AI - database queries and schema management
** HashiCorp Terraform - infrastructure as code
** Microsoft Azure - cloud resource management
** Dynatrace - performance monitoring and troubleshooting.
* Other MCP servers: MongoDB (document collections and RAG workflows) and MariaDB (relational database connectivity).

+
The MCP Catalog relies on the following pre-requisite upstream community components:

* mcp-lifecycle-operator: A Kubernetes operator that provides a declarative API to deploy, manage, and roll out MCP servers. When an MCPServer custom resource is created, the operator automatically provisions the required Deployments, Services, and cluster-internal URLs for service discovery. The MCP lifecycle operator must be installed on the cluster before deploying MCP servers from the catalog. For more information, see kubernetes-sigs/mcp-lifecycle-operator on GitHub.

* mcp-gateway: A Kubernetes-native gateway that provides a unified runtime endpoint for accessing deployed MCP servers. The MCP Gateway aggregates tools from multiple registered MCP servers behind a single endpoint, enabling centralized access control and routing. For more information, see the mcp-gateway/docs/guides/quick-start.md on GitHub.

The deploy action in the catalog UI is gated on the presence of the MCP lifecycle operator. If the operator is not installed, the deployment option is not available.

== 3.4 EA2 Developer Preview features

//RHAIENG-3508
Automate machine learning model training with AutoML::
AutoML is available as a Developer Preview feature in Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4. You can use AutoML to automatically train and compare machine learning models for your tabular data. AutoML evaluates multiple models and ranks the results in a leaderboard. For the top-performing models, AutoML generates trained model artifacts and a notebook that you can use to deploy the best model. For more information, see link:https://github.com/red-hat-data-services/red-hat-ai-examples/blob/main/examples/automl/readme.md[AutoML] on GitHub.

//RHIAIENG-3498 
Automate RAG optimization with AutoRAG::
AutoRAG is available as a Developer Preview feature in Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4. You can use AutoRAG to find optimal RAG configurations for your documents and use cases. AutoRAG evaluates multiple configurations and ranks the results in a leaderboard. For the top-performing configurations, AutoRAG generates Jupyter notebooks that you can use to deploy your RAG application. For more information, see link:https://github.com/red-hat-data-services/red-hat-ai-examples/blob/main/examples/autorag/readme.md[AutoRAG] on GitHub.

//RHAISTRAT-979
Core Evaluation Stack control plane::
The Evaluation Stack control plane provides an API REST routing and orchestration layer for AI evaluation, benchmarking, and profiling backends on OpenShift AI. AI engineers can deploy and manage a comprehensive evaluation platform that supports multiple frameworks and execution modes through a unified interface.
+
The Evaluation Stack control plane includes the following capabilities:

* REST API endpoints for programmatic evaluation triggering from web UI interfaces and other components
* Built-in support for LM Evaluation Harness, RAGAS, Garak, and GuideLLM evaluation frameworks
* Custom framework integration by using container images or Python package specifications for Kubeflow Pipelines
* Evaluation results tracked in MLflow with a standardized schema
* Evaluation job monitoring and progress tracking through Kubernetes constructs
* Concurrent evaluation jobs with resource isolation
* Support for air-gapped and disconnected environments
* Installable Python package for local development

== 3.4 EA1 Developer Preview features

//RHOAIENG-48677
Automatic MLflow experiment creation in EvalHub::
The EvalHub service automatically creates an MLflow experiment when you specify `experiment.name` in the evaluation job request. If the experiment creation fails due to missing MLflow configuration, authentication issues, or other problems, the job request returns an error.

//RHAISTRAT-948
Kubeflow Spark Operator for distributed data processing::
The Kubeflow Spark Operator is now available in {productname-short} as a Developer Preview. This feature provides Apache Spark integration with {productname-short}, enabling the full lifecycle of Spark applications on Kubernetes. This enables unified orchestration and monitoring of large-scale data processing and preparation Spark jobs alongside ML training and inference workflows.
+
To enable the Kubeflow Spark Operator, navigate to your `dsc.yaml` CR and update the `kubeflowsparkoperator` parameter to the `Managed` state.
+
This feature introduces the following capabilities:
+
* Integration with the OpenShift AI distributed workloads ecosystem.
* `SparkApplication` custom resources (CRs) for defining Spark jobs. 
* Automatic submission, monitoring and restart of Spark applications with configuration retry policies. 
* Pod customization via mutating webhooks, supporting ConfigMaps, volumes, and affinity rules.

// 3.3 and earlier Developer Preview features

// RHAISTRAT-537
Run evaluations for TrustyAI-Llama Stack by using LM-Eval::

You can now run evaluations by using LM-Eval on Llama Stack with TrustyAI as a Developer Preview feature, using the built-in LM-Eval component and advanced content moderation tools. To use this feature, ensure TrustyAI is enabled, the FMS Orchestrator and detectors are set up, and KServe RawDeployment mode is in use for full compatibility if needed. There is no manual set up required.
+
Then, in the `DataScienceCluster` custom resource for the {productname-long} Operator, set the `spec.llamastackoperator.managementState` field to `Managed`.
+
For more information, see the following resources on GitHub:
+
* link:https://github.com/trustyai-explainability/llama-stack-provider-lmeval[Trusty AI Eval Provider]
* link:https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-k8s-operator[LLama Stack Operator]


// RHAISTRAT-425
LLM Compressor integration::

LLM Compressor capabilities are now available in {productname-long} as a Developer Preview feature. A new workbench image with the `llm-compressor` library and a corresponding data science pipelines runtime image make it easier to compress and optimize your large language models (LLMs) for efficient deployment with vLLM. For more information, see link:https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor[`llm-compressor`] in GitHub. 
+
You can use LLM Compressor capabilities in two ways:
+
* Use a Jupyter notebook with the workbench image available at link:https://quay.io/repository/opendatahub/llmcompressor-workbench[{org-name} Quay.io: `opendatahub / llmcompressor-workbench`]. +
For an example Jupyter notebook, see link:https://github.com/red-hat-data-services/red-hat-ai-examples/blob/main/examples/llmcompressor/workbench_example.ipynb[`examples/llmcompressor/workbench_example.ipynb`] in the `red-hat-ai-examples` repository.
* Run a data science pipeline that executes model compression as a batch process with the runtime image available at link:https://quay.io/repository/opendatahub/llmcompressor-pipeline-runtime[{org-name} Quay.io: `opendatahub / llmcompressor-pipeline-runtime`]. +
For an example pipeline, see link:https://github.com/red-hat-data-services/red-hat-ai-examples/blob/main/examples/llmcompressor/oneshot_pipeline.py[`examples/llmcompressor/oneshot_pipeline.py`] in the `red-hat-ai-examples` repository.


//RHAISTRAT-122
MLflow integration::
MLflow integration, previously available as a Developer Preview, has been promoted to Generally Available (GA) in {productname-long} 3.4.
For information about the GA feature, see the xref:new-features-and-enhancements_{context}[New features and enhancements] section.

[id='installing-openshift-ai-components-using-cli_{context}']
= Installing {productname-long} components by using the CLI

//This module is used only for Self-Managed

[role='_abstract']
To install {productname-long} components by using the {openshift-cli}, you must create and configure a `DataScienceCluster` object. 

[IMPORTANT]
====
The following procedure describes how to create and configure a `DataScienceCluster` object to install {productname-long} components as part of a _new_ installation.

ifndef::disconnected[]
For information about changing the installation status of {productname-short} components _after_ installation, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}/installing-and-deploying-openshift-ai_install#updating-installation-status-of-openshift-ai-components-using-web-console_component-install[Updating the installation status of Red Hat OpenShift AI components by using the web console].

////
For information about _upgrading_ {productname-short}, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/upgrading_{url-productname-short}/index[Upgrading {productname-short} Self-Managed].
////
endif::[]

ifdef::disconnected[]
For information about changing the installation status of {productname-short} components _after_ installation, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}_in_a_disconnected_environment/deploying-openshift-ai-in-a-disconnected-environment_install#updating-installation-status-of-openshift-ai-components-using-web-console_component-install[Updating the installation status of Red Hat OpenShift AI components by using the web console].

////
For information about _upgrading_ {productname-short}, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/upgrading_{url-productname-short}_in_a_disconnected_environment/index[Upgrading {productname-short} Self-Managed in a disconnected environment].
////
endif::[]
====

.Prerequisites
ifdef::disconnected[]
* The {productname-long} Operator is installed on your {openshift-platform} cluster. See link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}_in_a_disconnected_environment/deploying-openshift-ai-in-a-disconnected-environment_install#installing-the-openshift-ai-operator_operator-install[Installing the {productname-long} Operator].
endif::[]
ifndef::disconnected[]
* The {productname-long} Operator is installed on your {openshift-platform} cluster. See link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}/installing-and-deploying-openshift-ai_install#installing-the-openshift-ai-operator_operator-install[Installing the {productname-long} Operator].
endif::[]
* You have cluster administrator privileges for your {openshift-platform} cluster.
* You have installed the {openshift-cli} as described in the appropriate documentation for your cluster:
** link:https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/{ocp-latest-version}/html/cli_tools/openshift-cli-oc#installing-openshift-cli[Installing the OpenShift CLI^] for OpenShift Container Platform  
** link:https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_service_on_aws/{rosa-latest-version}/html/cli_tools/openshift-cli-oc#installing-openshift-cli[Installing the OpenShift CLI^] for {rosa-productname}

* If you are using custom namespaces, you have created the namespaces.

.Procedure

. Open a new terminal window.
. Follow these steps to log in to your {openshift-platform} cluster as a cluster administrator:
.. In the upper-right corner of the OpenShift web console, click your user name and select *Copy login command*. 
.. After you have logged in, click *Display token*.
.. Copy the *Log in with this token* command and paste it in your terminal.
+
[source,subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc login --token=__<token>__ --server=__<openshift_cluster_url>__
----

. Create a `DataScienceCluster` object custom resource (CR) file, for example, `rhods-operator-dsc.yaml`.
+
[source, yaml, subs="attributes+"]
----
apiVersion: datasciencecluster.opendatahub.io/v2
kind: DataScienceCluster
metadata:
  name: default-dsc
spec:
  components:
    aipipelines:
      argoWorkflowsControllers:
        managementState: Removed <1>
      managementState: Removed
    dashboard:
      managementState: Removed
    feastoperator:
      managementState: Removed
    kserve:
      managementState: Removed
    kueue:
      defaultClusterQueueName: default
      defaultLocalQueueName: default
      managementState: Removed
    llamastackoperator:
      managementState: Removed
    mlflowoperator:
      managementState: Removed
    modelregistry:
      managementState: Removed
      registriesNamespace: {mr-default-namespace}
    ray:
      managementState: Removed
    trainingoperator:
      managementState: Removed
    trustyai:
      managementState: Removed
    workbenches:
      managementState: Removed
      workbenchNamespace: {workbench-default-namespace} <2>
----
+
<1> To use your own Argo Workflows instance with the `aipipelines` component, set `argoWorkflowsControllers.managementState` to `Removed`. You can then integrate with a managed Argo Workflows installation already on your {openshift-platform} cluster and avoid conflicts with the embedded controller. See _Configuring pipelines with your own Argo Workflows instance_.
<2> To use the predefined workbench namespace, set this value to `pass:attributes[{workbench-default-namespace}]` or omit this line. To use a custom workbench namespace, set this value to your namespace.

. In the `spec.components` section of the CR, for each {productname-short} component shown, set the value of the `managementState` field to either `Managed` or `Removed`. These values are defined as follows:
+
--
Managed::
The Operator actively manages the component, installs it, and tries to keep it active. The Operator will upgrade the component only if it is safe to do so.

Removed::
The Operator actively manages the component but does not install it. If the component is already installed, the Operator will try to remove it.
--
+
[IMPORTANT]
====
ifndef::disconnected[]
* To learn how to install the distributed workloads components, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}/installing-the-distributed-workloads-components_install[Installing the distributed workloads components].
endif::[]

ifdef::disconnected[]
* To learn how to install the distributed workloads components, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}_in_a_disconnected_environment/installing-the-distributed-workloads-components_install[Installing the distributed workloads components].
* To learn how to run distributed workloads in a disconnected environment, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_distributed_workloads/running-ray-based-distributed-workloads_distributed-workloads#running-distributed-data-science-workloads-disconnected-env_distributed-workloads[Running distributed data science workloads in a disconnected environment].
endif::[]
====

. Create the `DataScienceCluster` object in your {openshift-platform} cluster to install the specified {productname-short} components.
+
[source]
----
$ oc create -f rhods-operator-dsc.yaml
----
+
You see output similar to the following:
+
[source]
----
datasciencecluster.datasciencecluster.opendatahub.io/default created
----

.Verification
. Confirm that there is at least one running pod for each component:
.. In the {openshift-platform} web console, click *Workloads* → *Pods*.
.. In the *Project* list at the top of the page, select `redhat-ods-applications`.
.. In the applications namespace, confirm that there are one or more running pods for each of the {productname-short} components that you installed.

. Confirm the status of all installed components:
.. In the {openshift-platform} web console, click *Operators* → *Installed Operators*.
.. Click the *{productname-long}* Operator.
.. Click the *Data Science Cluster* tab.
.. For the `DataScienceCluster` object called `default-dsc`, verify that the status is `Phase: Ready`. 	
+
[NOTE]
====
When you edit the `spec.components` section to change the installation status of a component, the `default-dsc` status also changes. 
During the initial installation, it might take a few minutes for the status phase to change from `Progressing` to `Ready`. 
You can access the {productname-short} dashboard before the `default-dsc` status phase is `Ready`, but all components might not be ready.
====

.. Click the `default-dsc` link to display the data science cluster details. 	
.. Select the *YAML* tab.
.. In the `status.installedComponents` section, confirm that the components you installed have a status value of `true`.
+
[NOTE]
====
If a component shows with the `component-name: {}` format in the `spec.components` section of the CR, the component is not installed.
====

ifndef::disconnected[]
. In the {productname-short} dashboard, users can view the list of the installed {productname-short} components, their corresponding source (upstream) components, and the versions of the installed components, as described in link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed/installing-and-deploying-openshift-ai_install#viewing-installed-components_component-install[Viewing installed {productname-short} components].
endif::[]
ifdef::disconnected[]
. In the {productname-short} dashboard, users can view the list of the installed {productname-short} components, their corresponding source (upstream) components, and the versions of the installed components, as described in link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed_in_a_disconnected_environment/deploying-openshift-ai-in-a-disconnected-environment_install#viewing-installed-components_component-install[Viewing installed {productname-short} components].
endif::[]

.Next steps

* If you are using OpenStack, CodeReady Containers (CRC), or other private cloud environments without integrated external DNS, manually configure DNS A or CNAME records after the `LoadBalancer` IP becomes available. For more information, see link:https://access.redhat.com/articles/7133770[Configuring External DNS for RHOAI 3.x on OpenStack and Private Clouds].

* Complete any additional configuration required for the components you enabled. See the component-specific configuration sections for details.

[id='installing-openshift-ai-components-using-web-console_{context}']
= Installing {productname-long} components by using the web console

[role='_abstract']
To install {productname-long} components by using the {openshift-platform} web console, you must create and configure a `DataScienceCluster` object. 


[IMPORTANT]
====
The following procedure describes how to create and configure a `DataScienceCluster` object to install {productname-long} components as part of a _new_ installation. 

ifndef::disconnected[]
* For information about changing the installation status of {productname-short} components _after_ installation, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}/installing-and-deploying-openshift-ai_install#updating-installation-status-of-openshift-ai-components-using-web-console_component-install[Updating the installation status of Red Hat OpenShift AI components by using the web console].

////
* For information about _upgrading_ {productname-short}, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/upgrading_{url-productname-short}/index[Upgrading {productname-short} Self-Managed].
////
endif::[]

ifdef::disconnected[]
* For information about changing the installation status of {productname-short} components _after_ installation, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}_in_a_disconnected_environment/deploying-openshift-ai-in-a-disconnected-environment_install#updating-installation-status-of-openshift-ai-components-using-web-console_component-install[Updating the installation status of Red Hat OpenShift AI components by using the web console].

////
* For information about _upgrading_ {productname-short}, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/upgrading_{url-productname-short}_in_a_disconnected_environment/index[Upgrading {productname-short} Self-Managed in a disconnected environment].
////
endif::[]

====

.Prerequisites
ifdef::disconnected[]
* The {productname-long} Operator is installed on your {openshift-platform} cluster. See link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}_in_a_disconnected_environment/deploying-openshift-ai-in-a-disconnected-environment_install#installing-the-openshift-ai-operator_operator-install[Installing the {productname-long} Operator].
endif::[]
ifndef::disconnected[]
* The {productname-long} Operator is installed on your {openshift-platform} cluster. See link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}/installing-and-deploying-openshift-ai_install#installing-the-openshift-ai-operator_operator-install[Installing the {productname-long} Operator].
endif::[]


* You have cluster administrator privileges for your {openshift-platform} cluster.
* If you are using custom namespaces, you have created the namespaces.

.Procedure
. Log in to the {openshift-platform} web console as a cluster administrator.
. In the web console, click *Operators* → *Installed Operators* and then click the *{productname-long}* Operator.
. Click the *Data Science Cluster* tab.
. Click *Create DataScienceCluster*.
. For *Configure via*, select *YAML view*.
+
An embedded YAML editor opens showing a default custom resource (CR) for the `DataScienceCluster` object, similar to the following example:
+
[source, yaml, subs="attributes+"]
----
apiVersion: datasciencecluster.opendatahub.io/v2
kind: DataScienceCluster
metadata:
  name: default-dsc
spec:
  components:
    aipipelines:
      argoWorkflowsControllers:
        managementState: Removed <1>
      managementState: Removed
    dashboard:
      managementState: Removed
    feastoperator:
      managementState: Removed
    kserve:
      managementState: Removed
    kueue:
      defaultClusterQueueName: default
      defaultLocalQueueName: default
      managementState: Removed
    llamastackoperator:
      managementState: Removed
    mlflowoperator:
      managementState: Removed
    modelregistry:
      managementState: Removed
      registriesNamespace: {mr-default-namespace}
    ray:
      managementState: Removed
    trainingoperator:
      managementState: Removed
    trustyai:
      managementState: Removed
    workbenches:
      managementState: Removed
      workbenchNamespace: {workbench-default-namespace} <2>
----
+
<1> To use your own Argo Workflows instance with the `aipipelines` component, set `argoWorkflowsControllers.managementState` to `Removed`. You can then integrate with a managed Argo Workflows installation already on your {openshift-platform} cluster and avoid conflicts with the embedded controller. See _Configuring pipelines with your own Argo Workflows instance_.
<2> To use the predefined workbench namespace, set this value to `pass:attributes[{workbench-default-namespace}]` or omit this line. To use a custom workbench namespace, set this value to your namespace.


. In the `spec.components` section of the CR, for each {productname-short} component shown, set the value of the `managementState` field to either `Managed` or `Removed`. These values are defined as follows:
+
--
Managed::
The Operator actively manages the component, installs it, and tries to keep it active. The Operator will upgrade the component only if it is safe to do so.

Removed::
The Operator actively manages the component but does not install it. If the component is already installed, the Operator will try to remove it.
--
+
[IMPORTANT]
====
ifndef::disconnected[]
* To learn how to install the distributed workloads components, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}/installing-the-distributed-workloads-components_install[Installing the distributed workloads components].
endif::[]

ifdef::disconnected[]
* To learn how to install the distributed workloads components, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_{url-productname-short}_in_a_disconnected_environment/installing-the-distributed-workloads-components_install[Installing the distributed workloads components].
* To learn how to run distributed workloads in a disconnected environment, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_distributed_workloads/running-ray-based-distributed-workloads_distributed-workloads#running-distributed-data-science-workloads-disconnected-env_distributed-workloads[Running distributed data science workloads in a disconnected environment].
endif::[]

====

. Click *Create*.

.Verification
. Confirm the status of all installed components:

# Documentation Plan

**Project**: Workbenches MLflow SDK Support — zero-touch MLflow SDK configuration for RHOAI Workbench notebooks
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Ticket**: [RHOAIENG-45969](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-45969)

---

## Doc impact assessment

| Requirement | Grade | Rationale |
|-------------|-------|-----------|
| REQ-001: MLflow SDK zero-touch configuration | **High** | Major new feature — entirely new user-facing workflow for experiment tracking in Workbenches |
| REQ-002: opendatahub.io/mlflow-instance annotation | **High** | New annotation that triggers a new integration mechanism; core API surface for the feature |
| REQ-003: MLflow environment variables | **High** | New auto-injected environment variables that change how users interact with MLflow SDK |
| REQ-004: Automatic RBAC setup | **High** | New automatic RoleBinding creation; changes the RBAC workflow users previously followed |
| REQ-005: Validating webhook | **High** | New behavioral constraint with a specific error message users will encounter |
| REQ-006: K8s service account authentication | **High** | New zero-configuration authentication model replacing manual token management |
| REQ-007: params.env feature toggle | **Medium** | New configuration parameters for cluster administrators; enhancement to existing config surface |
| REQ-008: S3 artifact serving limitation | **Medium** | Known limitation affecting users who need custom artifact storage; no code evidence |

|-------------|----------------|-----------|-----------------|

| REQ-002 | **Grounded** (score 0.92) | params.env, ARCHITECTURE.md, Makefile | Full module specifications |

---

## What is the support status of the feature(s) being used to complete the user's JTBD (Job To Be Done)?

General Availability (GA) — RHOAI 3.4 stable release. Testing completed on RHOAI 3.4 nightly builds (confirmed 2026-04-06). The feature ships as GA with the 3.4 stable code freeze.

## Why is this content important?

Data scientists using RHOAI Workbenches currently face a multi-step, error-prone manual process to use MLflow for experiment tracking: they must discover and configure the MLflow tracking URI, obtain and configure service account tokens, and manually create RoleBindings. RHOAI 3.4 eliminates this friction with automatic, annotation-driven configuration. Without documentation, users cannot discover this capability, administrators cannot enable it, and both audiences lack the knowledge to troubleshoot issues such as the webhook-enforced annotation removal constraint. This documentation is critical for the RHOAI 3.4 release because leadership has mandated documentation readiness as a prerequisite for feature shipment.

## Who is the target persona(s)?

* Data Scientist: Primary user who runs MLflow experiment tracking code in RHOAI Workbenches. Needs to understand how to use the MLflow SDK with zero-touch configuration and how to work within the feature's constraints (annotation lifecycle, S3 limitations).
* IT Operations Leader / SysAdmin: Cluster administrator who enables the MLflow integration platform-wide via params.env configuration and manages the RHOAI operator. Needs to understand the two-level toggle architecture (cluster-wide feature flag + per-workbench annotation) and RBAC implications.

## What is the main JTBD? What user goal is being accomplished? What pain point is being avoided?

**Data Scientist job**: When I am developing ML models in an RHOAI Workbench and need to track experiments, I want to use the MLflow SDK immediately without configuring tracking URIs, authentication tokens, or RBAC permissions, so that I can focus on model development and experiment iteration rather than platform configuration.

**Administrator job**: When I am managing an RHOAI cluster and need to provide data scientists with MLflow experiment tracking capabilities, I want to enable MLflow integration through a single configuration toggle, so that I can ensure consistent, secure MLflow access across all workbenches without per-user RBAC setup.

Pain points avoided:
- Manual MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI discovery and configuration
- Manual service account token management for MLflow authentication
- Manual RoleBinding creation for each workbench
- Inconsistent configurations across workbenches leading to tracking failures
- Risk of broken state when removing MLflow from a running workbench

## How does the JTBD(s) relate to the overall real-world workflow for the user?

**Data Scientist workflow**: The MLflow integration sits at the experiment tracking phase of the ML lifecycle. After launching a Workbench with a notebook image, the data scientist writes model training code and needs to log parameters, metrics, and artifacts. Previously, this required a detour into platform configuration (finding URIs, setting up auth). With zero-touch configuration, the workflow proceeds directly from "launch Workbench" to "write experiment code" without interruption.

**Administrator workflow**: The MLflow enablement fits into the platform provisioning phase. After installing RHOAI and the MLflow operator, the administrator enables the integration cluster-wide. From that point, the Dashboard automatically annotates new workbenches with MLflow support. The administrator's ongoing responsibility is limited to monitoring (checking for MLflowClusterRolePending events) rather than per-user RBAC management.

## What high-level steps does the user need to take to accomplish the goal?

### Prerequisites
1. RHOAI 3.4 or later installed on the OpenShift cluster
2. MLflow operator installed and configured (mlflow-operator-mlflow-integration ClusterRole must exist)
3. MLflow component enabled in RHOAI (mlflow-enabled=true in params.env / odh-dashboard-config)
4. Workbench image with MLflow SDK pre-installed (standard in RHOAI 3.4 images)

### Administrator steps
1. Verify the MLflow operator is installed and the ClusterRole exists
2. Set `mlflow-enabled=true` in the notebook controller configuration (propagated via opendatahub operator)
3. Optionally set `gateway-url` if Gateway API auto-discovery is not suitable
4. Verify the Dashboard applies the `opendatahub.io/mlflow-instance` annotation to new workbenches

### Data Scientist steps
1. Create or update a Workbench with MLflow enabled (via Dashboard toggle or annotation)
2. Verify environment variables are injected (MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION, MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH)
3. Use the MLflow SDK in notebook code (mlflow.set_experiment, mlflow.start_run, mlflow.log_param, mlflow.log_metric)
4. To disable MLflow: stop the workbench first, then remove the annotation

## Is there a demo available or can one be created?

No public demo available. Testing was completed on RHOAI 3.4 nightly builds. The JIRA epic (RHOAIENG-45969) contains sample Python code for MLflow experiment tracking that can serve as a documentation example.

## Are there special considerations for disconnected environments?

Yes — the MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI is composed from the Gateway API hostname or the static `gateway-url` parameter. In disconnected environments, administrators must ensure the `gateway-url` parameter is configured with an accessible endpoint, as Gateway API auto-discovery may not resolve correctly. The Kubernetes service account token-based authentication does not require external network access.

## Who can provide information and answer questions?

* **Engineering SME**: Participant A (Andy Stoneberg) — primary developer of the MLflow integration in odh-notebook-controller; authored PR #751
* **Engineering Lead**: Participant B (Harshad Reddy Nalla) — led testing and coordination across Dashboard, Notebook Images, and operator teams
* **Program Management**: Participant C (Demethria Ramseur) — tracking documentation readiness for RHOAI 3.4 release
* **Documentation Contributor**: Participant D (Matteo Mortari) — authored draft documentation MR 2664 on internal GitLab

## Release Note needed?

Yes

Draft release note: Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4 introduces zero-touch MLflow SDK configuration for Workbenches. When MLflow integration is enabled, workbenches are automatically configured with the MLflow tracking URI, Kubernetes-based authentication, and the required RBAC permissions. Data scientists can use the MLflow Python SDK for experiment tracking immediately without manual configuration.

## Relationship analysis

All eight requirements relate to a single feature (MLflow-Workbench integration) delivered in one epic. The relationship structure is:

| Pair | Relationship | Notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| REQ-001 / REQ-002 | **Overlapping** | REQ-001 is the comprehensive overview; REQ-002 focuses on the annotation specifically. High consolidation opportunity. |
| REQ-001 / REQ-003 | **Overlapping** | REQ-003 (env vars) is a subset of REQ-001 (full integration). Consolidate into shared reference module. |
| REQ-001 / REQ-004 | **Complementary** | REQ-004 (RBAC) covers a distinct aspect of the integration described in REQ-001. Fold into the same assembly. |
| REQ-001 / REQ-005 | **Complementary** | REQ-005 (webhook constraint) is a behavioral aspect of the lifecycle described in REQ-001. |
| REQ-001 / REQ-006 | **Overlapping** | REQ-006 (K8s auth) is the authentication mechanism within REQ-001. High consolidation opportunity. |
| REQ-007 / REQ-001 | **Sequential** | REQ-007 (admin config) must be completed before REQ-001 (user workflow) is actionable. Separate persona. |
| REQ-008 / REQ-001 | **Complementary** | REQ-008 (S3 limitation) is a known limitation of the feature in REQ-001. |

### Theme clustering

| Theme | Summary | Requirements | Overlap risk | Recommended ownership |
|-------|---------|-------------|-------------|----------------------|
| **MLflow-Workbench integration (data scientist)** | End-to-end user workflow for using MLflow SDK in Workbenches with zero-touch configuration | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-005, REQ-006 | **High** | "Track experiments with MLflow in Workbenches" assembly |
| **MLflow platform configuration (admin)** | Cluster-level enablement and configuration of MLflow integration | REQ-004, REQ-007 | **Medium** | Admin procedure within "Enable MLflow integration" or existing install/configure assembly |
| **MLflow known limitations** | S3 artifact serving limitation and workaround | REQ-008 | **Low** | Known limitation note within the data scientist assembly, plus troubleshooting |

**Consolidation decision**: Requirements REQ-001 through REQ-006 describe different facets of the same feature. Rather than creating 18+ modules (3 per requirement), this plan consolidates them into a focused set organized by persona and job, reducing to 10 modules total. Each module traces back to its source requirements.

## JTBD hierarchy

### Category: Develop

**Main Job**: Track experiments with MLflow in Workbenches
- **Persona**: Data Scientist
- **Job statement**: When I am developing ML models in an RHOAI Workbench, I want the MLflow SDK to work immediately without manual configuration, so I can track experiment parameters, metrics, and artifacts and focus on model iteration rather than platform setup.

**User Stories**:
1. As a data scientist, I want to understand how the MLflow integration works (annotation, env vars, auth, RBAC) so I know what the platform does for me automatically.
2. As a data scientist, I want to enable MLflow on a workbench and run experiment tracking code so I can log parameters and metrics from my training runs.
3. As a data scientist, I want to disable MLflow integration on an existing workbench so I can reconfigure or remove it safely.
4. As a data scientist, I want a reference of all MLflow-related environment variables, annotations, and tracking URI rules so I can troubleshoot issues.

### Category: Configure

**Main Job**: Enable MLflow integration for RHOAI Workbenches
- **Persona**: IT Operations Leader / SysAdmin
- **Job statement**: When I am configuring an RHOAI cluster to support MLflow experiment tracking, I want to enable the integration through a cluster-wide toggle and understand the RBAC and webhook mechanisms, so I can provide data scientists with automatic MLflow access without per-user configuration.

**User Stories**:
1. As a cluster administrator, I want to understand the two-level toggle architecture (cluster flag + per-workbench annotation) and the automatic RBAC mechanism so I can plan the rollout.
2. As a cluster administrator, I want to enable MLflow integration cluster-wide by configuring params.env and verify the integration is working so data scientists can use it.
3. As a cluster administrator, I want a reference of configuration parameters, RBAC resources, and webhook behavior so I can troubleshoot platform-level issues.

@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+# Grants the controller SA the 'bind' verb on the 'mlflow-integration' ClusterRole.
+# This allows the controller to create RoleBindings referencing the mlflow-integration
+# ClusterRole without needing to hold all permissions that role grants.
+# Applied as a kustomize patch so it survives 'make manifests' regeneration.
+- op: add
+  path: /rules/-
+  value:
+    apiGroups: ["rbac.authorization.k8s.io"]
+    resources: ["clusterroles"]
+    verbs: ["bind"]
+    resourceNames: ["mlflow-operator-mlflow-integration"]

  "id": "REQ-001",
  "title": "Document MLflow SDK zero-touch configuration for Workbenches",
  "priority": "critical",
  "category": "new_feature",
  "sources": [
    {"label": "RHOAIENG-45969", "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-45969", "note": "Main epic: Workbenches MLFlow SDK Support - defines the zero-touch configuration goal, environment variables, annotation mechanism, and RBAC requirements"},
    {"label": "RHOAIENG-54379", "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-54379", "note": "Documentation task with acceptance criteria including sample Python code for MLflow experiment tracking"},
    {"label": "RHOAIENG-56218", "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-56218", "note": "CCS documentation story for MLflow-Workbench integration, targeting RHOAI 3.4 GA"},
    {"label": "PR #751", "url": "https://github.com/opendatahub-io/kubeflow/pull/751", "note": "Implementation PR adding notebook_mlflow.go, notebook_validating_webhook.go, RBAC patches, and mutating webhook integration"}
  ],
  "summary": "RHOAI 3.4 introduces zero-touch MLflow SDK configuration for Workbenches. When the MLflow operator is enabled in RHOAI and a Workbench is created (or updated) with the `opendatahub.io/mlflow-instance` annotation, the odh-notebook-controller automatically injects three environment variables (MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION, MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH) into the Workbench pod and creates a RoleBinding granting the Notebook ServiceAccount the mlflow-operator-mlflow-integration ClusterRole. This enables data scientists to use the MLflow Python SDK for experiment tracking immediately - without manually configuring server URLs, authentication tokens, or RBAC permissions. A validating webhook prevents removing the MLflow annotation from a running Workbench to avoid inconsistent state.",
  "user_impact": "Data scientists can launch a Workbench with MLflow enabled and immediately run MLflow SDK code (e.g., mlflow.set_experiment(), mlflow.log_metric()) without needing to configure tracking URIs, authentication, or RBAC permissions. Previously, users had to manually set MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, obtain and configure service account tokens, and ensure correct RoleBindings - all of which are now handled automatically by the platform.",
  "scope": "new",
  "documentation_actions": [
    {
      "action": "Create",
      "type": "CONCEPT",
      "description": "Explain how MLflow integration works with Workbenches, covering the annotation-driven mechanism, the automatic environment variable injection (MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI composed from Gateway hostname and instance name, MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION set to 'true', MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH set to 'kubernetes-namespaced'), the automatic RBAC setup (RoleBinding to mlflow-operator-mlflow-integration ClusterRole), the authentication flow via Kubernetes service account projected volumes, and the feature-flag gating via MLFLOW_ENABLED/mlflow-enabled in params.env",
      "note": null
    },
    {
      "action": "Create",
      "type": "PROCEDURE",
      "description": "Step-by-step procedure for using the MLflow SDK in a Workbench, including prerequisites (MLflow operator configured, mlflow-enabled=true in RHOAI config), creating/updating a Workbench with MLflow enabled via the Dashboard or by adding the opendatahub.io/mlflow-instance annotation, verifying the environment variables are injected, and running sample MLflow experiment tracking code. Include the constraint that the MLflow annotation cannot be removed from a running Workbench (must stop it first), and document the known limitation that custom S3 artifact serving requires manual configuration.",
      "note": null
    },
    {
      "action": "Create",
      "type": "REFERENCE",
      "description": "Reference table documenting the opendatahub.io/mlflow-instance annotation (valid values, behavior when absent/empty), the three injected environment variables (MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION, MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH) with their computed values and purpose, the mlflow-operator-mlflow-integration ClusterRole, the MLFLOW_ENABLED and GATEWAY_URL controller configuration parameters, and the tracking URI composition rules (default 'mlflow' instance vs custom instance name path segments)",
      "note": null
    }
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Users can identify the prerequisites for MLflow-Workbench integration (MLflow operator installed and configured, mlflow-enabled feature flag set to true)",
    "Users can create a Workbench with MLflow integration enabled and verify that MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION, and MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH environment variables are automatically set in the pod",
    "Users can execute the sample MLflow experiment tracking Python code (mlflow.set_experiment, mlflow.start_run, mlflow.log_param, mlflow.log_metric) in a Workbench without any manual SDK configuration",
    "Users understand that the opendatahub.io/mlflow-instance annotation triggers the integration and can describe valid annotation values ('mlflow' for default instance, custom names for multi-instance)",
    "Users understand how the MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI is composed (https://<gateway-hostname>/mlflow for default instance, https://<gateway-hostname>/mlflow-<name> for custom instances)",
    "Users understand that a RoleBinding is automatically created for the Notebook ServiceAccount granting access to MLflow resources via the mlflow-operator-mlflow-integration ClusterRole",
    "Users understand the constraint that the MLflow annotation cannot be removed from a running Workbench and know they must stop the Workbench first before disabling MLflow integration",
    "Users understand the known limitation that custom S3 artifact storage requires manual configuration within notebook cells due to Connection Types constraints"
  ],
  "references": [
    {"label": "RHOAIENG-45969 Description", "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-45969", "note": "Epic description with full implementation details, env var specifications, RBAC requirements, and acceptance criteria including sample Python code", "type": "jira"},
    {"label": "RHOAIENG-54379 Description", "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-54379", "note": "Documentation task with acceptance criteria and sample MLflow Python code", "type": "jira"},
    {"label": "RHOAIENG-56218 Description", "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-56218", "note": "CCS documentation story referencing RHAISTRAT-1161 for broader context", "type": "jira"},
    {"label": "RHOAIENG-45969 Comment #9 (2026-04-06)", "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-45969", "note": "Testing validation confirming: new workbenches get annotation and env vars automatically; old workbenches can be updated; annotation is reconciled on running notebooks; feature is gated by mlflowOperator enabled flag", "type": "jira"},

    {"label": "notebook_controller.go:498-513", "url": "https://github.com/opendatahub-io/kubeflow/blob/main/components/odh-notebook-controller/controllers/notebook_controller.go", "note": "Controller reconciliation loop - calls ReconcileMLflowIntegration for RoleBinding management when MLflowEnabled is true", "type": "code"},
    {"label": "config/base/params.env", "url": "https://github.com/opendatahub-io/kubeflow/blob/main/components/odh-notebook-controller/config/base/params.env", "note": "Feature toggle configuration: mlflow-enabled=false (default), gateway-url= (empty default)", "type": "code"},

    {"label": "main.go:210-255", "url": "https://github.com/opendatahub-io/kubeflow/blob/main/components/odh-notebook-controller/main.go", "note": "Startup initialization reading MLFLOW_ENABLED and GATEWAY_URL env vars, passing to both controller reconciler and webhooks", "type": "code"}

    "primary_language": "Go",
    "build_system": ["Makefile", "go.mod (per component)"],
    "major_directories": ["components/notebook-controller (upstream)", "components/odh-notebook-controller (ODH fork)"],
    "relevant_component": "components/odh-notebook-controller"
  },
  "notes": "1. Web search was unavailable during analysis; web_findings is empty. 2. Three Google Doc specifications (Tech Preview spec, Feature Refinement doc, Dev Preview Instructions) and the internal GitLab MR 2664 could not be accessed due to authentication requirements. The JIRA descriptions and PR diff provided sufficient detail for comprehensive analysis. 3. The MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH=kubernetes-namespaced env var is present in the code (notebook_mlflow.go) but not mentioned in the JIRA epic description, which only references MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI and MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION. Documentation should include all three env vars. 4. The feature is gated by mlflow-enabled in params.env (default: false) and the MLFLOW_ENABLED env var on the controller pod. When disabled, existing MLflow env vars on running pods are intentionally not cleaned up. 5. The tracking URI has two composition modes: (a) from GATEWAY_URL env var if configured, or (b) dynamically from the GatewayAPI Gateway instance hostname. Both need documentation for admin-facing configuration reference."

Removing this annotation while the notebook is running would create a broken state: the RoleBinding granting MLflow access is deleted immediately by the reconciler, but the MLflow environment variables (MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION, MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH) persist in the running pod until restart, leaving the MLflow SDK configured but unauthorized. Users must stop the notebook first (which sets the kubeflow-resource-stopped annotation), then remove the MLflow annotation.",

  },
  "notes": "This requirement is part of the broader MLflow GA integration (RHAISTRAT-1161) for RHOAI 3.4. The validating webhook is one component of a three-part system: (1) mutating webhook injects MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION=true, and MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH=kubernetes-namespaced env vars on notebook CREATE/UPDATE; (2) reconciler creates a namespace-scoped RoleBinding binding the notebook SA to the mlflow-operator-mlflow-integration ClusterRole; (3) validating webhook prevents annotation removal on running notebooks to avoid the broken state. The webhook uses failurePolicy=Fail, meaning if the webhook service is unavailable, notebook updates will be blocked. Testing was completed on RHOAI 3.4 nightly builds (comment from 2026-04-06). A documentation MR has already been contributed (GitLab MR 2664)."
}

{
  "id": "REQ-008",
  "title": "Document known limitation: S3 artifact serving not zero-touch",
  "priority": "medium",
  "category": "new_feature",
  "sources": [
    {"label": "RHOAIENG-45969", "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-45969", "note": "Parent epic for MLflow Workbench SDK support; contains the S3 artifact serving limitation description in the 'Implementation Details' section"}
  ],
  "summary": "The MLflow integration in RHOAI 3.4 provides zero-touch configuration for experiment tracking (tracking URI, authentication, RBAC) but does NOT automatically configure custom or external S3 storage for MLflow artifact serving. This is a platform-level limitation of the Connection Types feature in RHOAI: Connection Types inject credentials from Secrets as environment variables with statically-defined keys, so mounting more than one S3 connection on a workload causes a 'last one wins' collision. Users who need to store MLflow artifacts in a custom S3 bucket (separate from the default MLflow-managed storage) must manually configure S3 credentials within their notebook cells using Python code.",
  "user_impact": "Data scientists who want to use a custom or external S3 bucket for MLflow artifact storage cannot rely on the zero-touch integration and must manually set S3 credentials (such as AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL, and related environment variables) in their notebook code. This applies whenever a workbench would have more than one S3 connection. For users who only use the default MLflow artifact store, no additional action is needed.",
  "scope": "new",
  "documentation_actions": [
    {
      "action": "Create",
      "type": "CONCEPT",
      "description": "Document the known limitation that S3 artifact serving is not automatically configured as part of the MLflow zero-touch integration, explaining why (Connection Types inject S3 credentials as environment variables with static keys, making multiple S3 connections mutually exclusive) and clarifying that the default MLflow-managed artifact store works without manual configuration",
      "note": "This should be placed in or near the MLflow integration documentation as a 'Known limitations' or 'Important' admonition so users discover it in context"
    },
    {
      "action": "Create",
      "type": "PROCEDURE",
      "description": "Provide a workaround procedure showing how to manually configure S3 credentials within a Jupyter notebook cell for custom artifact storage, including example Python code to set boto3/MLflow S3 environment variables programmatically",
      "note": "The JIRA epic states 'Customer can write code within Jupyter cell to handle these shortcomings' -- the procedure should show a concrete example"
    }
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Users can identify from the documentation that custom S3 artifact storage is not automatically configured by the MLflow zero-touch integration",
    "Users can understand why multiple S3 connections cause a conflict (Connection Types static key collision)",
    "Users can follow a workaround procedure to manually configure S3 credentials in a notebook cell when they need custom artifact storage",
    "The documentation clearly states that the default MLflow artifact store works without manual S3 configuration",
    "The limitation is presented as a known limitation or important note within the MLflow integration documentation context"
  ],
  "references": [
    {
      "label": "RHOAIENG-45969 Description - S3 limitation paragraph",
      "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-45969",
      "note": "The epic description contains a dedicated paragraph under 'Implementation Details' explaining the S3 artifact serving limitation: 'There is another aspect to MLFlow + Workbench integration that is NOT being addressed as part of this Epic... Due to complexities (shortcomings) with the Connection Types feature in RHOAI, Workbenches is unable to achieve the zero-touch configuration goal if/when a Notebook would have > 1 S3 connection'",
      "type": "jira"
    },
    {
      "label": "RHOAIENG-45969 Description - Product guidance",
      "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-45969",
      "note": "Product guidance from epic: 'From a Product/TP standpoint - imho - we could claim that only MLFlow is supported for artifact serving in 3.4EA1. Customer can write code within Jupyter cell to handle these shortcomings.'",
      "type": "jira"
    },
    {
      "label": "PR #751 (notebook_mlflow.go)",
      "url": "https://github.com/opendatahub-io/kubeflow/pull/751",
      "note": "Implementation PR confirms no S3 artifact configuration code exists -- the controller only handles MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, MLFLOW_K8S_INTEGRATION, MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH env vars and RoleBinding creation",
      "type": "code"
    },
    {
      "label": "controllers/notebook_mlflow.go",
      "url": null,
      "note": "MLflow integration code handles only tracking URI, K8s integration flag, tracking auth, and RoleBinding -- no S3/artifact storage configuration is implemented, confirming the limitation",
      "type": "code"
    },
    {
      "label": "RHOAIENG-54379",
      "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-54379",
      "note": "Documentation tracking ticket for MLflow integration with workbenches -- this limitation should be included in that documentation effort",
      "type": "jira"
    },
    {
      "label": "RHOAIENG-56218",
      "url": "https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-56218",
      "note": "CCS documentation ticket for MLflow integration with Workbenches; MR 2664 contributed to GitLab for official RHOAI docs",
      "type": "jira"
    }
  ],
  "web_findings": [],
  "is_breaking_change": false,
  "deprecation_version": null,
  "notes": "This limitation is explicitly called out in the RHOAIENG-45969 epic description as an intentional scope exclusion for RHOAI 3.4. The root cause is architectural: RHOAI Connection Types inject S3 credentials as flat environment variables with static key names (e.g., AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID). When multiple S3 connections are mounted on the same workload, later mounts overwrite earlier ones ('last one wins'). Furthermore, Connection Types do not currently support mounting more than one instance of the same type on a single workload. This is described as needing a 'platform level' solution. The product recommendation for 3.4 GA is to state that only the default MLflow artifact store is supported out-of-the-box, and users requiring custom S3 storage must configure credentials manually in notebook code. No implementation evidence for S3 artifact configuration was found in the codebase, confirming this is a documentation-only known limitation."
}
