# Documentation Requirements

**Source**: Remove inline providers from Llama Stack distribution image
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Release/Sprint**: rhoai-3.5.EA1

## Summary

- Total requirements analyzed: 8
- New modules needed: 11
- Existing modules to update: 11
- Breaking changes requiring docs: 3

## Requirements by priority

### Critical

#### REQ-001: Remove inline provider toggle references from product documentation
- **Source**: [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374) | [RHAIENG-4639](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4639) | [PR #349](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349)
- **Summary**: The Llama Stack distribution image default runtime configuration (config.yaml) no longer includes inline provider definitions for inline::sentence-transformers, inline::milvus, and inline::faiss. The environment variable toggles (ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS, ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS, ENABLE_FAISS) that previously activated these providers have been removed. All product documentation referencing these inline provider toggles, the provider support table listing them as conditionally enabled, and any procedures that instruct users to enable them via environment variables must be updated to reflect that these providers are no longer part of the default configuration. The providers' dependencies remain in the image and can be used by supplying a custom config.yaml at runtime.
- **User impact**: Users who followed existing documentation to enable inline providers via environment variables (e.g., setting ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS or ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS) will find those toggles no longer work. Users must now supply a custom config.yaml at runtime to use these providers, or migrate to remote provider equivalents (remote::milvus, remote vLLM for embeddings). Documentation that still references the old toggles will mislead users.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `provider-support-table` (REFERENCE) Update the Llama Stack API provider support table to remove inline::sentence-transformers, inline::milvus, and inline::faiss from the list of conditionally enabled providers, or mark them as 'Dependency only - not in default config'. Remove references to the ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS, ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS, and ENABLE_FAISS environment variable toggles.
  - [ ] Update `rag-setup-procedures` (PROCEDURE) Update any RAG setup procedures, embedding configuration guides, or vector store setup instructions that reference inline providers or their environment variable toggles. Replace instructions to 'set ENABLE_FAISS' or 'set ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS' with guidance to either use remote provider equivalents or supply a custom config.yaml.
  - [ ] Create `inline-provider-deprecation-notice` (CONCEPT) Add a deprecation or migration notice explaining that inline providers are no longer part of the default Llama Stack runtime configuration in RHOAI 3.5 EA1. Explain the phased removal plan and direct users to remote provider alternatives.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can find no references to ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS, ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS, or ENABLE_FAISS environment variable toggles in the Llama Stack product documentation for RHOAI 3.5
  - [ ] Users can see that inline::sentence-transformers, inline::milvus, and inline::faiss are either removed from or clearly marked as 'Dependency only / not in default config' in the API provider support table
  - [ ] Users who need inline providers can find instructions for supplying a custom config.yaml at runtime as an alternative to the removed environment variable toggles
  - [ ] Users can find guidance directing them to remote provider alternatives (remote::milvus for vector storage, remote vLLM for embeddings) as the recommended production approach
  - [ ] Users can find a deprecation notice or release note explaining that inline providers are being phased out of the default distribution configuration
- **References**:
  - [RHAISTRAT-1374 - AC Phase 1](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374): Acceptance criteria: 'Documentation is updated to remove mention of inline provider toggles'
  - [RHAIENG-4639 - Provider support table](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html-single/working_with_llama_stack/index#llama_stack_api_provider_support): Existing documentation page with API provider support table that must be updated
  - [RHAIENG-5227](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-5227): Sibling ticket: Update RAG processes to reflect inline provider changes
  - [PR #349 - distribution/config.yaml](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349): Shows exact providers stripped and removal of ENABLE_* env var toggle pattern
  - [PostgreSQL recommended config](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag#using-postgresql-in-llama-stack_rag): Existing docs for PostgreSQL as recommended alternative

#### REQ-004: Update RAG documentation to reflect inline provider removal
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-5227](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-5227) | [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374)
- **Summary**: The Llama Stack distribution image default config.yaml no longer references inline providers (inline::sentence-transformers, inline::milvus, inline::faiss) as of RHOAI 3.5 EA1. Existing RAG documentation that instructs users to enable inline providers via environment variable toggles must be updated to direct users to remote provider alternatives (remote::milvus, remote::vllm for embeddings, remote::pgvector, remote::qdrant) or explain how to supply a custom config.yaml if inline providers are needed for development/experimentation.
- **User impact**: Users following existing RAG documentation will encounter errors because the environment variable toggles for inline providers no longer activate anything in the default config.yaml. Users must now either configure remote providers for production RAG workflows or supply a custom config.yaml at container startup to use the inline providers whose dependencies remain pre-installed.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `rag-procedures` (PROCEDURE) Update RAG setup and usage procedures to replace all references to inline provider toggles with instructions for configuring remote providers (remote::milvus for vector stores, remote::vllm or remote::openai for embeddings). Include the new recommended production pattern.
  - [ ] Update `provider-config-reference` (REFERENCE) Update the provider configuration reference to reflect that inline::sentence-transformers, inline::milvus, and inline::faiss are now 'dependency only' providers. Remove references to ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS, ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS, and ENABLE_FAISS toggles.
  - [ ] Create `production-provider-architecture` (CONCEPT) Add a conceptual explanation clarifying the production provider architecture: why remote providers are recommended for production RAG, what 'dependency only' means, and how the build.yaml/config.yaml split works.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can set up a complete RAG pipeline using only remote providers by following the updated procedures
  - [ ] No documentation references the ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS, ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS, or ENABLE_FAISS environment variable toggles as the way to enable providers
  - [ ] Users who need inline providers for development can find instructions for supplying a custom config.yaml at container startup
  - [ ] The provider reference table accurately reflects that inline::sentence-transformers, inline::milvus, and inline::faiss are 'dependency only'
  - [ ] Documentation explains that inline providers are not recommended for production and that remote providers should be used instead
  - [ ] The embedding model configuration documents the VLLM_EMBEDDING_URL, VLLM_EMBEDDING_API_TOKEN, and EMBEDDING_MODEL environment variables as the recommended embedding setup
- **References**:
  - [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374): Feature description with phased approach, acceptance criteria, and cross-team stakeholder list
  - [RHAIENG-5227](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-5227): CCS documentation story for RAG updates
  - [RHAIENG-5325](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-5325): Spike: Investigate docs impact of inline provider deprecation
  - [PR #349](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349): Implementation PR introducing build.yaml/config.yaml split
  - [RHOAI 3.4 RAG documentation](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag): Existing RAG documentation that needs updating

#### REQ-008: Release note for deprecated inline provider functionality
- **Source**: [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374)
- **Summary**: In RHOAI 3.5 EA1, three inline providers — inline::sentence-transformers, inline::milvus, and inline::faiss — are removed from the default Llama Stack runtime configuration (config.yaml). The provider dependencies remain installed in the container image, so users who need them can still enable them by supplying a custom config.yaml at runtime. Full dependency removal is planned for a future release (EA2 or 3.5 GA). A Deprecated Functionality release note is required.
- **User impact**: Users who relied on inline providers being available in the default Llama Stack configuration will find them absent after upgrading to RHOAI 3.5 EA1. While the providers can still be activated by passing a custom config.yaml at runtime, users must take explicit action to re-enable them. The environment variable toggles are replaced by a custom config.yaml workflow.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `deprecated-inline-providers-rn` (RELEASE_NOTE) Write a Deprecated Functionality release note entry for RHOAI 3.5 EA1 stating that inline::sentence-transformers, inline::milvus, and inline::faiss are removed from the default config.yaml. State that dependencies remain in the image for now but will be fully removed in a future release. Mention that inline::localfs is NOT affected.
  - [ ] Create `custom-config-workaround` (PROCEDURE) Provide brief instructions on how to supply a custom config.yaml at runtime to re-enable deprecated inline providers as a transitional workaround.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can find a Deprecated Functionality release note for RHOAI 3.5 EA1 that names all three deprecated inline providers
  - [ ] The release note explains that the providers are removed from the default config.yaml but their dependencies remain in the container image
  - [ ] The release note states that full dependency removal is planned for a future release
  - [ ] The release note describes or links to the custom config.yaml workaround
  - [ ] The release note identifies the recommended remote provider alternatives
  - [ ] The release note explicitly states that inline::localfs is NOT deprecated
  - [ ] The release note does not reference the old environment variable toggle mechanism as a current enablement method
- **References**:
  - [RHAISTRAT-1374 description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374): Phased removal plan
  - [RHAIENG-4636 description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4636): Docs epic scope: update API provider support table, prepare Deprecated Functionality RN
  - [RHAISTRAT-1528](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1528): Gen AI Studio changes deferred to 3.5 GA
  - [PR #349](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349): Implementation: build.yaml/config.yaml split

### High

#### REQ-002: Document build.yaml vs config.yaml split for provider configuration
- **Source**: [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374) | [PR #349](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349)
- **Summary**: The Llama Stack distribution introduces a build.yaml/config.yaml split to separate the full provider manifest (build.yaml) from the production runtime configuration (config.yaml). build.yaml is now the source of truth containing all provider definitions including inline providers. config.yaml is auto-generated by build.py with those inline providers stripped out. The dependencies for stripped providers remain pre-installed in the container image, allowing users who need them to supply a custom config.yaml at runtime.
- **User impact**: Users who previously relied on environment variable toggles to activate inline providers must now provide a custom config.yaml at container startup instead. The default runtime configuration no longer includes inline providers, so RAG workflows or embedding scenarios that depended on inline::faiss, inline::milvus, or inline::sentence-transformers require explicit custom configuration.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `build-config-yaml-architecture` (CONCEPT) Explain the build.yaml vs config.yaml architecture: build.yaml is the full provider manifest and source of truth; config.yaml is the auto-generated runtime config with dependency-only providers stripped.
  - [ ] Create `dependency-only-providers-procedure` (PROCEDURE) How to use dependency-only providers by passing a custom config.yaml at runtime. Include steps for extracting provider definitions from build.yaml, adding them to a custom config.yaml, and mounting/passing the file to the container.
  - [ ] Update `provider-reference-table` (REFERENCE) Update the provider reference table to reflect the new 'Dependency only' status. Remove references to the deprecated environment variable toggles.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can identify which providers are 'dependency-only' versus enabled by default in the provider reference table
  - [ ] Users can successfully activate a dependency-only provider by following the custom config.yaml procedure
  - [ ] Documentation no longer references the deprecated ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS, ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS, or ENABLE_FAISS environment variable toggles
  - [ ] Users understand that build.yaml is the full provider manifest and config.yaml is auto-generated for runtime use
  - [ ] Users running RAG workflows that previously used inline providers can find migration guidance
- **References**:
  - [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374): Feature ticket with phased plan and acceptance criteria
  - [PR #349](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349): Implementation: build.py generates config.yaml from build.yaml
  - [RHAIENG-4636](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4636): CCS docs epic
  - [RHAIENG-4667](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4667): Engineering ticket: Remove inline providers from LLS distro image runtime config
  - [RHOAI 3.4 Llama Stack docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html/working_with_llama_stack/): Current published docs that need updating

#### REQ-003: Document custom config.yaml for re-enabling inline providers
- **Source**: [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374) | [PR #349](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349)
- **Summary**: In RHOAI 3.5 EA1, the Llama Stack distribution image default config.yaml no longer includes inline providers, but their Python dependencies remain pre-installed in the container image. Users who need these inline providers for development, experimentation, or downstream integration can re-enable them by supplying a custom config.yaml at container runtime. This procedure must be documented.
- **User impact**: Users who previously relied on environment variable toggles to activate inline providers will find those toggles no longer work. They must now create a custom config.yaml containing the desired inline provider definitions and mount it at runtime. Without this procedure documented, users will be unable to use inline embedding, inline FAISS vector search, or inline Milvus in development or experimentation scenarios.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `custom-config-yaml-procedure` (PROCEDURE) Step-by-step procedure for re-enabling inline providers via a custom config.yaml, covering: identifying providers from build.yaml, creating a custom config.yaml, mounting it into the container, passing the custom config path to the entrypoint. Include a concrete example.
  - [ ] Create `dependency-only-providers-reference` (REFERENCE) Reference table listing each dependency-only provider, its API category, required config stanza, and caveats. Mark as Dev Preview/Tech Preview.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can identify which providers are dependency-only by consulting the documented reference
  - [ ] Users can create a valid custom config.yaml that includes inline::sentence-transformers by following the procedure
  - [ ] Users can create a valid custom config.yaml that includes inline::faiss by following the procedure
  - [ ] Users can create a valid custom config.yaml that includes inline::milvus and are warned about multi-worker incompatibility
  - [ ] Users can mount a custom config.yaml into the container and start the Llama Stack server using the documented command
  - [ ] The procedure states that dependency-only providers are Dev Preview/Tech Preview and not supported for production use
  - [ ] The procedure warns that custom config.yaml compatibility is not guaranteed across image updates
- **References**:
  - [RHAISTRAT-1374 AC Phase 1](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374): Acceptance criterion implies documenting the replacement mechanism
  - [PR #349 - README.md note](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349): Adds NOTE block explaining dependency-only providers and custom config.yaml
  - [PR #349 - distribution/build.yaml](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349): Complete provider manifest with config stanzas
  - [JIRA comment - Lightspeed Core dependency](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374): Lightspeed Core depends on inline::sentence-transformer and inline::faiss

#### REQ-005: Mark inline providers as Dev Preview/Tech Preview in documentation
- **Source**: [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374) | [RHOAIENG-59161](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-59161)
- **Summary**: In RHOAI 3.5 EA1, inline providers are removed from the default Llama Stack runtime config.yaml but their dependencies remain pre-installed. Documentation must clearly label all remaining inline provider references as Dev Preview/Tech Preview, mark them as 'dependency only', and warn that they are not suitable for production use. This is Phase 1 of a two-phase deprecation.
- **User impact**: Users who currently rely on inline providers will find these no longer active by default. They can still use them by providing a custom config.yaml at runtime, but documentation must make clear these are unsupported Dev Preview/Tech Preview capabilities. Users should plan to migrate to remote provider equivalents.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `provider-support-table-tp` (REFERENCE) Update the Llama Stack API and provider support table to mark inline providers as 'Dev Preview / Dependency only'. Add a column or annotation indicating support level (GA, Tech Preview, Dev Preview).
  - [ ] Create `deprecation-admonition` (CONCEPT) Add a deprecation notice explaining that inline providers are deprecated for production use, classified as Dev Preview/Tech Preview, and will be fully removed in a future release.
  - [ ] Update `inline-procedures-tp` (PROCEDURE) Update procedures that reference inline providers to use remote providers as the primary path, with inline providers mentioned only as a Dev Preview alternative.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can identify from the API provider support table which providers are GA, Tech Preview, and Dev Preview without ambiguity
  - [ ] Users understand that inline providers require custom config.yaml to enable
  - [ ] Users can follow documented steps to enable dependency-only inline providers for development/experimentation
  - [ ] Users can identify the remote provider alternative for each deprecated inline provider
  - [ ] No documentation page implies that inline providers are suitable for production deployments
  - [ ] The deprecated functionality release note clearly states the Phase 1 scope and warns about upcoming Phase 2
  - [ ] References to legacy environment variable toggles are removed or updated
- **References**:
  - [RHAISTRAT-1374 Phase 1 AC](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374): Phase 1 acceptance criteria
  - [PR #349 distribution README](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349): Shows new 'Dependency only' column and asterisk footnote
  - [RHOAIENG-59161](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-59161): Confirms Tech Preview classification
  - [RHAISTRAT-1528](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1528): Gen AI Studio changes deferred to 3.5 GA
  - [RHOAI 3.4 Llama Stack API provider table](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html-single/working_with_llama_stack/index#llama_stack_api_provider_support): Current documentation page that needs updating

#### REQ-006: Add deprecation notice for upcoming full removal of inline providers
- **Source**: [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374)
- **Summary**: In RHOAI 3.5 EA1, several inline providers are removed from the default Llama Stack runtime configuration, though their dependencies remain in the container image. Users who rely on these providers can still enable them via custom config.yaml. A deprecation notice must warn users that in a future release, the dependencies themselves will be removed entirely and a modularity mechanism will be provided.
- **User impact**: Users who previously relied on inline providers being available in the default configuration must now explicitly enable them. They should begin migrating to remote provider equivalents because the inline provider dependencies will be fully removed in a future release.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `provider-table-deprecated` (REFERENCE) Update the Llama Stack API provider support table to reflect that inline::milvus, inline::sentence-transformers, and inline::faiss are no longer in the default configuration. Mark as deprecated with future removal note. Note that inline::localfs is NOT being removed.
  - [ ] Create `deprecated-functionality-rn` (RELEASE_NOTE) Write a Deprecated Functionality release note entry for RHOAI 3.5 EA1. Include guidance on using custom config.yaml and migration to remote providers.
  - [ ] Update `existing-procedures-deprecated` (PROCEDURE) Update existing procedures that reference inline provider toggles with remote provider alternatives. Add brief procedure for custom config.yaml workaround.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] The provider support table accurately reflects that inline::milvus, inline::sentence-transformers, and inline::faiss are deprecated
  - [ ] The table confirms that inline::localfs is NOT removed
  - [ ] A Deprecated Functionality release note clearly states that inline provider dependencies will be fully removed in a future release
  - [ ] Users can find instructions for re-enabling inline providers via custom config.yaml
  - [ ] Users can identify remote provider alternatives
  - [ ] No documentation references inline provider toggles as a current/active feature
- **References**:
  - [RHAISTRAT-1374 Description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374): Full feature description with phased approach
  - [RHAIENG-4636 Description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4636): CCS documentation epic with scope change details
  - [RHAISTRAT-1528](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1528): Gen AI Studio changes deferred
  - [PR #349](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-distribution/pull/349): Implementation PR

#### REQ-007: Document remote provider alternatives for each removed inline provider
- **Source**: [RHAISTRAT-1374](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-1374) | [RHAIENG-4639](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4639)
- **Summary**: Three inline providers have been removed from the default Llama Stack distribution config.yaml. Documentation must map each removed inline provider to its production-ready remote equivalent: remote::vllm for embedding inference (replacing inline::sentence-transformers), remote::milvus (replacing inline::milvus), and remote::pgvector or remote::qdrant (replacing inline::faiss for vector storage).

Include environment variables (MILVUS_ENDPOINT, ENABLE_PGVECTOR, VLLM_EMBEDDING_URL).
- **Acceptance criteria**:

## Technical Review -- RHAISTRAT-1374: Llama Stack Provider Configuration Documentation

### File 1: inline-provider-deprecation-in-rhoai.adoc

**Doc type detected:** Concept (`:_module-type: CONCEPT`)
**Reviewer lens applied:** Architect
**Overall technical confidence:** HIGH -- All provider type strings, environment variable names, and architectural claims are confirmed by source code evidence.

#### Critical issues (must fix before publication)

None identified.

#### Significant issues (should fix)

1. **Location:** Line 56 -- "Environment variable toggles no longer function" section
   - **Issue:** The doc states that in previous releases, environment variables `ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS`, `ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS`, and `ENABLE_FAISS` could be set on the `LlamaStackDistribution` custom resource to enable inline providers. These env vars have no trace in the current codebase (confirmed by code-evidence scan verdict: `no_evidence_found` for all three). The doc does not specify which prior release introduced them or when exactly they were removed, making it difficult for a reader to assess whether their deployment was affected.
   - **Impact:** A reader running a pre-3.5 deployment cannot determine which prior release(s) supported these env vars to assess their migration scope.
   - **Suggestion:** Add a brief note indicating the version range in which these env vars were supported (e.g., "In {productname-short} 3.3 and 3.4"), or note "prior releases" if the exact version is unknown. SME should confirm the version range.

2. **Location:** Line 85 -- Remote alternatives table, `inline::faiss` row
   - **Issue:** The table lists `remote::pgvector` or `remote::qdrant` as alternatives to `inline::faiss`, but does not mention that pgvector requires the `ENABLE_PGVECTOR` env var and qdrant requires the `ENABLE_QDRANT` env var to activate. The `remote::vllm` and `remote::milvus` rows correctly mention their activation env vars (`VLLM_EMBEDDING_URL` and `MILVUS_ENDPOINT`), creating an inconsistency.
   - **Impact:** A reader attempting to migrate from `inline::faiss` to `remote::pgvector` or `remote::qdrant` will not know they need to set the activation env var and will find the provider does not start.
   - **Suggestion:** Add the activation env vars to the `inline::faiss` row description, consistent with the other rows. Source code confirms: pgvector activates with `ENABLE_PGVECTOR` (build.yaml line 98), qdrant activates with `ENABLE_QDRANT` (build.yaml line 109).

#### Minor issues (consider fixing)

1. **Location:** Line 7 -- Abstract
   - **Issue:** The abstract says "you can re-enable them by supplying a custom `config.yaml` at runtime" but does not link to the procedure. The links appear at the bottom in "Additional resources" but not inline at the point where re-enablement is mentioned.
   - **Impact:** Readers scanning the abstract may miss the path to the procedure.
   - **Suggestion:** Add an inline xref or callout pointing to the re-enablement procedure where it is first mentioned.

2. **Location:** Lines 33-35 -- "Why inline providers are removed" section
   - **Issue:** The multi-worker incompatibility bullet is specific to `inline::milvus` only but appears in a section framed as applying to all three inline providers. A reader might mistakenly conclude that `inline::faiss` and `inline::sentence-transformers` also have multi-worker issues.
   - **Impact:** Slight misattribution; minor but could affect a reader deciding whether to use `inline::faiss` in a multi-worker dev setup.
   - **Suggestion:** Prefix the bullet with "For `inline::milvus`:" to scope the statement.

#### SME verification needed

1. **Location:** Lines 58-60 -- Environment variable names
   - **Issue:** The env var names `ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS`, `ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS`, and `ENABLE_FAISS` have no trace in the current codebase. This is expected if they were removed as part of this deprecation, but SME should confirm the exact names match what was previously shipped.
   - **Why SME is needed:** These names cannot be verified from the current source repository; they existed in a prior release only.

2. **Location:** Line 56 -- `LlamaStackDistribution` custom resource
   - **Issue:** The CRD `LlamaStackDistribution` with apiVersion `llamastack.io/v1alpha1` is referenced but is part of the RHOAI operator, not the llama-stack-distribution repo. Cannot verify CRD name or apiVersion from the code evidence available.
   - **Why SME is needed:** CRD naming and API version must be confirmed against the RHOAI operator source.

#### Strengths

- The concept clearly explains the two-phase deprecation plan, which gives readers a concrete migration timeline.
- The distinction between "dependency-only" (libraries installed, config stripped) and "fully removed" (future Phase 2) is precise and avoids ambiguity.
- The note about `inline::localfs` not being affected is proactive and prevents reader confusion.
- All provider type strings (`inline::sentence-transformers`, `inline::milvus`, `inline::faiss`, `remote::vllm`, `remote::milvus`, `remote::pgvector`, `remote::qdrant`) are confirmed in source code.
- The `VLLM_EMBEDDING_URL` and `MILVUS_ENDPOINT` environment variables are confirmed in `distribution/config.yaml`.

**Reviewer lens applied:** Developer (accuracy) and Architect (completeness)
**Overall technical confidence:** HIGH -- All three YAML configuration stanzas are byte-for-byte confirmed against `build/build.yaml`. Provider type strings, db_path, persistence config, and namespace values all match.

None identified.

#### Significant issues (should fix)

1. **Location:** Line 46 -- "The following stanzas are sourced from the `build.yaml` provider manifest"
   - **Issue:** The sentence says the stanzas are "sourced from the `build.yaml` provider manifest" but does not tell the reader where to find `build.yaml`. A reader following this reference doc to re-enable providers needs to know the file is in the distribution source repository at `build/build.yaml`, or that they can extract the default `config.yaml` from the container image.
   - **Impact:** A reader may search for `build.yaml` inside their deployed container and not find it (it is not shipped in the container image; only `config.yaml` is copied into the image per the Containerfile).
   - **Suggestion:** Clarify that `build.yaml` is in the upstream source repository and is not present in the container image. Alternatively, point readers to the re-enablement procedure which shows how to extract the base `config.yaml`.

#### Minor issues (consider fixing)

1. **Location:** Lines 23-27 -- `inline::sentence-transformers` row, "Provider API" column
   - **Issue:** The Provider API is listed as "Inference (embeddings)". The generated `distribution/README.md` in the source repo lists it under the `inference` API without the "(embeddings)" qualifier. The concept doc (File 1, line 15) says "inference and embeddings". These three phrasings are slightly inconsistent.
   - **Impact:** A reader cross-referencing the docs may be unsure whether this provider handles general inference or only embeddings.
   - **Suggestion:** Align the terminology across all docs. Based on the `build.yaml` structure (the provider appears under the `inference` section), "Inference" is the API name. The "(embeddings)" qualifier is useful clarification but should be consistent across files.

2. **Location:** Lines 89-92 -- "Providers not affected" section
   - **Issue:** This section mentions `inline::localfs` and `inline::file-search` but does not mention other inline providers that remain in the default config (e.g., `inline::builtin` under responses, messages; `inline::pypdf` under file_processors; `inline::reference` under batches). A reader might wonder whether those are also at risk.
   - **Impact:** Low -- the section title says "not affected" which scopes it, but a completeness-minded reader may question the omission.
   - **Suggestion:** Consider adding a brief note that only the three providers listed in this document are classified as dependency-only; other inline providers (such as `inline::builtin` and `inline::pypdf`) remain in the default runtime configuration and are not affected.

#### SME verification needed

#!/bin/bash
# workflow-completion-check.sh
#
# Stop hook: blocks Claude from stopping while the ACTIVE workflow
# is still running. Only checks the workflow identified by the
# .active-workflow marker — stale workflows from other sessions
# are ignored.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 = allow stop
#   2 = block stop (reason sent to stderr)
#
# Requires: jq

set -u

INPUT=$(cat)

if ! cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Cannot access project directory; cannot verify workflow status." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Look for progress files
shopt -s nullglob
PROGRESS_FILES=(.agent_workspace/*/workflow/*.json)
shopt -u nullglob
if [ ${#PROGRESS_FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

MARKER=".agent_workspace/.active-workflow"

# No marker file → no active workflow → allow stop
if [ ! -f "$MARKER" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Read the marker — fail closed on parse errors
PROGRESS_FILE=$(jq -r '.progress_file // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_PF=$?
TICKET=$(jq -r '.ticket // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_TK=$?

if [ "$JQ_RC_PF" -ne 0 ] || [ "$JQ_RC_TK" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Failed to parse $MARKER; refusing to stop (fail closed)." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Marker parsed successfully but fields are empty → stale marker → clean up
if [ -z "$PROGRESS_FILE" ] || [ -z "$TICKET" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Progress file doesn't exist → stale marker → clean up and allow stop
if [ ! -f "$PROGRESS_FILE" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Check the workflow status — only block for in_progress workflows
WORKFLOW_STATUS=$(jq -r '.status' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ "$WORKFLOW_STATUS" != "in_progress" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

WORKFLOW_TYPE=$(jq -r '.workflow_type' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

# Anti-loop guard: per-workflow counter prevents infinite blocking
COUNTER_FILE="${PROGRESS_FILE}.stop_count"
if [ -f "$COUNTER_FILE" ]; then
  COUNT=$(cat "$COUNTER_FILE")
else
  COUNT=0
fi
if [ "$COUNT" -ge 5 ]; then
  rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Get step order from the progress file
mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.step_order[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#STEP_ORDER[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.steps | keys[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
fi

# Find the first incomplete step
NEXT_STEP=""
for step in "${STEP_ORDER[@]}"; do
  STEP_STATUS=$(jq -r --arg s "$step" '.steps[$s].status // "missing"' "$PROGRESS_FILE")
  case "$STEP_STATUS" in
    completed|skipped|deferred) continue ;;
    *) NEXT_STEP="$step"; break ;;
  esac
done

if [ -n "$NEXT_STEP" ]; then
  echo "$((COUNT + 1))" > "$COUNTER_FILE"
  echo "Documentation workflow '$WORKFLOW_TYPE' for $TICKET is not complete. Next step: $NEXT_STEP. Continue the workflow." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# All steps done — clean up and allow stop
rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
rm -f "$MARKER"
exit 0

[id="external-s3-provider-for-files-endpoint_{context}"]
= External S3-compatible provider for the /v1/files endpoint

[role="_abstract"]
The Llama Stack Files API supports two providers in {productname-short}: the default `inline::localfs` provider, which stores files on the local file system of the Llama Stack pod, and the `remote::s3` provider, which stores file content in an external S3-compatible object storage service. Use the `remote::s3` provider when you require scalable, durable storage for file content that is independent of the Llama Stack pod lifecycle, or when you must integrate with enterprise-managed storage platforms.

[IMPORTANT]
====
The external S3-compatible files provider is a Developer Preview feature. Developer Preview features are not intended for production use and are not officially tested. Red{nbsp}Hat does not provide support for Developer Preview features, but you can provide feedback and report issues. For more information about the support scope of Developer Preview features, see link:https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/devpreview/[Developer Preview Support Scope].
====

The `remote::s3` provider stores file content in an S3 bucket. File metadata, such as the file ID, filename, purpose, size, and timestamps, is stored in the PostgreSQL metadata store that Llama Stack requires in {productname-short}. The Files API metadata is managed automatically within the same PostgreSQL instance that holds metadata for the other Llama Stack APIs. No additional database configuration is required.

The provider works with any object storage system that exposes an S3-compatible API, including the following examples:

* Amazon S3
* MinIO
* Ceph Object Gateway (RGW)
* Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Object Storage, through the S3 Compatibility API

Because Llama Stack interacts with the storage system through the S3 API, any storage technology is compatible if it implements the S3 API.

*Benefits*

Using external S3-compatible storage for the `/v1/files` endpoint provides the following advantages:

* Reuse existing, approved object storage services and governance controls for file content.
* Scale file content storage independently of Llama Stack compute resources.
* Persist file content across Llama Stack pod restarts and rescheduling events.
* Centralize file content across multiple AI applications and clusters.
* Meet compliance requirements by integrating with enterprise-managed storage platforms.
* Integrate S3-backed files into retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows by attaching files to vector stores.

*Response schema differences from the upstream specification*

The `/v1/files` endpoint responses from the `remote::s3` provider differ from the upstream Llama Stack Pydantic model in the following ways:

* The `status` and `status_details` fields that are present in the upstream model are not included in responses from this provider.
* The `expires_at` field is returned as `null` in all responses rather than being omitted from the response body.

These differences do not affect client compatibility with the OpenAI `/v1/files` API.
Clients that rely on the `status` or `status_details` fields must account for their absence.

*Compatibility and constraints*

The `remote::s3` provider has the following compatibility characteristics and constraints:

* The provider is compatible with the OpenAI `/v1/files` API.
* The `inline::localfs` provider remains supported and requires no configuration changes for existing deployments.
* Migration from the `inline::localfs` provider to the `remote::s3` provider is not performed automatically. Files stored by one provider are not available through the other.
* The external storage system must implement a compatible S3 API. Provider-specific features that deviate from the S3 specification are not supported.
* The provider uses the same `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variables as the `remote::bedrock` inference provider. If you use both providers and require different credentials for each, use IAM roles for service accounts or a non-AWS S3-compatible backend.
* Some S3-compatible backends require additional client-side environment variables, such as checksum-handling settings. Consult the documentation for your S3-compatible backend for the configuration that it requires.
* If the provider fails to initialize, the Llama Stack pod enters `CrashLoopBackOff`.

## Recent comments (last 30 days)

### [Participant B] — 2026-05-12 20:52

Update: @Jiri Petrlik 

I tested the doc end-to-end against the rh-dev distribution image (Llama Stack 0.7.1+rhaiv.1) on a cluster, using MinIO as the S3 backend. The MR has been updated with corrections based on what I found. Here's a summary of what's now resolved versus what I'd still like you to look at.
Resolved from my testing (no action needed, but worth a sanity check during your pass):
- Item 1: ENABLE_S3="true" enables the provider. I didn't test other truthy values — please confirm whether "1" or "yes" also work.
- Item 2: AWS_DEFAULT_REGION is the correct variable (the run.yaml substitution uses ${env.AWS_DEFAULT_REGION:=us-east-1}). Please confirm whether AWS_REGION is also honored.
- Item 3: All documented env vars behave as expected with the provider enabled.
- Item 5: PostgreSQL metadata storage is confirmed. The resolved run.yaml in the pod logs shows metadata_store.backend: sql_default, which resolves to PostgreSQL on the rh-dev image. No customer-side database configuration is needed.
- Item 7 (service URL pattern): Confirmed across two instances — the operator names the service <distribution-name>-service. The doc now documents this convention.
- Item 9 (purpose): Confirmed "assistants" is valid. Also confirmed it's required — omitting it returns a 400. Please confirm during your testing which other values (batch, fine-tune, vision, user_data) are accepted.
- Item 10 (response schemas): I captured real responses for upload, list, retrieve metadata, retrieve content, and delete, and updated the doc to match. Two notable differences from the upstream Pydantic schema: status and status_details are not in the responses, and expires_at is returned as null rather than omitted.
Additional findings worth flagging:
- Bucket-missing failure mode is verified: if S3_BUCKET_NAME points at a bucket that doesn't exist and S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET is false, the Llama Stack pod enters CrashLoopBackOff with RuntimeError: S3 bucket '<name>' does not exist. Either create the bucket manually or set 'auto_create_bucket: true' in your configuration. The doc now documents this exact behavior.
- There's no explicit "provider registered" log line at startup — the resolved run.yaml config dump (which lists the s3 provider entry) is the actual observable signal. The doc's verification bullets have been updated to reflect this.
- Both Files providers (inline::localfs with provider_id: meta-reference-files, and remote::s3 with provider_id: s3) remain registered simultaneously when ENABLE_S3="true" is set. They share the same files_metadata PostgreSQL table. Not currently a customer-facing concern, but worth knowing.
Still open for you:
- Item 4 (IRSA on real AWS S3): I couldn't test this - no AWS account or IAM setup on the test cluster.
- Item 6 (credential sharing with remote::bedrock): I didn't have Bedrock configured alongside S3. Please confirm both providers read the same AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY env vars with no env-var-level scoping.
- Item 8 (external route access): I tested only in-cluster access via the service URL. Please confirm an external route works as documented.
- CA bundle / private CA TLS (not in the original list): The doc cross-references the existing "Configuring a CA bundle for Llama Stack" procedure on the assumption that the operator's tlsConfig.caBundle mechanism mounts a bundle that boto3 will pick up via the system trust store. I couldn't test this without an S3 endpoint using a private CA. If you have such an environment, please confirm the existing CA bundle procedure works for the remote::s3 provider.
- Support tier: the doc currently marks the provider as Technology Preview in the section 1.4 provider table. The provider source declares Developer Preview at one point. Please confirm the correct tier for the 3.4 GA release notes, or let me know who to ask

[id="configuring-external-s3-provider-for-files-endpoint_{context}"]
= Configure the external S3-compatible provider for the /v1/files endpoint

[role="_abstract"]
To use external S3-compatible object storage as the backend for the Llama Stack `/v1/files` endpoint, update your `LlamaStackDistribution` custom resource (CR) to enable the `remote::s3` provider and supply the required configuration through environment variables.

.Prerequisites

* You have deployed a Llama Stack server and configured a PostgreSQL database for Llama Stack metadata storage. For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/deploying-a-llama-stack-server[Deploying a Llama Stack server]. Metadata for the `remote::s3` provider is stored in this same PostgreSQL instance automatically.
* You have created a secret that contains your S3 credentials. For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/using-external-s3-compatible-storage-for-the-files-api_rag#creating-secrets-for-the-external-s3-compatible-files-provider_rag[Creating secrets for the external S3-compatible files provider].
* If your S3 endpoint uses a TLS certificate signed by a private certificate authority (CA), you have configured the Llama Stack server to trust that CA. For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag#configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack_rag[Configuring a CA bundle for Llama Stack]. The Llama Stack Operator injects the CA bundle into the pod file system through the `tlsConfig.caBundle` mechanism. The `boto3` library that the `remote::s3` provider uses reads this bundle automatically at the operating-system level. You do not need to set an additional SSL-related environment variable for the provider.
* You have the S3 configuration details including: the external S3 endpoint URL, the bucket name, and the region value.
* The S3 bucket exists. Bucket creation is the responsibility of a storage administrator. For development environments where automatic bucket creation is acceptable, see the optional `S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET` field in the configuration example.
* You have permission to edit custom resources in your project.

.Procedure

. Log in to the {productname-short} web console as a cluster administrator.

. From the *Project* list, select the project that contains your `LlamaStackDistribution` CR.

. Update your `LlamaStackDistribution` CR to enable the `remote::s3` files provider and reference the secret that you created.

.. Click *Home* -> *Search*.

.. From the *Resources* list, search for `LlamaStackDistribution` and select it. The cluster also exposes a `LlamaStackOperator` resource, which is an internal {productname-short} resource that is managed by the {productname-long} Operator. Do not select `LlamaStackOperator`.

.. From the list of `LlamaStackDistribution` instances, click the name of the instance that you want to update.

.. Click the *YAML* tab.

.. Update the resource to include the following fields, and then click *Save*:
+
[source,yaml,subs="+quotes"]
----
apiVersion: llamastack.io/v1alpha1
kind: LlamaStackDistribution
metadata:
  name: __<distribution_name>__ <1>
  namespace: __<project>__ <2>
spec:
  server:
    containerSpec:
      env:
        - name: ENABLE_S3 <3>
          value: "true"
        - name: S3_BUCKET_NAME <4>
          value: "__<bucket_name>__"
        - name: AWS_DEFAULT_REGION <5>
          value: "__<region>__"
        - name: S3_ENDPOINT_URL <6>
          value: "__<s3_endpoint_url>__"
        - name: S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET <7>
          value: "false"
        - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID <8>
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: s3-files-credentials
              key: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
        - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: s3-files-credentials
              key: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    name: llama-stack
    port: 8321
  distribution:
    name: rh-dev
----
<1> Specifies the name of the `LlamaStackDistribution` instance. Replace with the name of your existing distribution.
<2> Specifies the project namespace where the `LlamaStackDistribution` resource is deployed. Replace with your project name.
<3> Enables the `remote::s3` files provider.
<4> Specifies the name of the S3 bucket where files are stored. S3 bucket names must be globally unique.
<5> Specifies the region for the S3 bucket, for example, `us-east-1`. For non-AWS backends, set this value to match the region configuration of your backend, if it requires one. The default of `us-east-1` is appropriate for many S3-compatible backends, including MinIO.
<6> Optional: Specifies the S3 endpoint URL for S3-compatible backends other than AWS S3. Omit this field when you use AWS S3. Set this field for MinIO, Ceph Object Gateway, OCI Object Storage, or other S3-compatible backends.
<7> Optional: When set to `"true"`, allows the provider to create the bucket if it does not exist. Requires the `s3:CreateBucket` IAM permission. Leave unset or set to `"false"` in production environments.
<8> Specifies the S3 credentials, sourced from the secret that you created. Omit `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` if the Llama Stack service account uses an IAM role.

[NOTE]
====
For production deployments, {org-name} recommends authenticating to AWS S3 by using IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) rather than static access keys. When you use an IAM role, omit the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variables, and bind the IAM role to the service account used by the Llama Stack pod.
====

[NOTE]
====
The `remote::s3` provider reads the same `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variables as the `remote::bedrock` inference provider. If you have configured both providers and require different credentials for each, use IAM roles for service accounts or a non-AWS S3-compatible backend.
====

[IMPORTANT]
====
If the configured bucket does not exist and `S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET` is set to `false`, the Llama Stack pod enters `CrashLoopBackOff`.
The pod logs include the following error: `RuntimeError: S3 bucket '<bucket_name>' does not exist. Either create the bucket manually or set 'auto_create_bucket: true' in your configuration.`
For more troubleshooting guidance, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/using-external-s3-compatible-storage-for-the-files-api_rag#troubleshooting-external-s3-provider_rag[Troubleshooting the external S3-compatible files provider].
====

.Verification

* The Llama Stack pod restarts and reaches the `Running` state.
* The pod logs show the resolved Llama Stack configuration containing a Files provider entry with `provider_id: s3` and `provider_type: remote::s3`. You can also confirm provider registration by sending a `GET` request to the `/v1/providers` endpoint of the Llama Stack API and verifying that an entry with `"api": "files"` and `"provider_id": "s3"` is displayed in the response.
* File operations against the `/v1/files` endpoint complete successfully, confirming that Llama Stack can communicate with the S3-compatible backend. For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/using-external-s3-compatible-storage-for-the-files-api_rag#using-the-v1-files-endpoint-with-external-s3-compatible-storage_rag[Using the /v1/files endpoint with external S3-compatible storage].

[role="_additional-resources"]
.Additional resources

* link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/using-external-s3-compatible-storage-for-the-files-api_rag#environment-variables-for-external-s3-files-provider_rag[Environment variables for the external S3-compatible files provider]
* link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/using-external-s3-compatible-storage-for-the-files-api_rag#troubleshooting-external-s3-provider_rag[Troubleshooting the external S3-compatible files provider]

[id="environment-variables-for-external-s3-files-provider_{context}"]
= Environment variables for the external S3-compatible files provider

[role="_abstract"]
You can configure the `remote::s3` files provider by setting environment variables in the `LlamaStackDistribution` custom resource (CR).
The following table lists all environment variables that the provider recognizes, their default values, and whether each variable is required.
Variables that contain credentials must be stored in a Kubernetes secret and referenced by using `secretKeyRef` in the CR.

.Environment variables for the `remote::s3` files provider
[cols="2,1,1,1,1,3", options="header"]
|===
|Variable
|Type
|Default
|Required
|Sensitive
|Description

|`ENABLE_S3`
|String
|Not set (provider disabled)
|Yes
|No
|Enables the `remote::s3` files provider.
Set to `"true"` to enable the provider.

|`S3_BUCKET_NAME`
|String
|None
|Yes, when `ENABLE_S3` is `"true"`
|No
|Specifies the name of the S3 bucket where file content is stored.
S3 bucket names must be globally unique.
The bucket must exist before the provider starts, unless `S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET` is set to `"true"`.

|`S3_ENDPOINT_URL`
|String (URL)
|None
|No
|No
|Specifies the endpoint URL for S3-compatible backends other than AWS S3, for example, `\https://minio.example.com:9000`.
Omit this variable when you use AWS S3.
Set this variable for MinIO, Ceph Object Gateway, OCI Object Storage, or other S3-compatible backends.
For more information about endpoint URL formats, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag#overview-of-object-storage-endpoints_rag[Overview of object storage endpoints].

|`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`
|String
|`us-east-1` (via `run.yaml` substitution)
|No
|No
|Specifies the AWS region for the S3 bucket, for example, `us-east-1`.
For non-AWS backends, set this value to match the region configuration of your backend, if it requires one.
The default of `us-east-1` is appropriate for many S3-compatible backends, including MinIO.
The recognized variable is `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`. The `AWS_REGION` variable is not used by this provider.

|`S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET`
|String
|`"false"`
|No
|No
|When set to `"true"`, allows the provider to create the S3 bucket automatically at startup if the bucket does not exist.
Requires the `s3:CreateBucket` IAM permission.
{org-name} recommends pre-creating the bucket administratively rather than enabling automatic bucket creation in production environments.

|`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
|String
|None
|Conditional
|Yes
|Specifies the access key ID for the S3-compatible storage backend.
Required unless you use IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) for authentication.
Store this value in a Kubernetes secret.

|`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`
|String
|None
|Conditional
|Yes
|Specifies the secret access key for the S3-compatible storage backend.
Required unless you use IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) for authentication.
Store this value in a Kubernetes secret.
|===

[NOTE]
====
The `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variables are shared with the `remote::bedrock` inference provider.
If you use both the `remote::s3` files provider and the `remote::bedrock` inference provider, and you require different credentials for each, use IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) or a non-AWS S3-compatible backend.
====

[NOTE]
====
For production deployments, {org-name} recommends authenticating to AWS S3 by using IAM roles for service accounts (IRSA) rather than static access keys.
When you use an IAM role, omit the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variables, and bind the IAM role to the service account that the Llama Stack pod uses.
IRSA-based authentication has not been validated by {org-name} Quality Engineering for this provider.
====

.Additional resources

# Documentation Plan

**Project**: Document External S3-Compatible Provider Configuration for Llama Stack /v1/files Endpoint
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Ticket**: [RHAIENG-2388](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388)

## What is the support status of the feature(s) being used to complete the user's JTBD (Job To Be Done)?

Developer Preview. The `remote::s3` provider is listed as Developer Preview in the existing `llama-stack-providers-support.adoc` provider table and in the concept module abstract. There is a discrepancy with the documentation MR which marks Technology Preview at one point. **OPEN ITEM**: The support tier must be confirmed with product management before publication (see REQ-009).

## Why is this content important?

Enterprise customers using Red Hat OpenShift AI with Llama Stack need to store files in external S3-compatible object storage (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph) rather than the default local filesystem. Without comprehensive documentation, users cannot determine which environment variables are required versus optional, how to authenticate securely, how to configure private CA trust, or how to troubleshoot common failure modes such as the CrashLoopBackOff caused by a missing S3 bucket. This documentation enables users to configure, secure, verify, and use external S3 storage for the /v1/files API with confidence.

## Who is the target persona(s)?

* SysAdmin: Configures the LlamaStackDistribution custom resource, creates Kubernetes Secrets for S3 credentials, manages IAM policies, and handles CA bundle trust configuration on the OpenShift cluster.
* Developer: Consumes the /v1/files API to upload, retrieve, and delete files as part of RAG and document-processing workflows. Writes client code against the response schemas.

## What is the main JTBD? What user goal is being accomplished? What pain point is being avoided?

**SysAdmin job**: When I need to provide scalable, persistent file storage for Llama Stack AI workloads on my OpenShift cluster, I want to configure an external S3-compatible storage backend for the /v1/files endpoint, so that I can reuse existing enterprise object storage infrastructure, meet compliance requirements, and decouple storage from pod lifecycle, while avoiding misconfigured credentials that cause CrashLoopBackOff failures or SSL handshake errors against private endpoints.

**Developer job**: When I am building RAG or document-processing applications that use the Llama Stack /v1/files API backed by external S3 storage, I want tested API usage examples with accurate response schemas, so that I can integrate file operations into my application without reverse-engineering behavior from source code, while avoiding integration errors caused by undocumented schema deviations from the upstream OpenAI specification.

## How does the JTBD(s) relate to the overall real-world workflow for the user?

The external S3 provider configuration is part of the broader Llama Stack deployment and application development workflow on Red Hat OpenShift AI:

1. **Platform setup** (SysAdmin): The SysAdmin activates the Llama Stack Operator, deploys a Llama Stack server with PostgreSQL metadata storage, and configures inference providers. External S3 configuration is an extension of this deployment step.
2. **Storage configuration** (SysAdmin): After the base Llama Stack server is running, the SysAdmin creates S3 credential secrets, configures the LlamaStackDistribution CR with S3 environment variables, and optionally configures CA trust for private endpoints. This step enables the remote::s3 provider.
3. **Verification** (SysAdmin): The SysAdmin confirms the provider is registered by inspecting pod logs and running basic API health checks.
4. **Application development** (Developer): Once the SysAdmin confirms the S3 provider is operational, developers use the /v1/files API to upload, list, retrieve, and delete files as part of their RAG or document-processing pipelines.
5. **Ongoing operations** (SysAdmin): The SysAdmin manages credential rotation, monitors for bucket-related failures, and enforces least-privilege IAM policies.

## What high-level steps does the user need to take to accomplish the goal?

### SysAdmin steps

Prerequisites:
* Llama Stack server deployed with PostgreSQL metadata storage
* Access to an S3-compatible storage backend (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph, or other)
* S3 bucket created (or willingness to enable auto-creation for development)
* S3 access credentials (access key ID and secret access key) or IRSA role binding

Steps:
1. Create a Kubernetes Secret containing S3 credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY)
2. Update the LlamaStackDistribution CR to enable the remote::s3 provider (ENABLE_S3=true) and set required/optional environment variables
3. If using a private CA endpoint, configure the CA bundle via the operator's tlsConfig mechanism
4. Verify the provider is registered by inspecting the resolved run.yaml config dump in pod logs
5. Confirm file operations work by running a test upload

### Developer steps

Prerequisites:
* S3 provider configured and verified by SysAdmin
* Llama Stack API endpoint URL (in-cluster service or external route)
* API authentication token (if required)

Steps:
1. Set the LLAMA_STACK_URL and LLAMA_STACK_TOKEN environment variables
2. Upload files using POST /v1/files with the required purpose field
3. List, retrieve metadata, retrieve content, and delete files using the documented curl commands
4. Optionally associate uploaded files with a vector store for RAG workflows

## Is there a demo available or can one be created?

No demo is available. End-to-end testing was performed against Llama Stack 0.7.1+rhaiv.1 with MinIO (confirmed in RHAIENG-2388 Comment #8, 2026-05-12). The curl commands in the usage examples module serve as a practical walkthrough.

## Are there special considerations for disconnected environments?

Yes. The `remote::s3` provider entry in the provider support table indicates "Yes" for disconnected support, meaning the provider can function in disconnected environments as long as the S3-compatible endpoint is reachable within the disconnected network. However, AWS S3 is not usable in fully disconnected environments. On-premises S3-compatible backends such as MinIO and Ceph are the expected targets for disconnected deployments.

## Who can provide information and answer questions?

* PM / Technical SME: Contacts extracted from RHAIENG-2388 and RHAISTRAT-283 (assignee, reporter, and watchers on those tickets). The QE reviewer who approved in Comment #9 (2026-05-14) is also a contact.
* Open questions:
  - Support tier confirmation (Technology Preview vs Developer Preview) -- route to product management
  - IRSA authentication validation -- route to QE or engineering
  - Bedrock credential sharing validation -- route to engineering

## Release Note needed?

Yes.

Draft release note: You can now configure an external S3-compatible storage provider for the Llama Stack /v1/files endpoint in Red Hat OpenShift AI. This enables file upload, storage, and retrieval using enterprise object storage backends such as AWS S3, MinIO, and Ceph Object Gateway, instead of the default local filesystem provider. The feature is available as Developer Preview.

## Links to existing content

* Existing assembly: `assemblies/using-external-s3-compatible-storage-for-the-files-api.adoc` (already includes 6 modules)
* Existing concept: `modules/about-using-external-s3-compatible-providers-for-the-files-endpoint.adoc`
* Existing procedure (configuration): `modules/configuring-external-s3-compatible-providers-for-the-files-endpoint.adoc`
* Existing procedure (secrets): `modules/creating-secrets-for-the-external-s3-compatible-files-provider.adoc`
* Existing procedure (usage): `modules/using-the-v1-files-endpoint-with-external-s3-compatible-storage.adoc`
* Existing reference (IAM policy): `modules/about-the-iam-policy-for-external-s3-compatible-files-providers.adoc`
* Existing reference (limitations): `modules/limitations-of-external-s3-compatible-files-providers.adoc`
* Existing reference (provider table): `modules/llama-stack-providers-support.adoc`
* Existing procedure (self-signed certs): `modules/accessing-s3-compatible-object-storage-with-self-signed-certificates.adoc`
* Existing concept (object storage endpoints): `modules/overview-of-object-storage-endpoints.adoc`
* Parent assembly: `assemblies/llama-stack-adv-examples.adoc` (includes the S3 assembly)
* Book entry point: `self-managed-working-with-llama-stack/master.adoc`

---

| REQ-002: S3 provider configuration | Critical | Primary configuration procedure; users cannot enable the feature without this |
| REQ-003: Authentication and secrets | Critical | Credential misconfiguration causes pod failures; two auth paths must be documented |
| REQ-004: SSL/TLS and CA bundle | High | Enterprise customers with private CAs cannot connect without this guidance |
| REQ-005: /v1/files API usage examples | High | Users need copy-paste curl commands and response examples to use the API |
| REQ-006: Bucket auto-creation and errors | Medium | Missing bucket is the most common failure mode; troubleshooting guidance is essential |
| REQ-007: Response schema documentation | Medium | Schema deviations from upstream cause client integration errors |
| REQ-008: Security considerations | High | Enterprise customers require actionable security guidance for compliance |
| REQ-009: Provider table update | Medium | Users need to find the provider in the support table with the correct tier |
| REQ-010: Verification and troubleshooting | High | No explicit provider-registered log line; users need guidance to confirm success |

## Code evidence status

All 10 requirements are grounded (code evidence found in the documentation repository). The existing documentation repository already contains a substantial draft of the S3 provider documentation, organized as an assembly with 6 included modules. The evidence indicates that MR !2697 has already been drafted and is under review.

# Documentation Requirements

**Source**: Document External S3-Compatible Provider Configuration for Llama Stack /v1/files Endpoint
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Release/Sprint**: rhoai-3.5.EA1

## Summary

- Total requirements analyzed: 10
- New modules needed: 20
- Existing modules to update: 4
- Breaking changes requiring docs: 0

## Requirements by priority

### Critical

#### REQ-002: S3 provider configuration in LlamaStackDistribution
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-2388](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388) | [RHAISTRAT-283](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-283) | [MR !2697](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2697)
- **Summary**: Llama Stack on Red Hat OpenShift AI now supports an external S3-compatible storage provider for the /v1/files endpoint, enabled via the ENABLE_S3 environment variable on the LlamaStackDistribution container. Configuration requires documenting all environment variables (ENABLE_S3, S3_BUCKET_NAME, S3_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY), their defaults and interactions, and network-level options such as proxy settings and custom CA bundles for private S3 endpoints.
- **User impact**: Users who want to store files in external S3-compatible storage rather than local filesystem storage must configure multiple environment variables on their LlamaStackDistribution custom resource. Without this documentation, users cannot determine which variables are required versus optional, what defaults apply (e.g., AWS_DEFAULT_REGION defaults to us-east-1), or how to set up non-AWS endpoints using S3_ENDPOINT_URL.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `PROCEDURE` — Step-by-step procedure for configuring the external S3-compatible provider on a LlamaStackDistribution, covering: enabling the provider (ENABLE_S3), setting required variables (S3_BUCKET_NAME), configuring optional variables (S3_ENDPOINT_URL for non-AWS, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET), and specifying network options (proxy, timeout). Must include a complete LlamaStackDistribution YAML example with environment variable configuration.
  - [ ] Create `REFERENCE` — Environment variable reference table for the S3 provider listing each variable (ENABLE_S3, S3_BUCKET_NAME, S3_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY), its type, default value, required/optional status, and description. Must note that AWS_DEFAULT_REGION (not AWS_REGION) is the correct variable, with default us-east-1 sourced from run.yaml substitution.
  - [ ] Create `CONCEPT` — Brief conceptual explanation of how the external S3 provider (remote::s3) fits into the LlamaStackDistribution architecture: it coexists with the inline::localfs provider, uses the existing PostgreSQL metadata store, and requires no additional database configuration. (May be combined with the overview requirement REQ-001 at planner discretion.)
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can identify all environment variables needed to enable and configure the external S3 provider on a LlamaStackDistribution custom resource
  - [ ] Users can determine which variables are required (ENABLE_S3, S3_BUCKET_NAME) versus optional (S3_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, S3_AUTO_CREATE_BUCKET) and what defaults apply
  - [ ] Users can configure S3_ENDPOINT_URL to point to a non-AWS S3-compatible endpoint (e.g., MinIO, Ceph)
  - [ ] Users can set AWS_DEFAULT_REGION correctly, understanding it is the recognized variable (not AWS_REGION) with a default of us-east-1
  - [ ] Users can apply the documented LlamaStackDistribution YAML example to their own cluster and have the S3 provider enabled successfully
  - [ ] Users understand that enabling S3 does not disable the inline::localfs provider and that both providers share the PostgreSQL metadata store
  - [ ] Users can configure network options (proxy, timeout) for enterprise environments with restricted network access
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-2388 Scope Section 2](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388): Defines configuration documentation scope: endpoint URL, region, bucket name, SSL/TLS, authentication, network options
  - [RHAISTRAT-283 Requirement 1](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-283): External S3 Configuration: extend Llama Stack configuration to support external S3 endpoints, regions, and custom domains
  - [RHAISTRAT-283 Requirement 4](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-283): Network Configuration: support proxy settings, custom CA certificates, and network timeouts for enterprise environments
  - [RHAIENG-2388 Comment #7 (2026-05-12)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388): QE review request enumerating all env vars, confirms run.yaml substitution pattern ${env.AWS_DEFAULT_REGION:=us-east-1}
  - [RHAIENG-2388 Comment #8 (2026-05-12)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388): End-to-end test results against Llama Stack 0.7.1+rhaiv.1 with MinIO
  - [RHAIENG-2388 Comment #9 (2026-05-14)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388): QE approval; IRSA and Bedrock not yet tested

#### REQ-003: S3 provider authentication and secrets management
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-2388](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388) | [RHAISTRAT-283](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-283)
- **Summary**: Llama Stack on Red Hat OpenShift AI now supports configuring an external S3-compatible storage provider (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph, or any S3-compatible system) for the /v1/files endpoint. Users must understand two authentication paths: (1) explicit access key/secret key credentials injected as environment variables via Kubernetes Secrets (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY), and (2) IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) where credentials are omitted and the Llama Stack service account uses a bound IAM role.
- **User impact**: Enterprise customers configuring external S3 storage for Llama Stack file management must correctly provision authentication credentials. Misconfigured secrets cause pod CrashLoopBackOff failures. Users on AWS who want to avoid static credentials need guidance on IRSA setup. Users running both S3 and Bedrock providers need to understand that AWS credentials are shared at the environment-variable level with no scoping mechanism.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `PROCEDURE` — How to configure authentication for the external S3 provider on Llama Stack, covering two methods: (1) Creating a Kubernetes Secret containing AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and injecting them as environment variables, and (2) Configuring IRSA-based authentication by omitting static credentials and annotating the Llama Stack service account with an IAM role ARN. (IRSA path was not tested by either the doc author or QE.)
  - [ ] Create `REFERENCE` — Reference table of all environment variables consumed by the remote::s3 provider with security classification
  - [ ] Create `CONCEPT` — Security considerations for S3 provider authentication: least-privilege bucket policies, encryption in transit, shared-credential model between remote::s3 and remote::bedrock providers
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can create a Kubernetes Secret containing S3 access credentials and inject them into a LlamaStackDistribution deployment
  - [ ] Users can identify which environment variables are required versus optional for S3 authentication
  - [ ] Users understand that AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are shared between the remote::s3 and remote::bedrock providers with no env-var-level scoping
  - [ ] Users can verify the S3 provider is registered by checking the resolved run.yaml config dump in pod logs
  - [ ] The documentation explains IRSA-based authentication as an alternative to static credentials
  - [ ] Users can diagnose a CrashLoopBackOff caused by a missing S3 bucket
  - [ ] The documentation notes whether IRSA has been validated in the current release or is based on upstream design patterns
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-2388 Scope item 3](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388): Access key/secret key management, IAM-based auth, encryption in transit
  - [RHAISTRAT-283 Requirements](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-283): Multi-provider authentication (access keys, IAM roles, STS tokens, service accounts)
  - [RHAIENG-2388 Comments](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388): QE confirmed IRSA and Bedrock credential sharing not tested

### High

#### REQ-001: External S3-compatible provider overview and introduction
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-2388](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388) | [RHAISTRAT-283](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-283) | [MR !2697](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2697)
- **Summary**: Llama Stack in Red Hat OpenShift AI now supports configuring an external S3-compatible storage provider (remote::s3) for the /v1/files endpoint, extending beyond the built-in inline::localfs provider. This enables enterprise customers to use any S3-compatible object storage backend (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph, or others) for file ingestion, retrieval, and management in RAG and document processing workflows while maintaining OpenAI API compatibility.
- **User impact**: Users who need to integrate existing S3-compatible storage infrastructure with Llama Stack AI workflows can now do so via a standardized provider. This overview section is the entry point that helps users understand what external S3 support offers, which backends are compatible, and whether this feature addresses their enterprise storage needs.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `CONCEPT` — New overview section explaining the purpose of external S3-compatible provider support for the /v1/files endpoint, covering: what the remote::s3 provider is, which S3-compatible backends are supported (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph), enterprise benefits, and OpenAI API compatibility
  - [ ] Update `REFERENCE` — Add the remote::s3 provider entry to the existing provider support table (section 1.4) with the correct support tier designation. (Support tier requires clarification: MR marks Technology Preview but provider source declares Developer Preview.)
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can read the overview section and understand the purpose of external S3-compatible provider support
  - [ ] The overview clearly states that any S3-compatible backend works and does not imply provider-specific logic
  - [ ] Users can identify enterprise benefits: leveraging existing storage, meeting compliance requirements, scaling storage independently
  - [ ] The overview explains the relationship between remote::s3 and inline::localfs providers
  - [ ] The overview states that the /v1/files endpoint maintains OpenAI API compatibility regardless of backend
  - [ ] The provider support table includes the remote::s3 provider with a clearly stated support tier
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-2388 Scope Item 1](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388): Defines the overview section scope
  - [RHAISTRAT-283 Feature Overview](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-283): Strategic rationale, goals, background context
  - [RHAISTRAT-283 Out of Scope](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-283): Excludes non-S3 providers, cross-region replication, custom permission management, multi-provider sync, migration tools

- **Source**: [RHAIENG-2388](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-2388) | [RHAISTRAT-283](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-283) | [MR !2697](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2697)

  - [ ] Create `PROCEDURE` — Troubleshooting guidance for bucket-missing CrashLoopBackOff (RuntimeError: S3 bucket '<name>' does not exist)
  - [ ] Create `CONCEPT` — Bucket lifecycle and prerequisites for the external S3 provider
- **Acceptance criteria**:

  - [ ] Users can follow troubleshooting steps for missing-bucket CrashLoopBackOff
