#### REQ-004: ConfigMap options documentation (odh-trusted-ca-bundle and dedicated)
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-4485](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485)
- **Summary**: Users need documentation explaining the two ConfigMap-based approaches for supplying CA certificates to a LlamaStackDistribution CR: (1) reusing the operator-managed odh-trusted-ca-bundle ConfigMap that is auto-detected in the CR's namespace, and (2) creating a dedicated ConfigMap referenced via spec.server.tlsConfig.caBundle fields including cross-namespace support via configMapNamespace. The procedure must include a 'You have the following options' lead-in that mirrors the existing section 8.5.2 pattern, with cross-links to sections 8.3 (Adding certificates to a cluster-wide CA bundle) and 8.4 (Adding certificates to a custom CA bundle) to guide users through prerequisite ConfigMap creation.
- **User impact**: Users configuring LlamaStackDistribution to connect to external LLM providers with self-signed or private CA certificates must understand which ConfigMap approach suits their environment. Without this documentation, users cannot determine whether to leverage the existing cluster trust infrastructure (odh-trusted-ca-bundle) or create a purpose-built ConfigMap, and they may not know about cross-namespace ConfigMap referencing.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `proc_configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Include a 'You have the following options' lead-in section within this procedure module that documents the two ConfigMap approaches: (1) odh-trusted-ca-bundle auto-detection and (2) dedicated ConfigMap with explicit spec.server.tlsConfig.caBundle fields. Each option needs a sub-procedure with YAML examples. Cross-link to sections 8.3 and 8.4 as prerequisites for ConfigMap creation.
  - [ ] Create `ref_ca-bundle-configmap-fields.adoc (discrete subsection within the procedure module)` (REFERENCE) Document the tlsConfig.caBundle spec fields (configMapName, configMapNamespace, configMapKeys) as a discrete reference sub-section at the end of the procedure module, including validation constraints (MaxItems=50, key pattern regex, MaxLength=253 per key). Also document the odh-trusted-ca-bundle auto-detection behavior and its three management states (Managed, Unmanaged, Removed).
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can identify which ConfigMap approach (odh-trusted-ca-bundle vs dedicated) is appropriate for their environment based on documented decision criteria
  - [ ] Users can configure a LlamaStackDistribution CR to use the odh-trusted-ca-bundle ConfigMap by verifying the ConfigMap exists in the CR's namespace (auto-detected, no explicit spec field needed)
  - [ ] Users can configure a LlamaStackDistribution CR to reference a dedicated ConfigMap using spec.server.tlsConfig.caBundle.configMapName with a valid YAML example
  - [ ] Users can reference a ConfigMap in a different namespace using spec.server.tlsConfig.caBundle.configMapNamespace and understand the default behavior (same namespace as the CR)
  - [ ] Users can specify multiple keys within a ConfigMap using spec.server.tlsConfig.caBundle.configMapKeys and understand the concatenation behavior
  - [ ] The procedure cross-links to section 8.3 (Adding certificates to a cluster-wide CA bundle) for users who need to add certs to the cluster-wide bundle that feeds odh-trusted-ca-bundle
  - [ ] The procedure cross-links to section 8.4 (Adding certificates to a custom CA bundle) for users who need to create a custom CA bundle via DSCInitialization
  - [ ] The 'You have the following options' lead-in mirrors the structural pattern used in section 8.5.2 (Configuring a certificate for pipelines)
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-4485 Description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485): Acceptance criteria specify the two ConfigMap options, cross-links to 8.3/8.4, and the 8.5.2 structural pattern
  - [api/v1alpha1/llamastackdistribution_types.go](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-k8s-operator/blob/main/api/v1alpha1/llamastackdistribution_types.go): Go type definitions for CABundleConfig (configMapName, configMapNamespace, configMapKeys) and TLSConfig structs with kubebuilder validation annotations
  - [controllers/ogxserver_controller.go -- gatherCABundleData](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-k8s-operator/blob/main/controllers/ogxserver_controller.go): Implements dual-source CA gathering: gatherExplicitCABundle (user-specified ConfigMaps) and gatherODHCABundle (auto-detected odh-trusted-ca-bundle). Certificates from both sources are concatenated into a single managed ConfigMap.
  - [controllers/ogxserver_controller.go -- detectODHTrustedCABundle](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-k8s-operator/blob/main/controllers/ogxserver_controller.go): Auto-detects the odh-trusted-ca-bundle ConfigMap in the CR's namespace, extracts all data keys, and feeds them into the certificate collector. Non-fatal if not found.
  - [controllers/ogxserver_controller.go -- reconcileManagedCABundleConfigMap](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-k8s-operator/blob/main/controllers/ogxserver_controller.go): Creates/updates the <instance-name>-ca-bundle managed ConfigMap with owner references. Uses patch-based updates to avoid race conditions.
  - [controllers/resource_helper.go -- addCABundleVolumeMount](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/llama-stack-k8s-operator/blob/main/controllers/resource_helper.go): Mounts the managed CA bundle ConfigMap read-only at /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle/ and sets SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle/ca-bundle.crt
  - [Section 8.3 -- Adding certificates to a cluster-wide CA bundle](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed/working-with-certificates_certs): Cross-link target: explains how to add certificates to the cluster-wide CA bundle, which are injected into odh-trusted-ca-bundle by the Cluster Network Operator
  - [Section 8.4 -- Adding certificates to a custom CA bundle](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed/working-with-certificates_certs): Cross-link target: explains how to add certificates via DSCInitialization customCABundle field, which also populates odh-trusted-ca-bundle
  - [LlamaStack Kubernetes Operator API Reference](https://llama-stack-k8s-operator.pages.dev/reference/api/): Public API documentation for CABundleConfig, TLSConfig, and UserConfigSpec fields

#### REQ-003: Troubleshooting reference for CA bundle configuration
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-4567](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4567) | [RHAIENG-4485](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485)
- **Summary**: A new troubleshooting reference module must be created to help users diagnose and resolve common issues when configuring custom CA bundles for the LlamaStackDistribution custom resource. The module covers failure scenarios including missing ConfigMaps, invalid PEM certificate format, operator permission problems, unparseable X.509 certificates, and pod restart behavior after ConfigMap updates. This is a companion to the main CA bundle configuration procedure (REQ-001) and addresses the need for users working in enterprise environments with self-signed certificates or private CAs to quickly resolve configuration issues.
- **User impact**: Users configuring custom CA bundles for Llama Stack to connect to external LLM providers with self-signed certificates will be able to self-diagnose and resolve common configuration failures without filing support tickets. Without this module, users encountering cryptic TLS errors or silent pod failures have no Red Hat-specific guidance to follow.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `ref_troubleshooting-ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc` (REFERENCE) New troubleshooting reference module. Should use a two-column table or symptom/cause/resolution format. Each entry covers one failure scenario with the error message, root cause, and resolution steps using oc commands. Place in the Installing and uninstalling book, as a companion to the CA bundle procedure at section 8.5.x, or as a dedicated troubleshooting entry.
  - [ ] Update `proc_configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Add a cross-reference (xref) from the main CA bundle procedure module to the new troubleshooting reference module, so users can navigate to troubleshooting guidance from the procedure page.
  - [ ] Update `assembly or master.adoc for the Installing and uninstalling book` (ASSEMBLY) Include the new troubleshooting reference module in the book's TOC, likely as a subsection of the Working with certificates chapter or as a standalone troubleshooting section.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can identify the cause of a 'ConfigMap not found' error when the specified CA bundle ConfigMap does not exist in the target namespace and follow resolution steps to create or correct it
  - [ ] Users can diagnose and resolve 'invalid PEM format' errors by verifying their certificate file contains valid PEM-encoded data with correct BEGIN/END markers
  - [ ] Users can identify operator permission problems preventing the Llama Stack Operator from reading or creating the managed CA bundle ConfigMap, and follow steps to verify RBAC configuration
  - [ ] Users can understand pod restart behavior after ConfigMap updates, including when pods automatically pick up new certificates and when manual restart is required
  - [ ] Users can diagnose unparseable or corrupted X.509 certificate errors using oc commands to inspect the ConfigMap contents and validate certificate data
  - [ ] Users can identify issues with missing certificate keys in the ConfigMap (e.g., wrong data key name) and correct the ConfigMap structure
  - [ ] Each troubleshooting entry includes: symptom description, example error message or observable behavior, root cause explanation, and step-by-step resolution using oc commands where appropriate
  - [ ] The troubleshooting module cross-links back to the main CA bundle configuration procedure (proc_configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc) and to sections 8.3 and 8.4 for cluster-wide and custom CA bundle setup
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-4567 description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4567): Defines the six troubleshooting scenarios to cover: missing certificate/ConfigMap key, operator permissions, invalid PEM format, ConfigMap not found, pod restart behavior, unparseable X.509 certs
  - [RHAIENG-4567 acceptance criteria](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4567): AC: new reference module, common issues with error messages and resolutions, oc command examples
  - [RHAIENG-4485 description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485): Parent ticket defining the full CA bundle feature: ConfigMap approaches (odh-trusted-ca-bundle vs. dedicated), configMapNamespace for cross-namespace references, operator validation/lifecycle, pod mount architecture
  - [RHAIENG-4485 out-of-scope note](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485): Parent ticket explicitly noted standalone troubleshooting module as out of scope for REQ-001, stating it could be added later — RHAIENG-4567 fulfills this need
  - [GitLab MR #2691](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2691): Referenced in RHAIENG-4485 comments as the documentation MR that was peer reviewed and merged. May contain the implemented troubleshooting content.

#### REQ-005: Operator validation and lifecycle behavior reference
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-4485](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485)
- **Summary**: The Llama Stack Operator implements validation, certificate concatenation, managed ConfigMap lifecycle management, and pod volume mount behavior when users configure custom CA bundles via the LlamaStackDistribution CR's spec.server.tlsConfig.caBundle field. This reference content documents the operator's internal processing pipeline — from validating the source ConfigMap and its keys, through concatenating multiple PEM certificates into a single bundle file, to creating and maintaining a managed <instance-name>-ca-bundle ConfigMap and mounting it into the Llama Stack server pod. Users need this reference to understand what the operator does behind the scenes, how it responds to configuration changes, and what constraints (such as the 50-key maximum for configMapKeys) apply.
- **User impact**: Users configuring CA bundles for Llama Stack need to understand the operator's validation rules (e.g., the configMapKeys MaxItems: 50 constraint), concatenation behavior (all keys merged into one bundle file), managed ConfigMap naming convention (<instance-name>-ca-bundle), automatic pod restart on ConfigMap changes, and status phase transitions (Pending, Initializing, Ready, Failed, Terminating) to diagnose configuration issues and understand the propagation pipeline from source ConfigMap to running pod.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `ref_llama-stack-operator-ca-bundle-behavior.adoc` (REFERENCE) Discrete reference sub-sections within the main procedure module (proc_configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc) documenting: (1) CABundleConfig field reference (configMapName, configMapNamespace, configMapKeys with MaxItems:50 validation), (2) certificate concatenation behavior (all keys concatenated into single bundle file in order), (3) managed ConfigMap lifecycle (<instance-name>-ca-bundle creation, updates on source change, deletion on CR removal), (4) pod mount architecture (volume mount path, read-only mount), (5) status phase transitions (Pending, Initializing, Ready, Failed, Terminating) and how CA bundle errors surface in status
  - [ ] Update `proc_configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc` (PROCEDURE) The reference sub-sections from REQ-005 are appended as [discrete] sub-sections at the end of the procedure module, per the acceptance criteria specifying 'discrete sub-sections at the end for the field reference and validation limits'
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can identify the three CABundleConfig fields (configMapName, configMapNamespace, configMapKeys) and their validation constraints from the reference sub-section
  - [ ] Users can determine the maximum number of configMapKeys allowed (50) from the reference content
  - [ ] Users can understand how the operator concatenates certificates from multiple keys into a single bundle file
  - [ ] Users can identify the naming convention for the managed ConfigMap (<instance-name>-ca-bundle) created by the operator
  - [ ] Users can determine what happens when the source ConfigMap is updated (operator reconciles and triggers pod restart)
  - [ ] Users can identify the LlamaStackDistribution status phases (Pending, Initializing, Ready, Failed, Terminating) and understand how CA bundle validation errors surface in the status
  - [ ] Users can locate the pod mount path where the concatenated CA bundle file is made available to the Llama Stack server container
  - [ ] The reference sub-sections use [discrete] AsciiDoc headings at the end of the procedure module, consistent with the structural pattern specified in the acceptance criteria
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-4485 Description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485): Acceptance criteria define the scope: 'High-level architecture: source ConfigMap -> operator -> managed <instance-name>-ca-bundle ConfigMap -> pod mount' and '[discrete] sub-sections at the end for the field reference and validation limits'
  - [RHAIENG-4485 Comments](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485): Comments confirm the work was peer reviewed and merged; references GitLab MR 2691
  - [LlamaStack K8s Operator API Reference](https://llama-stack-k8s-operator.pages.dev/reference/api/): Authoritative API reference for CABundleConfig type: configMapName (string), configMapNamespace (string, defaults to CR namespace), configMapKeys (string array, MaxItems: 50). Documents that 'All certificates from these keys will be concatenated into a single CA bundle file'
  - [LlamaStack K8s Operator Overview](https://llama-stack-k8s-operator.pages.dev/): Documents that ConfigMap changes trigger automatic pod restarts and that the reconciler uses a declarative approach ensuring actual state matches desired state

#### REQ-006: Verification steps for CA bundle configuration
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-4485](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485)
- **Summary**: Users need documented verification steps to confirm that a custom CA bundle has been correctly applied to a LlamaStackDistribution CR and that the Llama Stack server pod can establish trusted TLS connections to external LLM providers. The verification steps should cover checking the managed ConfigMap creation, confirming certificates are mounted in the pod, validating operator status conditions, and optionally testing end-to-end connectivity to the external provider.
- **User impact**: Without verification steps, users who configure CA bundles have no documented way to confirm their configuration is correct, leading to trial-and-error debugging when TLS connections to external LLM providers fail. These steps give users confidence that their certificate chain is complete and operational.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `proc_configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Add a 'Verification' sub-section within the procedure module. The verification steps are part of the single procedure module specified by RHAIENG-4485, not a standalone module. Include verification commands inline after the procedure steps, following the same pattern used in section 8.5.2 (Configuring a certificate for pipelines).
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can verify that the operator created the managed <instance-name>-ca-bundle ConfigMap in the CR namespace using an oc get configmap command
  - [ ] Users can verify that the managed ConfigMap contains their expected CA certificates by inspecting the ConfigMap data keys
  - [ ] Users can verify that the Llama Stack server pod has the CA bundle mounted at the expected path by exec-ing into the pod and running cat on the mount path
  - [ ] Users can check the LlamaStackDistribution CR status conditions or phase to confirm the CR reached Ready state after CA bundle configuration
  - [ ] Users can verify end-to-end TLS connectivity from the Llama Stack server to the external LLM provider endpoint (e.g., by checking server logs for successful provider connections or by sending a test inference request)
  - [ ] The verification sub-section follows the structural pattern established by section 8.5.2 (Configuring a certificate for pipelines), using oc and kubectl commands consistent with OpenShift AI documentation conventions
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-4485 Scope](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485): Scope section explicitly includes 'Verification steps for users'
  - [RHAIENG-4485 Architecture](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-4485): High-level architecture: source ConfigMap -> operator -> managed <instance-name>-ca-bundle ConfigMap -> pod mount
  - [LlamaStack Operator API Reference](https://llama-stack-k8s-operator.pages.dev/reference/api/): CRD spec defines spec.server.tlsConfig.caBundle with configMapName, configMapNamespace, configMapKeys fields; status has conditions array and phase enum (Pending, Initializing, Ready, Failed, Terminating)
  - [OpenShift AI 3.4 Working with certificates](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed/working-with-certificates_certs): Chapter 8 contains the peer sections (8.5.1-8.5.4) whose verification patterns (oc get configmap, pod terminal inspection) should be followed for consistency
  - [GitLab MR #2691 (merged)](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2691): Implementation MR referenced in JIRA comments; peer-reviewed and merged. ## Technical Review -- RHAIENG-4485: Document CA bundle configuration for LlamaStackDistribution

**Doc type detected:** Assembly (working-with-certificates.adoc, llama-stack-adv-examples.adoc) containing Concept, Procedure, Reference, and Reference (troubleshooting) modules
**Reviewer lens applied:** Both (Developer for procedures/references, Architect for concepts/assembly coherence)
**Overall technical confidence:** MEDIUM -- The documentation is technically sound in its description of operator behavior, YAML schemas, and verification steps. The docs-worktree versions represent substantial improvements over the code-repo versions, fixing broken cross-references, adding actionable troubleshooting commands, and correcting placeholder formatting. However, there are broken anchor links in the code-repo that need fixing before merge, the troubleshooting module inclusion in the assembly needs scope confirmation against the JIRA ticket, specific operator limits and API claims need SME verification, and the `openssl x509` troubleshooting command has a known limitation with multi-certificate bundles.

---

### Critical issues (must fix before publication)

**C1. Broken anchor link in code-repo procedure module (double hyphen typo)**

- **Location:** `modules/configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc`, line 15 (code-repo, non-disconnected conditional)
- **Issue:** The cross-reference anchor contains a double hyphen typo: `#ca-bundle-configuration--for-llama-stack_certs` (note `--` between "configuration" and "for"). The actual anchor ID in `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc` is `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack_{context}` with a single hyphen. This link will resolve to a broken anchor in the published output.
- **Impact:** Readers clicking the link to the reference module from the procedure will land on a broken anchor or the top of the page, unable to find the alternative configuration patterns.
- **Suggestion:** Fix the code-repo link to `#ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack_certs`. The docs-worktree version has already corrected this.

**C2. Inconsistent cross-reference anchor between concept and reference modules in code-repo**

- **Location:** `modules/about-ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc`, lines 39 and 42 (code-repo)
- **Issue:** The code-repo concept module links to `#ca-bundle-configuration-reference-for-llama-stack_certs` with the word "reference" in the anchor. The actual reference module ID is `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack_{context}` -- no "reference" in the ID. The docs-worktree version corrects this to `#ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack_certs`, which matches the actual module ID. Additionally, the link text says "CA bundle configuration reference for Llama Stack" while the target module title is "CA bundle configuration for Llama Stack" -- these should be reconciled.
- **Impact:** In the code-repo, the link from the concept module to the reference module is broken. Readers following the cross-reference will not reach the intended content.
- **Suggestion:** Confirm the docs-worktree correction. The anchor target must match `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack_{context}`.

**C3. Missing troubleshooting module in code-repo assembly**

- **Location:** `assemblies/working-with-certificates.adoc` (code-repo), between lines 67 and 69
- **Issue:** The docs-worktree version includes `include::modules/troubleshooting-custom-ca-bundles.adoc[leveloffset=+2]` at line 69 after the CA bundle reference module. The code-repo version jumps directly from `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc` to `managing-certificates-without-the-operator.adoc`, omitting the troubleshooting module entirely.
- **Impact:** The troubleshooting content is not wired into the published assembly. Users who encounter CA bundle validation errors have no documented resolution path within the chapter.
- **Suggestion:** Note that the JIRA ticket states a standalone troubleshooting module is "out of scope" and "can be added later if needed." The docs-worktree version adds it anyway. Clarify scope with the author -- if the troubleshooting module is intended for this release, add the include to the code-repo assembly.

---

### Significant issues (should fix)

**S1. Missing RBAC command block for cross-namespace references in code-repo**

- **Location:** `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc`, "Referencing a config map in a different namespace" section
- **Issue:** The code-repo version states that cross-namespace references "require that the Llama Stack Operator service account has read access to the source config map" but provides no commands to grant that access. The docs-worktree version correctly includes `oc get serviceaccounts`, `oc create role`, and `oc create rolebinding` commands with proper placeholder values (lines 86-104).
- **Impact:** Users attempting cross-namespace ConfigMap references will encounter "permission denied" errors with no clear path to resolution from this module.
- **Suggestion:** Ensure the RBAC command block from the docs-worktree version is included in the published output. This is an essential operational step for the cross-namespace pattern.

**S2. Code-repo troubleshooting module lacks actionable commands**

- **Location:** `modules/troubleshooting-custom-ca-bundles.adoc` (code-repo vs. docs-worktree comparison)
- **Issue:** The code-repo version has minimal one-line descriptions for common issues (e.g., "Certificate not found:: Ensure the ConfigMap exists and contains the specified key.") with no verification commands. The docs-worktree significantly improves this by adding `oc get configmap`, `oc auth can-i`, `openssl x509`, `oc get llamastackdistribution`, and `oc rollout restart` commands with proper placeholder formatting. The code-repo version also uses a hardcoded value `my-ca-bundle` in the "CA bundle key not found" resolution instead of a placeholder.
- **Impact:** In the code-repo version, readers with troubleshooting issues receive guidance too abstract to act on. The hardcoded `my-ca-bundle` may be copied literally.
- **Suggestion:** Publish the docs-worktree version's improvements. Replace `my-ca-bundle` with `__<configmap-name>__`.

**S3. Procedure YAML example uses hardcoded values in code-repo instead of placeholders**

- **Location:** `configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc`, lines 71-77 (code-repo)
- **Issue:** The code-repo uses hardcoded `name: my-llamastack` and `namespace: my-llamastack-namespace` in the procedure YAML example without `subs="+quotes"` on the source block. The docs-worktree correctly uses `__<instance-name>__` and `__<namespace>__` placeholders with `[source,yaml,subs="+quotes"]`, rendering them as clearly user-replaceable italic placeholders.
- **Impact:** Readers may copy `my-llamastack` and `my-llamastack-namespace` literally, or may be uncertain whether these are example values or required names.
- **Suggestion:** Use the docs-worktree approach with placeholders and `subs="+quotes"`.

**S4. Code-repo procedure uses AsciiDoc callouts despite repo conventions prohibiting them**

- **Location:** `configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc`, lines 87-93 (code-repo); `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc`, lines 51-53 and 76-80 (code-repo)
- **Issue:** The code-repo uses AsciiDoc callouts (`<1>`, `<2>`) to explain YAML fields. The repository's CLAUDE.md explicitly states "Do not use AsciiDoc callouts" and prescribes definition lists or "where:" blocks. The docs-worktree versions correctly use definition lists with "Where:" introduction.
- **Impact:** Non-compliance with the repository's documented code example conventions.
- **Suggestion:** The docs-worktree's definition list approach is correct per the project style guide.

**S5. Prerequisite about adding CAs should be qualified for the recommended pattern only**

- **Location:** `configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc`, lines 28-33 (code-repo)
- **Issue:** The code-repo states unconditionally: "You have added the required CAs to the cluster-wide CA bundle or to a custom CA bundle." This prerequisite only applies if the user is following the recommended `odh-trusted-ca-bundle` pattern. If using a dedicated ConfigMap, they do not need to add CAs to the cluster-wide or custom bundle first. The docs-worktree qualifies: "If you are using the `odh-trusted-ca-bundle` config map (the recommended pattern), you have added the required CAs..."
- **Impact:** Users choosing the dedicated ConfigMap path may perform unnecessary prerequisite steps.
- **Suggestion:** Use the docs-worktree's qualified prerequisite.

**S6. ConfigMap size limit unit inconsistency (1 MiB vs 1 MB)**

- **Location:** `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc`, limits section (line 108 in code-repo, line 133 in docs-worktree)
- **Issue:** The code-repo states "The standard 1 MB Kubernetes config map size limit" while the docs-worktree correctly states "The standard 1 MiB Kubernetes config map size limit." The official Kubernetes documentation specifies the limit as 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes), not 1 MB (1,000,000 bytes). The docs-worktree also adds useful context: "In practice, a bundle from a single source config map cannot reach 10 MB because of the 1 MiB config map limit."
- **Impact:** Using "1 MB" is technically imprecise and inconsistent with Kubernetes documentation.
- **Suggestion:** Use "1 MiB" consistently to match the Kubernetes documentation. Include the docs-worktree's clarifying note about why 10 MB is unreachable in practice.

**S7. `openssl x509 -text -noout` only validates the first certificate in a bundle**

- **Location:** `troubleshooting-custom-ca-bundles.adoc` (docs-worktree), lines 49-57 ("Invalid certificate" section) and lines 98-105 ("Invalid CA bundle format" section)
- **Issue:** The `openssl x509 -text -noout -in <certificate_file>` command only processes the first PEM block in a file. If the user has a multi-certificate bundle file (which is the expected case for CA bundles), this command silently ignores all certificates after the first. A user could have a valid first certificate but corrupted subsequent certificates and the validation would still pass.
- **Impact:** Users may get a false positive validation result, concluding their bundle is valid when only the first certificate was checked.
- **Suggestion:** Add a note that this command validates only the first certificate in a bundle. For bundles with multiple certificates, suggest `openssl storeutl -noout -text <bundle_file>` (OpenSSL 1.1.1+) or provide the `openssl crl2pkcs7 -nocrl -certfile <bundle_file> | openssl pkcs7 -print_certs -text -noout` pipeline as an alternative.

---

### Minor issues (consider fixing)

**M1. `subfields` incorrectly formatted with backticks in code-repo reference module**

- **Location:** `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc`, lines 7 and 11 (code-repo)
- **Issue:** The code-repo wraps "subfields" in backticks (`` `subfields` ``) in the abstract and section intro. "Subfields" is a descriptive English word here, not a code element or field name. The docs-worktree correctly renders it without backticks.
- **Impact:** Readers may misinterpret "subfields" as a literal API element name.
- **Suggestion:** Use the docs-worktree's plain-text version.

**M2. Docs-worktree procedure adds useful fallback verification note for containers without curl**

- **Location:** `configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc`, lines 167-168 (docs-worktree)
- **Issue:** The docs-worktree adds a NOTE about alternative verification if `curl` is not available in the container, suggesting checking server logs or running `python3 -c "import httpx; ..."`. The code-repo lacks this.
- **Impact:** Readers whose container images lack `curl` (which is common with minimal base images) will have no verification path for the final TLS connectivity test.
- **Suggestion:** Retain the docs-worktree's fallback note.

**M3. Inconsistent `:_mod-docs-content-type:` vs `:_module-type:` attribute usage**

- **Location:** `modules/troubleshooting-custom-ca-bundles.adoc`, line 1 (code-repo uses `:_module-type:`, docs-worktree uses `:_mod-docs-content-type:`); `assemblies/working-with-certificates.adoc` and `assemblies/llama-stack-adv-examples.adoc`, line 1 (both use `:_module-type:`)
- **Issue:** The project conventions specify `:_mod-docs-content-type:` for content type attributes. The assembly files and code-repo troubleshooting module use the older `:_module-type:` attribute.
- **Impact:** Tooling that relies on `:_mod-docs-content-type:` for module type detection may not correctly identify these files.
- **Suggestion:** Standardize on `:_mod-docs-content-type:` across all modules.

**M4. Docs-worktree llama-stack-adv-examples assembly omits content present in code-repo**

- **Location:** `assemblies/llama-stack-adv-examples.adoc` (docs-worktree vs. code-repo)
- **Issue:** The code-repo includes a bullet "Using external object storage for files" and a corresponding `include::` for `using-external-s3-compatible-storage-for-the-files-api.adoc` that the docs-worktree omits. Conversely, the docs-worktree includes "Using self-signed certificates with Llama Stack" in its bullet list while the code-repo does not.
- **Impact:** The docs-worktree assembly is missing a section that exists in the code-repo, suggesting the docs-worktree was based on an older version. Both bullet lists should reflect their respective includes.
- **Suggestion:** Ensure the published assembly includes all intended sections and that the introductory bullet list matches.

**M5. Operator service account name never specified**

- **Location:** `ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc`, RBAC section (docs-worktree); `troubleshooting-custom-ca-bundles.adoc`, permission denied section (docs-worktree)
- **Issue:** RBAC commands use `__<operator-sa-name>__` as a placeholder. The docs-worktree includes `oc get serviceaccounts -n __<operator-namespace>__` as a discovery step, which is good, but neither version states the actual default service account name.
- **Impact:** Readers must run a discovery command and identify the correct service account from a list.

**M6. Missing cross-reference links in code-repo troubleshooting module**

- **Location:** `modules/troubleshooting-custom-ca-bundles.adoc` (code-repo)
- **Issue:** The code-repo version has no `ifndef::disconnected[]` conditional cross-reference links to the procedure or adding-certificates modules. The docs-worktree adds these links (lines 11-18), helping readers navigate from troubleshooting back to the configuration procedure.
- **Impact:** Readers have no navigational path from troubleshooting back to the relevant procedures.
- **Suggestion:** Include the docs-worktree's cross-reference links.

---

### SME verification needed

**SME1. Confirm the 10 MB concatenated bundle size limit and 1000 certificate count**

- **Question:** Are these limits implemented in the Llama Stack Operator code for RHOAI 3.4? Given the 1 MiB Kubernetes ConfigMap constraint, the 10 MB limit appears unreachable from a single source ConfigMap. Is this a defensive maximum for a future multi-ConfigMap feature, or is it a documentation artifact?
- **Why it matters:** Documenting unreachable limits without explanation may confuse readers or suggest future capabilities that do not exist.

**SME2. Verify the Llama Stack Operator service account name**

- **Question:** What is the default service account name used by the Llama Stack Operator? The RBAC commands use `__<operator-sa-name>__` with no documented default.
- **Why it matters:** Without the actual name, RBAC troubleshooting and cross-namespace configuration commands are incomplete.

**SME3. Confirm LlamaStackClient http_client parameter accepts raw httpx.Client**

- **Question:** Does `LlamaStackClient(http_client=httpx.Client(verify=...))` work correctly, or must users use `DefaultHttpxClient` from `llama_stack_client`? The upstream SDK documentation recommends `DefaultHttpxClient`.
- **Why it matters:** If `httpx.Client` works but loses SDK defaults (timeouts, retries, error handling), the example may cause production issues. If it does not work at all, the code example is broken.

**SME4. Verify condition type names and status.phase values**

- **Question:** Are the condition type names (`DeploymentReady`, `ServiceReady`, `HealthCheck`) and phase values (`Initializing`, `Ready`, `Failed`) correct per the LlamaStackDistribution CRD and controller code for RHOAI 3.4?
- **Why it matters:** Incorrect condition names would cause verification steps to fail silently.

**SME5. Confirm pod label selector `app.kubernetes.io/instance=<instance-name>`**

- **Question:** Does the Llama Stack Operator set `app.kubernetes.io/instance` on pods? Verification step 4 in the procedure uses this label to find the server pod.
- **Why it matters:** If the operator uses a different label, the verification command returns empty output.

**SME6. Confirm the mount path `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle/ca-bundle.crt` and SSL_CERT_FILE usage**

- **Question:** Is the CA bundle mounted at `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle/ca-bundle.crt`? Is `SSL_CERT_FILE` (not `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` or `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`) the environment variable set by the operator? Do Python libraries (`httpx`, `requests`) in the Llama Stack server image honor this variable?
- **Why it matters:** Incorrect paths or variable names would cause all verification steps and client code examples to fail.

**SME7. Confirm whether curl is available in the Llama Stack server container image (rh-dev distribution)**

- **Question:** Does the rh-dev distribution container image include `curl`?
- **Why it matters:** The final verification step relies on `curl`. If unavailable, the fallback note in the docs-worktree version becomes essential rather than a nice-to-have.

---

### Strengths

1. **Comprehensive verification steps in the procedure module.** Six distinct verification steps progressively confirm: managed ConfigMap creation, CR status conditions, pod running state, mount path and SSL_CERT_FILE env var, certificate content inspection, and end-to-end TLS validation. This is significantly more thorough than most Red Hat OpenShift AI procedures.

2. **Clear architectural flow in the concept module.** The numbered list describing the four-step operator workflow (read, concatenate, mount, set env var) gives readers an accurate mental model of how the system works before they start the procedure.

3. **Three-option pattern mirrors existing certificate modules.** The concept module presents three options (cluster-wide CA, custom CA, dedicated Llama Stack CA) with cross-references, maintaining consistency with the existing certificate sections for pipelines, workbenches, and model serving.

4. **Production impact warning is prominent and repeated.** The IMPORTANT admonition about service interruption during CA bundle changes appears consistently across concept and procedure modules, ensuring production users are aware before proceeding.

5. **Docs-worktree fixes multiple broken elements from the code-repo.** The docs-worktree corrects broken cross-reference anchors (double hyphen typo and mismatched "reference" in anchor), adds RBAC commands for cross-namespace setup, improves troubleshooting entries with actionable commands and proper placeholder formatting, qualifies the prerequisite for the recommended pattern, and adds a curl-unavailable fallback note.

6. **Well-structured reference module.** The reference module cleanly separates subfield documentation, configuration examples with working YAML, validation rules, limits, failure conditions, and client code usage into distinct sections.

7. **Correct handling of disconnected environment conditionals.** All cross-references properly use `ifndef::disconnected[]` / `ifdef::disconnected[]` blocks with appropriate URL patterns for both connected and disconnected installation guides.

[id="troubleshooting-custom-ca-bundles_{context}"]
= Troubleshooting custom CA bundles

[role="_abstract"]
If you experience errors when configuring custom CA bundles for self-signed certificates, use the following information to resolve common issues and error messages.

If your issue is not described in the following information or in the release notes, contact {org-name} Support.

ifndef::disconnected[]
For the CA bundle configuration procedure, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed/working-with-certificates_certs#configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack_certs[Configuring a CA bundle for Llama Stack].
For information about adding CAs to the cluster-wide or custom CA bundle, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed/working-with-certificates_certs#adding-certificates-to-a-cluster-ca-bundle_certs[Adding certificates to a cluster-wide CA bundle] and link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed/working-with-certificates_certs#adding-certificates-to-a-custom-ca-bundle_certs[Adding certificates to a custom CA bundle].
endif::[]
ifdef::disconnected[]
For the CA bundle configuration procedure, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed_in_a_disconnected_environment/working-with-certificates_certs#configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack_certs[Configuring a CA bundle for Llama Stack].
For information about adding CAs to the cluster-wide or custom CA bundle, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed_in_a_disconnected_environment/working-with-certificates_certs#adding-certificates-to-a-cluster-ca-bundle_certs[Adding certificates to a cluster-wide CA bundle] and link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/installing_and_uninstalling_openshift_ai_self-managed_in_a_disconnected_environment/working-with-certificates_certs#adding-certificates-to-a-custom-ca-bundle_certs[Adding certificates to a custom CA bundle].
endif::[]

[id="common-issues_{context}"]
== Common issues

Certificate not found::
Ensure the config map exists in the expected namespace and contains the specified key.
To verify the config map and its keys, run the following command:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ -o yaml
----
+
Confirm that the expected key, such as `ca-bundle.crt`, is displayed in the `data` section of the output.

Permission denied::
Check that the Llama Stack Operator service account has permissions to read the config map.
To verify the operator's permissions, run the following command:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc auth can-i get configmaps \
  --as=system:serviceaccount:__<operator-namespace>__:__<operator-sa-name>__ \
  -n __<configmap-namespace>__
----
+
To find the service account name that the Llama Stack Operator uses, run `oc get serviceaccounts -n __<operator-namespace>__`.
+
If the output is `no`, create a `Role` and `RoleBinding` in the config map namespace to grant the operator service account `get` access to config maps.

Invalid certificate::
Verify that the certificate is in valid Privacy-Enhanced Mail (PEM) format.
To validate a certificate file, run the following command:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ openssl x509 -text -noout -in __<certificate_file>__
----
+
If the command reports an error, the certificate is not valid PEM or is corrupted.

Pod not restarting::
When you update the `spec.server.tlsConfig.caBundle` field or the contents of the source config map, the Llama Stack Operator automatically updates the managed config map annotation, which triggers a pod rollout.
If the pod does not restart automatically, verify that the `LlamaStackDistribution` CR status does not report a validation error:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get llamastackdistribution __<instance-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ -o yaml
----
+
Check the `status.conditions` field for a `DeploymentReady` condition set to `"False"`.
If the CR status is healthy but the pod has not restarted, manually restart the deployment:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc rollout restart deployment/__<instance-name>__ -n __<namespace>__
----

[id="common-error-messages-and-solutions_{context}"]
== Common error messages and solutions

CA bundle key not found in ConfigMap::
+
.Problem
The specified key does not exist in the ConfigMap data.
+
.Resolution
Check the key name in your `LlamaStackDistribution` spec. The default key name is `ca-bundle.crt`. Run the following command and verify that your expected key is displayed in the output:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ -o yaml
----

Invalid CA bundle format::
+
.Problem
The certificate data is not in valid PEM format or contains invalid certificates.
+
.Resolution
Ensure that each certificate is enclosed in `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` and `-----END CERTIFICATE-----` markers (PEM format).
To verify the format, extract the certificate data from the config map and validate it:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.ca-bundle\.crt}' > /tmp/ca-bundle.crt
$ openssl x509 -text -noout -in /tmp/ca-bundle.crt
----

Referenced CA bundle ConfigMap not found::
+
.Problem
The ConfigMap specified in `tlsConfig.caBundle.configMapName` does not exist.
+
.Resolution
Verify that the config map exists in the expected namespace:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__
----
+
If the config map does not exist, create it before applying the `LlamaStackDistribution` CR:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc create configmap __<configmap-name>__ \
  --from-file=ca-bundle.crt=__<path_to_ca_certificate>__ \
  -n __<namespace>__
----

No valid certificates found in CA bundle::
+
.Problem
The ConfigMap contains data but no parseable certificates.
+
.Resolution
Verify that the certificate file contains valid certificate data in PEM format.
To validate the certificate, run the following command:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ openssl x509 -text -noout -in __<certificate_file>__
----
+
If the certificate file is valid but the config map data is corrupted, re-create the config map with the correct certificate file.

Failed to parse certificate::
+
.Problem
Certificate data is corrupted or not a valid X.509 certificate.
+
.Resolution
Regenerate the certificate or verify the source.
Check that the certificate data is not double base64-encoded, which can occur when copying certificate content through intermediate tools.
To verify the encoding, extract and inspect the raw data:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.ca-bundle\.crt}' | head -5
----
+
The first line of valid PEM data is `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`. If the output shows base64-encoded content without PEM markers, decode it first and re-create the config map.

#!/bin/bash
# workflow-completion-check.sh
#
# Stop hook: blocks Claude from stopping while the ACTIVE workflow
# is still running. Only checks the workflow identified by the
# .active-workflow marker — stale workflows from other sessions
# are ignored.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 = allow stop
#   2 = block stop (reason sent to stderr)
#
# Requires: jq

set -u

INPUT=$(cat)

if ! cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Cannot access project directory; cannot verify workflow status." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Look for progress files
shopt -s nullglob
PROGRESS_FILES=(.agent_workspace/*/workflow/*.json)
shopt -u nullglob
if [ ${#PROGRESS_FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

MARKER=".agent_workspace/.active-workflow"

# No marker file → no active workflow → allow stop
if [ ! -f "$MARKER" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Read the marker — fail closed on parse errors
PROGRESS_FILE=$(jq -r '.progress_file // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_PF=$?
TICKET=$(jq -r '.ticket // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_TK=$?

if [ "$JQ_RC_PF" -ne 0 ] || [ "$JQ_RC_TK" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Failed to parse $MARKER; refusing to stop (fail closed)." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Marker parsed successfully but fields are empty → stale marker → clean up
if [ -z "$PROGRESS_FILE" ] || [ -z "$TICKET" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Progress file doesn't exist → stale marker → clean up and allow stop
if [ ! -f "$PROGRESS_FILE" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Check the workflow status — only block for in_progress workflows
WORKFLOW_STATUS=$(jq -r '.status' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ "$WORKFLOW_STATUS" != "in_progress" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

WORKFLOW_TYPE=$(jq -r '.workflow_type' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

# Anti-loop guard: per-workflow counter prevents infinite blocking
COUNTER_FILE="${PROGRESS_FILE}.stop_count"
if [ -f "$COUNTER_FILE" ]; then
  COUNT=$(cat "$COUNTER_FILE")
else
  COUNT=0
fi
if [ "$COUNT" -ge 5 ]; then
  rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Get step order from the progress file
mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.step_order[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#STEP_ORDER[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.steps | keys[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
fi

# Find the first incomplete step
NEXT_STEP=""
for step in "${STEP_ORDER[@]}"; do
  STEP_STATUS=$(jq -r --arg s "$step" '.steps[$s].status // "missing"' "$PROGRESS_FILE")
  case "$STEP_STATUS" in
    completed|skipped|deferred) continue ;;
    *) NEXT_STEP="$step"; break ;;
  esac
done

if [ -n "$NEXT_STEP" ]; then
  echo "$((COUNT + 1))" > "$COUNTER_FILE"
  echo "Documentation workflow '$WORKFLOW_TYPE' for $TICKET is not complete. Next step: $NEXT_STEP. Continue the workflow." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# All steps done — clean up and allow stop
rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
rm -f "$MARKER"
exit 0

[id="working-with-certificates_{context}"]
= Working with certificates

ifdef::preview[]
include::../_artifacts/document-attributes-global.adoc[]
endif::preview[]

[role='_abstract']
When you install {productname-long}, OpenShift automatically applies a default Certificate Authority (CA) bundle to manage authentication for most {productname-short} components, such as workbenches and model servers. These certificates are trusted self-signed certificates that help secure communication. However, as a cluster administrator, you might need to configure additional self-signed certificates to use some components, such as the AI pipeline server and object storage solutions. If an {productname-short} component uses a self-signed certificate that is not part of the existing cluster-wide CA bundle, you have the following options for including the certificate:

* Add it to the OpenShift cluster-wide CA bundle.

* Add it to a custom CA bundle, separate from the cluster-wide CA bundle. 

As a cluster administrator, you can also change how to manage authentication for {productname-short} as follows:

* Manually manage certificate changes, instead of relying on the {productname-short} Operator to handle them automatically.

* Remove the cluster-wide CA bundle, either from all namespaces or specific ones. If you prefer to implement a different authentication approach, you can override the default {productname-short} behavior, as described in _Removing the CA bundle_.

include::upstream-modules/understanding-certificates.adoc[leveloffset=+1]

== Adding certificates

If you must use a self-signed certificate that is not part of the existing cluster-wide CA bundle, you have two options for configuring the certificate:

* Add it to the cluster-wide CA bundle. 
+
This option is useful when the certificate is needed for secure communication across multiple services or when it is required by security policies to be trusted cluster-wide. This option ensures that all services and components in the cluster trust the certificate automatically. It simplifies management because the certificate is trusted across the entire cluster, avoiding the need to configure the certificate separately for each service. 

* Add it to a custom CA bundle that is separate from the OpenShift cluster-wide bundle. 
+ 
Consider this option for the following scenarios:

** Limit scope: Only specific services need the certificate, not the whole cluster.
** Isolation: Keeps custom certificates separate, preventing changes to the global configuration.
** Avoid global impact: Does not affect services that do not need the certificate.
** Easier management: Makes it simpler to manage certificates for specific services.


include::upstream-modules/adding-certificates-to-a-cluster-ca-bundle.adoc[leveloffset=+1]

include::upstream-modules/adding-certificates-to-a-custom-ca-bundle.adoc[leveloffset=+1]

== Using self-signed certificates with {productname-short} components

Some {productname-short} components have additional options or required configuration for self-signed certificates.

include::upstream-modules/accessing-s3-compatible-object-storage-with-self-signed-certificates.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

include::upstream-modules/configuring-a-certificate-for-pipelines.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

include::upstream-modules/configuring-a-certificate-for-workbenches.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

include::upstream-modules/using-the-cluster-CA-bundle-for-model-serving.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

include::upstream-modules/about-ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

include::upstream-modules/configuring-a-ca-bundle-for-llama-stack.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

include::upstream-modules/ca-bundle-configuration-for-llama-stack.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

include::modules/troubleshooting-custom-ca-bundles.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

include::upstream-modules/managing-certificates-without-the-operator.adoc[leveloffset=+1]

== Removing the CA bundle

If you prefer to implement a different authentication approach for your {productname-short} installation, you can override the default behavior by removing the CA bundle.

You have two options for removing the CA bundle:

* Remove the CA bundle from all non-reserved projects in {productname-short}.

* Remove the CA bundle from a specific project.


include::upstream-modules/removing-the-ca-bundle-from-all-namespaces.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

include::upstream-modules/removing-the-ca-bundle-from-a-single-namespace.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

Acceptance Criteria Coverage:

However, the ticket specifically asks for documentation of 'confidence scores,' and while the docs explicitly note that confidence scores are NOT included in annotations, this is documented as a limitation rather than as a feature. The docs handle this honestly, which is appropriate, but the ticket seemed to expect confidence scores as a feature to document.
  1. Usage instructions: how to enable and configure in Llama Stack — Addressed. The docs clearly state annotations are enabled by default and require no additional configuration. The procedure doc provides step-by-step instructions for accessing annotations via the API.

The reference doc mentions that the UI displays filenames as clickable links for downloading source files, and that file_id/index are only accessible via API. However, there are no screenshots or detailed UI walkthrough — just brief mentions and cross-references to a viewing-file-citation-annotations-in-llama-stack-ui module that is included but not provided in the output.
  1. Example API requests and responses demonstrating annotation fields — Excellently covered. The procedure doc includes Python SDK examples, curl examples, full JSON response payloads showing annotation structure, and the reference doc includes a complete response payload example.

.output/writing/file-citation-annotation-reference.adoc
:_mod-docs-content-type: REFERENCE

[id="file-citation-annotation-reference_{context}"]
= File citation annotation reference

[role="_abstract"]
The `file_citation` annotation type is returned by Llama Stack through the OpenAI-compatible Responses API.
You can use this information to parse and display citation data in your application.

ifndef::upstream[]
[IMPORTANT]
====
ifdef::self-managed[]
This feature is currently available in {productname-long} {vernum} as a Technology Preview feature.
endif::[]
ifdef::cloud-service[]
This feature is currently available in {productname-long} as a Technology Preview feature.
endif::[]
Technology Preview features are not supported with {org-name} production service level agreements (SLAs) and might not be functionally complete.
{org-name} does not recommend using them in production.
These features provide early access to upcoming product features, enabling customers to test functionality and provide feedback during the development process.

For more information about the support scope of {org-name} Technology Preview features, see link:https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview/[Technology Preview Features Support Scope].
====
endif::[]

[id="annotation-location_{context}"]
== Annotation location

Annotations are returned in the `annotations` field of `output_text` content items within the `output[].content[]` structure of the Responses API response.

The following example shows a complete Responses API response payload that includes file citation annotations.
When the `file_search` tool is used, the `output` array contains a `file_search_call` item followed by a `message` item.
The annotations appear in the `content` array of the `message` item.

[source,json]
----
{
  "id": "resp-abc123",
  "object": "response",
  "created_at": 1749638400,
  "model": "meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct",
  "output": [
    {
      "type": "file_search_call",
      "id": "fs_abc123",
      "status": "completed",
      "queries": [
        "Red Bank Financial overview"
      ],
      "results": null
    },
    {
      "type": "message",
      "id": "msg_abc123",
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "output_text",
          "text": "According to the document, Red Bank Financial is a community-focused financial institution.",
          "annotations": [
            {
              "type": "file_citation",
              "file_id": "file-57610eaac6364459bfefae60377837b7",
              "filename": "redbankfinancial_about.pdf",
              "index": 139
            },
            {
              "type": "file_citation",
              "file_id": "file-a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6",
              "filename": "redbankfinancial_services.pdf",
              "index": 42
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "status": "completed"
}
----

[NOTE]
====
When the `include` parameter is set to `file_search_call.results` in the request, the `file_search_call` item contains a `results` array with extended search result metadata.
When `include` is not specified, the `results` field is `null`.
====

[id="supported-annotation-type_{context}"]
== Supported annotation type

In {productname-short}, Llama Stack returns the `file_citation` annotation type when using the `file_search` tool.

[id="openai-annotation-type-compatibility_{context}"]
== OpenAI annotation type compatibility

The following table compares the annotation types defined in the OpenAI schema with their support status in Llama Stack in {productname-short} {vernum}.
The request schema for `file_search` tool configuration, including the `vector_store_ids` parameter, is identical to the OpenAI specification.

[cols="2,1,3",options="header"]
|===
|Annotation type |Status |Notes

|`file_citation`
|Supported
|Returned when the `file_search` tool retrieves content from a vector store.
Includes `file_id`, `filename`, and `index` fields.

|`url_citation`
|Not produced
|Defined in the OpenAI schema for web search results.
Llama Stack does not produce this type because it does not perform web searches.

|`container_file_citation`
|Not produced
|Defined in the OpenAI schema for container-based file retrieval.
This type is specific to OpenAI container environments.

|`file_path`
|Not produced
|Defined in the OpenAI schema for Code Interpreter file outputs.
Llama Stack does not include a Code Interpreter tool.
|===

[id="file-citation-fields_{context}"]
== File citation fields

The `file_citation` annotation includes the following fields:

[cols="1,1,2",options="header"]
|===
|Field |Type |Description

|type
|string
|Always `file_citation`.

|file_id
|string
|Identifier of the source file used during retrieval.

|filename
|string
|Name of the source file.

|index
|integer
|Character position in the output text where the citation should be inserted.
This value corresponds to the position in the generated text, not an index into a list of files.
|===

[NOTE]
====
Confidence scores are not included in file citation annotations.
The annotation provides document-level attribution without a relevance or confidence indicator.
====

[id="metadata-availability-by-pipeline-stage_{context}"]
== Metadata availability by pipeline stage

The following table shows which metadata fields are available at each stage of the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline.
Custom attributes that you attach during file ingestion are preserved in search results but are not included in the final annotation output.

[cols="2,1,1,1",options="header"]
|===
|Metadata field |Vector store |Search results |File citation annotations

|`file_id`
|Yes
|Yes
|Yes

|`filename`
|Yes
|Yes
|Yes

|Custom attributes (for example, `title`, `author`)
|Yes
|Yes
|No

|Relevance score
|No
|Yes
|No

|Chunk text
|No
|Yes
|No

|`index`
|No
|No
|Yes

|Timestamps (created, modified)
|No
|No

... truncated (228 lines total)
.output/writing/openai-compatible-apis-in-llama-stack.adoc
:_mod-docs-content-type: REFERENCE
[id="openai-compatible-apis-in-Llama-Stack_{context}"]
= OpenAI-compatible APIs in Llama Stack

[role="_abstract"]
{productname-short} includes a Llama Stack component that exposes OpenAI-compatible APIs. You can reuse existing OpenAI SDKs, tools, and workflows directly within your {openshift-platform} environment, without changing your client code. This compatibility layer supports retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), inference, and embedding workloads by using OpenAI-compatible endpoints, schemas, and authentication patterns.

This compatibility layer has the following capabilities:

* *Standardized endpoints*: REST API paths align with OpenAI specifications.  
* *Schema parity:* Request and response fields follow OpenAI data structures.  

[IMPORTANT]
====
When connecting OpenAI SDKs or third-party tools to {productname-short}, you must update the client configuration to use your deployment's Llama Stack route as the `base_url`.

When you use OpenAI-compatible SDKs, the `base_url` **must include the `/v1` path suffix** so that requests are routed to the OpenAI-compatible API surface exposed by Llama Stack.

When you use OpenAI SDKs or send raw HTTP requests to Llama Stack, always include the `/v1` path suffix in the base URL.

For example:
`http://llama-stack-service:8321/v1`

Using the service endpoint without `/v1` results in request failures.
====

These endpoints are exposed under the OpenAI compatibility layer and are distinct from the native Llama Stack APIs.

== Supported OpenAI-compatible APIs in {productname-short}

Before running the following examples, ensure you have:

* The OpenAI Python SDK installed: `pip install -q openai rich`
* A configured client pointing to your Llama Stack endpoint
* Model IDs from your deployment (see Models API section)

[source,python]
----
import os
from openai import OpenAI
import rich

# We'll be using a llama-stack server deployed in {productname-short}.
# Once all pods associated to the LlamaStackDistribution are running,
# create the base_url using the llama-stack service hostname (with /v1 at the end when using openai sdk)
base_url = "http://llama-stack-distribution-service.my-project.svc.cluster.local:8321/v1"

import openai
client = openai.OpenAI(
    api_key="your-llama-stack-key",
    base_url=base_url
)
----

ifdef::upstream[]
For more information, see link:{odhdocshome}/working-with-llama-stack/#deploying-llama-stack-server_rag[Deploying a Llama Stack server].
endif::[]
ifndef::upstream[]
For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/deploying-llama-stack-server_rag[Deploying a Llama Stack server].
endif::[]

---

=== Models API
* *Endpoint:* `/v1/models`.  
* *Providers:* All model-serving back ends configured within {productname-short}.
* *Support level:* Technology Preview. 

The Models API lists and retrieves available model resources from the Llama Stack deployment running on {productname-short}. By using the Models API, you can enumerate models, view their capabilities, and verify deployment status through a standardized OpenAI-compatible interface.

Example code in Python:

[source,python]
----
# List models available in the llama-stack server
models = client.models.list()
rich.print(models)

# Select the first LLM and first embedding model
model_id = next(m for m in models if m.custom_metadata["model_type"] == "llm").id
embedding_model_id = (
    em := next(m for m in models if m.custom_metadata["model_type"] == "embedding")
).id
embedding_dimension = em.custom_metadata["embedding_dimension"]
----
---

=== Chat Completions API
* *Endpoint:* `/v1/chat/completions`.  
* *Providers:* All inference back ends deployed through {productname-short}.
* *Support level:* Technology Preview. 

The Chat Completions API enables conversational, message-based interactions with models served by Llama Stack in {productname-short}.

Example code in Python:

[source,python]
----
# Test chat completion functionality with a simple question
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=model_id,
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"},
    ],
    temperature=0,
)
# Optional verification check
assert len(response.choices) > 0, "No response after basic inference on llama-stack server"
content = response.choices[0].message.content
rich.print(content)
----
---

=== Completions API
* *Endpoint:* `/v1/completions`.  
* *Providers:* All inference back ends managed by {productname-short}.
* *Support level:* Technology Preview. 

The Completions API supports single-turn text generation and prompt completion.

Example code in Python:

[source,python]
----
# Test completion functionality with a simple question
response = client.completions.create(
    model=model_id,
    prompt="Answer with one word only: What is the capital of France?",
    max_tokens=64,
    temperature=0.1
)
# Optional verification check
assert len(response.choices) > 0, "No response after basic inference on llama-stack server"
content = response.choices[0].text
rich.print(content)
----
---

=== Embeddings API
* *Endpoint:* `/v1/embeddings`.  
* *Providers:* All embedding models enabled in {productname-short}.

The Embeddings API generates numerical embeddings for text or documents that can be used in downstream semantic search or RAG applications.

Example code in Python:

[source,python]
----
# Create text embeddings
response = client.embeddings.create(
    input="Your text string goes here",
    model=embedding_model_id
)
embedding = response.data[0].embedding
rich.print(embedding[:5] + ["..."] + embedding[-5:])
----
---

=== Files API
* *Endpoint:* `/v1/files`.  
* *Providers:* File system-based file storage provider for managing files and documents stored locally in your cluster.
* *Support level:* Technology Preview. 

The Files API manages file uploads for use in embedding and retrieval workflows.

Example code in Python:

[source,python]
----
import requests
from rich import print
from rich.rule import Rule
import time

# -----------------------------
# Download the PDF from url
# -----------------------------
print(Rule("[bold cyan]Downloading PDF[/bold cyan]"))

# We'll use IBM 2025-Q4 report to test RAG, as models don't have that info
pdf_url = "https://www.ibm.com/downloads/documents/us-en/1550f7eea8c0ded6"
filename = "ibm-Q4-2025-4q25-press-release.pdf"
title = "IBM-4Q25-Earnings-Press-Release"

print("📥 Fetching PDF from URL...")
response = requests.get(pdf_url)
response.raise_for_status()
print("✅ PDF fetched successfully")

print(f"💾 Saving PDF as [bold]{filename}[/bold]...")
with open(filename, "wb") as f:
    f.write(response.content)
print(f"✅ Downloaded and saved: [green]{filename}[/green]")

# -----------------------------
# Upload the PDF
# -----------------------------
print(Rule("[bold cyan]Uploading File[/bold cyan]"))

[id="openai-file-citation-annotations-in-llama-stack_{context}"]
= OpenAI-compatible file citation annotations in Llama Stack

[role="_abstract"]
{productname-short} provides OpenAI-compatible file citation annotations in Responses API outputs when you use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with the `file_search` tool.
You can use these annotations to trace generated responses back to the source files used during retrieval without changing existing OpenAI client code.
When you use the Responses API with the `file_search` tool, Llama Stack returns citation metadata that references the source file used to generate the response.
Annotations are enabled by default and require no additional configuration in {productname-short} {vernum}.

ifndef::upstream[]
[IMPORTANT]
====
ifdef::self-managed[]
This feature is currently available in {productname-long} {vernum} as a Technology Preview feature.
endif::[]
ifdef::cloud-service[]
This feature is currently available in {productname-long} as a Technology Preview feature.
endif::[]
Technology Preview features are not supported with {org-name} production service level agreements (SLAs) and might not be functionally complete.
{org-name} does not recommend using them in production.
These features provide early access to upcoming product features, enabling customers to test functionality and provide feedback during the development process.

For more information about the support scope of {org-name} Technology Preview features, see link:https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview/[Technology Preview Features Support Scope].
====
endif::[]

[id="openai-compatibility-for-annotations_{context}"]
== OpenAI compatibility for file citation annotations

Llama Stack implements the same annotation schema as the OpenAI Responses API.
The request schemas, including `file_search` tool configuration and `vector_store_ids`, are identical to the OpenAI specification.
The response schemas, including the `annotations` array and `file_citation` fields (`type`, `file_id`, `filename`, `index`), also match the OpenAI specification.
This means that existing OpenAI client applications can consume file citation annotations from Llama Stack without any code changes.

You can use the standard OpenAI Python SDK or any HTTP client that targets the OpenAI Responses API to send requests to Llama Stack and receive annotation data in the same format that OpenAI returns.
The only required change is updating the `base_url` in the client configuration to point to your Llama Stack server endpoint.

Only the `file_citation` annotation type is supported.
The `url_citation`, `container_file_citation`, and `file_path` annotation types that are defined in the OpenAI schema are not produced by Llama Stack.
For a detailed comparison of supported and unsupported annotation types, see xref:openai-annotation-type-compatibility_{context}[the OpenAI annotation type compatibility table].

[id="annotation-capabilities_{context}"]
== Annotation capabilities and limitations

Llama Stack returns `file_citation` annotations when the `file_search` tool retrieves content from a vector store during a RAG query.
Annotations are enabled by default and require no additional configuration.
Llama Stack attributes citations at the document level, meaning each annotation references the source file rather than a specific chunk or token.

In the Llama Stack UI, annotations display the source filename as a clickable link.
You can click the filename to download the corresponding source file.
For more information about viewing annotations in the UI, see xref:viewing-file-citation-annotations-in-llama-stack-ui_{context}[].

The following capabilities are not available in {productname-short} {vernum}:

* Confidence scores are not included in annotations.
* Chunk-level and token-level attribution are not supported.
* Configurable annotation levels, such as basic, detailed, or comprehensive, are not implemented.

[NOTE]
====
Configurable annotation levels are not available in {productname-short} {vernum}.
====

[id="metadata-flow-through-the-rag-pipeline_{context}"]
== Metadata flow through the RAG pipeline

When you build a RAG application that uses file citation annotations, it is important to understand which metadata is preserved at each stage of the pipeline.
Not all metadata that you attach during file ingestion is included in the final annotation output.

The metadata flows through the following stages:

. *File ingestion*: When you upload a file to a vector store and attach it by using the Vector Store Files API, the system records the `file_id`, `filename`, and any custom attributes that you specify (such as `title` or `author`).
Custom attributes are passed as the `attributes` parameter during the `client.vector_stores.files.create()` call.
ifdef::upstream[]
For more information, see link:{odhdocshome}/working-with-llama-stack/#openai-compatible-apis-in-Llama-Stack_rag[OpenAI-compatible APIs in Llama Stack].
endif::[]
ifndef::upstream[]
For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/index#openai-compatible-apis-in-Llama-Stack_rag[OpenAI-compatible APIs in Llama Stack].
endif::[]
The file is chunked and each chunk inherits the `filename` from the parent file record.
. *Vector store storage*: The vector store persists chunked embeddings along with the chunk metadata.
Custom attributes that you specified during ingestion are preserved in the chunk metadata at this stage.
. *Search results*: When the `file_search` tool retrieves relevant chunks during a RAG query, the search results include the `file_id`, `filename`, custom attributes, relevance scores, and chunk text.
You can access these extended search result details by using the `include` parameter in your Responses API request.
. *File citation annotations*: The final `file_citation` annotation objects in the Responses API output contain only the `file_id`, `filename`, and `index` fields.
Custom attributes, relevance scores, and chunk text are not included in the annotation output.

If you need to access metadata beyond what annotations provide, such as relevance scores, chunk text, or custom attributes, use the `include` parameter with the value `file_search_call.results` in your Responses API request.
For more information, see xref:viewing-file-citation-annotations-in-responses-api-output_{context}[].
