#!/bin/bash
# workflow-completion-check.sh
#
# Stop hook: blocks Claude from stopping while the ACTIVE workflow
# is still running. Only checks the workflow identified by the
# .active-workflow marker — stale workflows from other sessions
# are ignored.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 = allow stop
#   2 = block stop (reason sent to stderr)
#
# Requires: jq

set -u

INPUT=$(cat)

if ! cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Cannot access project directory; cannot verify workflow status." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Look for progress files
shopt -s nullglob
PROGRESS_FILES=(.agent_workspace/*/workflow/*.json)
shopt -u nullglob
if [ ${#PROGRESS_FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

MARKER=".agent_workspace/.active-workflow"

# No marker file → no active workflow → allow stop
if [ ! -f "$MARKER" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Read the marker — fail closed on parse errors
PROGRESS_FILE=$(jq -r '.progress_file // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_PF=$?
TICKET=$(jq -r '.ticket // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_TK=$?

if [ "$JQ_RC_PF" -ne 0 ] || [ "$JQ_RC_TK" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Failed to parse $MARKER; refusing to stop (fail closed)." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Marker parsed successfully but fields are empty → stale marker → clean up
if [ -z "$PROGRESS_FILE" ] || [ -z "$TICKET" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Progress file doesn't exist → stale marker → clean up and allow stop
if [ ! -f "$PROGRESS_FILE" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Check the workflow status — only block for in_progress workflows
WORKFLOW_STATUS=$(jq -r '.status' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ "$WORKFLOW_STATUS" != "in_progress" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

WORKFLOW_TYPE=$(jq -r '.workflow_type' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

# Anti-loop guard: per-workflow counter prevents infinite blocking
COUNTER_FILE="${PROGRESS_FILE}.stop_count"
if [ -f "$COUNTER_FILE" ]; then
  COUNT=$(cat "$COUNTER_FILE")
else
  COUNT=0
fi
if [ "$COUNT" -ge 5 ]; then
  rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Get step order from the progress file
mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.step_order[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#STEP_ORDER[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.steps | keys[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
fi

# Find the first incomplete step
NEXT_STEP=""
for step in "${STEP_ORDER[@]}"; do
  STEP_STATUS=$(jq -r --arg s "$step" '.steps[$s].status // "missing"' "$PROGRESS_FILE")
  case "$STEP_STATUS" in
    completed|skipped|deferred) continue ;;
    *) NEXT_STEP="$step"; break ;;
  esac
done

if [ -n "$NEXT_STEP" ]; then
  echo "$((COUNT + 1))" > "$COUNTER_FILE"
  echo "Documentation workflow '$WORKFLOW_TYPE' for $TICKET is not complete. Next step: $NEXT_STEP. Continue the workflow." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# All steps done — clean up and allow stop
rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
rm -f "$MARKER"
exit 0

[id="deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project"]
= Deploy a RAG stack in a project

:context: deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project

ifndef::upstream[]
[IMPORTANT]
====
ifdef::self-managed[]
This feature is currently available in {productname-long} {vernum} as a Technology Preview feature.
endif::[]
ifdef::cloud-service[]
This feature is currently available in {productname-long} as a Technology Preview feature.
endif::[]
Technology Preview features are not supported with {org-name} production service level agreements (SLAs) and might not be functionally complete.
{org-name} does not recommend using them in production.
These features provide early access to upcoming product features, enabling customers to test functionality and provide feedback during the development process.

For more information about the support scope of {org-name} Technology Preview features, see link:https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview/[Technology Preview Features Support Scope].
====

[role="_abstract"]
As an {openshift-platform} cluster administrator, you can deploy a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) stack in {productname-short}. This stack provides the infrastructure, including LLM inference, vector storage, and retrieval services that data scientists and AI engineers use to build conversational workflows in their projects.

To deploy the RAG stack in a project, complete the following tasks:

* Activate the Llama Stack Operator in {productname-short}.
* Enable GPU support on the {openshift-platform} cluster. This task includes installing the required NVIDIA Operators.
* Deploy an inference model, for example, the llama-3.2-3b-instruct model. This task includes creating a storage connection and configuring GPU allocation.
* Create a `LlamaStackDistribution` instance to enable RAG functionality. This action deploys Llama Stack with a vector store provider such as Milvus, FAISS, or PostgreSQL with pgvector, and connects it to the inference model.
* Ingest domain data into the configured vector store by running Docling in an AI pipeline or Jupyter notebook. This process keeps the embeddings synchronized with the source data.
* Expose and secure the model endpoints.

include::upstream-modules/overview-of-rag.adoc[leveloffset=+1]
include::upstream-modules/overview-of-vector-databases.adoc[leveloffset=+1]
include::upstream-modules/overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc[leveloffset=+2]

[id="llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference_{context}"]
= Llama Stack SDK API changes in version 0.3.1

[role="_abstract"]
The Llama Stack SDK version 0.3.1 introduces breaking API changes that affect all vector store providers, including inline Milvus, remote Milvus, inline FAISS, and PostgreSQL with pgvector.
If you have existing Jupyter notebooks or scripts that use the Llama Stack SDK version 0.2.x, you must update your code to use the new API patterns.

Review the breaking changes, before-and-after code comparisons, and affected SDK methods to update your code.

== Summary of breaking changes

The following table lists the breaking API changes introduced in Llama Stack SDK version 0.3.1.

.Llama Stack SDK 0.3.1 breaking changes
[options="header"]
|===
|Change |Old API pattern (SDK 0.2.x) |New API pattern (SDK 0.3.1)

|Vector store creation
|`client.vector_dbs.register(vector_db_id=..., embedding_model=..., embedding_dimension=..., provider_id=...)`
|`client.vector_stores.create(name=..., extra_body={"embedding_model": ..., "embedding_dimension": ..., "provider_id": ...})`

|Document ingestion
|`RAGDocument` objects with `client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert()`
|`client.vector_stores.files.create(vector_store_id=..., file_id=..., chunking_strategy={...})`

|Content querying
|`client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.query()`
|`client.responses.create(tools=[{"type": "file_search", "vector_store_ids": [...]}])`

|Vector store identifier parameter
|`vector_db_id` and `vector_db_ids`
|`vector_store_id` and `vector_store_ids`

|Minimum SDK version
|`llama_stack_client >= 0.2.22`
|`llama_stack_client >= 0.3.1`

|`fire` dependency
|Required (`pip install fire`)
|Removed from dependencies
|===

== Vector store creation with `extra_body`

In SDK 0.3.1, you pass vector store creation parameters such as `embedding_model`, `embedding_dimension`, and `provider_id` inside an `extra_body` dictionary instead of as top-level keyword arguments.

.Old pattern (SDK 0.2.x)
[source,python]
----
vector_db = client.vector_dbs.register(
    vector_db_id="my_store",
    embedding_model=embedding_model_id,
    embedding_dimension=embedding_dimension,
    provider_id="milvus",
)
----

.New pattern (SDK 0.3.1)
[source,python]
----
vector_store = client.vector_stores.create(
    name="my_store",
    extra_body={
        "embedding_model": embedding_model_id,
        "embedding_dimension": embedding_dimension,
        "provider_id": "milvus",
    },
)
vector_store_id = vector_store.id
----

Verify that `vector_store.id` returns a non-empty string to confirm the vector store was created successfully.

This change applies to all vector store providers.
Replace the `provider_id` value with the provider that matches your deployment: `milvus` for inline Milvus, `milvus-remote` for remote Milvus, `faiss` for inline FAISS, or `pgvector` for PostgreSQL with pgvector.

== Document ingestion with the vector store files API

In SDK 0.3.1, document ingestion uses the `client.vector_stores.files.create()` method with file upload instead of the `RAGDocument` class and `rag_tool.insert()` method.

.Old pattern (SDK 0.2.x)
[source,python]
----
from llama_stack_client.types import RAGDocument

documents = [
    RAGDocument(
        document_id="doc-1",
        content="https://example.com/document.pdf",
        mime_type="application/pdf",
        metadata={},
    ),
]

client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert(
    tool_name="builtin::rag/knowledge_search",
    vector_db_id=vector_db_id,
    documents=documents,
    chunk_size_in_tokens=800,
)
----

.New pattern (SDK 0.3.1)
[source,python]
----
# Upload the file first
with open("document.pdf", "rb") as f:
    file_info = client.files.create(
        file=("document.pdf", f),
        purpose="assistants",
    )

# Add the file to a vector store with chunking
vector_store_file = client.vector_stores.files.create(
    vector_store_id=vector_store_id,
    file_id=file_info.id,
    chunking_strategy={
        "type": "static",
        "static": {
            "max_chunk_size_tokens": 800,
            "chunk_overlap_tokens": 400,
        },
    },
)
----

Verify that `vector_store_file.id` returns a non-empty string to confirm the file was ingested successfully.

The following list describes the key differences:

* SDK 0.3.1 removes the `RAGDocument` class. Remove it from your import statements.
* You must upload files to Llama Stack with `client.files.create()` before ingestion.
Documents must be available as local files.
URL-based document references, such as `content="https://example.com/document.pdf"`, are no longer directly supported.
If your existing code loads documents by URL, you must download the file to local storage before uploading it with `client.files.create()`.
* You specify chunking parameters in a `chunking_strategy` dictionary instead of as a `chunk_size_in_tokens` argument.
Tune the `chunk_overlap_tokens` value based on your use case.
The value of `400` in this example is a high overlap (50% of `max_chunk_size_tokens`) chosen for illustration.
A typical starting value is 100 to 200 tokens.
Higher overlap values increase index size but can improve retrieval quality for context-dependent content.
* The method returns metadata about the ingested file, which you can use for verification.

== Content querying with the responses API

In SDK 0.3.1, RAG queries use the `client.responses.create()` method with a `file_search` tool instead of the `rag_tool.query()` method.

.Old pattern (SDK 0.2.x)
[source,python]
----
response = client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.query(
    tool_name="builtin::rag/knowledge_search",
    vector_db_ids=[vector_db_id],
    content="What is retrieval-augmented generation?",
)
----

.New pattern (SDK 0.3.1)
[source,python]
----
response = client.responses.create(
    model=model_id,
    input="What is retrieval-augmented generation?",
    instructions="Use retrieved context when available.",
    tools=[
        {
            "type": "file_search",
            "vector_store_ids": [vector_store_id],
        }
    ],
)

print(response.output_text)
----

Verify that `response.output_text` contains a model-generated answer that incorporates the retrieved context from your ingested documents.

The following list describes the key differences:

* The `responses.create()` method with a `file_search` tool type replaces the `rag_tool.query()` method.
* The `response.output_text` attribute contains a model-generated answer that incorporates the retrieved context.
Unlike the old `rag_tool.query()` method, which returned raw retrieved chunks, the Responses API returns text generated by the LLM.
To access the raw retrieved chunks, inspect the `output` array in the full response object for file search results.
* You must specify the `model` parameter to indicate which LLM generates the response.
* Customize the `instructions` parameter for your specific use case to improve response quality.
For a more detailed example, see xref:querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model_{context}[Querying ingested content in a Llama model].

== Parameter rename: `vector_db_id` to `vector_store_id`

SDK 0.3.1 renames all occurrences of `vector_db_id` and `vector_db_ids` to `vector_store_id` and `vector_store_ids`.

.Affected parameters
[options="header"]
|===
|Old parameter name |New parameter name |Context

|`vector_db_id`
|`vector_store_id`

[id="overview-of-faiss-vector-databases_{context}"]
= Overview of FAISS vector databases

[role="_abstract"]
FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) is an open source framework for high-performance vector search and clustering, optimized for dense numerical embeddings, and supports both CPU and GPU execution.
In {productname-short}, FAISS is supported as an inline vector store provider for Llama Stack, enabling fast, in-process similarity search without requiring a separate vector database service.

When you enable inline FAISS in a `LlamaStackDistribution`, Llama Stack uses FAISS as an embedded vector index that runs inside the Llama Stack server container.
This configuration supports lightweight development, experimentation, and single-node retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows.

Inline FAISS provides the following capabilities in {productname-short}:

* In-process similarity search using FAISS indexes.
* Low-latency embedding ingestion and query operations.
* Simple deployment with no external vector database service.
* Compatibility with OpenAI-compatible Vector Stores API endpoints.

In {productname-short} 3.2, inline FAISS relies on the Llama Stack metadata and persistence backend for managing vector store state.
PostgreSQL is the default and recommended backend for production-grade deployments, even when you use FAISS as the inline vector index.

SQLite can be explicitly configured for local or on-the-fly development scenarios, but it is not recommended for production use.

Inline FAISS is suitable for the following use cases:

* Rapid prototyping of RAG workflows.
* Development or testing environments.
* Disconnected or single-node deployments where external vector databases are not required.

[NOTE]
====
Inline FAISS does not offer distributed storage, replication, or high availability.
For production-grade RAG workloads that require durability, scalability, or multi-node access, use a remote vector database such as Milvus or PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension.
====

ifdef::upstream[]
For an example of deploying a `LlamaStackDistribution` instance with inline FAISS, see link:{odhdocshome}/working-with-llama-stack/#example_c_llamastackdistribution_with_inline_faiss[Example C: LlamaStackDistribution with Inline FAISS].
endif::[]
ifndef::upstream[]
For an example of deploying a `LlamaStackDistribution` instance with inline FAISS, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag#example_c_llamastackdistribution_with_inline_faiss[Example C: LlamaStackDistribution with Inline FAISS].
endif::[]

# Documentation Plan: FAISS Vector Store Integration for RHOAI 3.0

**Ticket**: RHAIENG-1550
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Release**: RHOAI 3.0
**Output format**: AsciiDoc (`.adoc`)
**Status**: Closed (docs published to docs.redhat.com)

---

## 1. Requirements Summary

RHAIENG-1550 covers two interleaved documentation changes for the RHOAI 3.0 Llama Stack runtime:

1. **FAISS vector store integration** -- Adding inline FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) as a third vector store option alongside inline Milvus Lite and remote Milvus across all RAG procedure documentation (deployment, ingestion, querying, Docling pipeline).

2. **Llama Stack SDK 0.3.1 API migration** -- A set of five breaking API changes bundled in the same PR that affect all vector store providers, not just FAISS:
   - `extra_body` dict pattern for vector store creation parameters
   - `client.vector_stores.files.create()` replaces `RAGDocument` + `rag_tool.insert()`
   - `client.responses.create()` with `file_search` replaces `rag_tool.query()`
   - `vector_db_id` renamed to `vector_store_id` throughout
   - SDK minimum version bumped from 0.2.22 to 0.3.1

Additionally, two minor changes are included: a `--enable-auto-tool-choice` vLLM prerequisite addition and a websearch/wolfram_alpha tool availability clarification.

All 14 requirements trace to a single JIRA ticket (RHAIENG-1550), one upstream PR (#1046, 963 lines across 7 files), and one downstream MR (!2105).

---

## 2. Documentation Impact Assessment

| Requirement | Title | Impact Grade | Priority | Evidence Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-001 | New FAISS vector store overview concept module | High | Critical | Grounded |
| REQ-002 | FAISS deployment example in LlamaStackDistribution CR | High | Critical | Grounded |
| REQ-003 | Add FAISS to vector databases overview comparison | High | High | Grounded |
| REQ-004 | FAISS as vector store option in ingestion procedure | High | High | Grounded |
| REQ-005 | FAISS as vector store option in query procedure | High | High | Grounded |
| REQ-006 | FAISS as vector store option in Docling pipeline procedure | High | High | Grounded |
| REQ-007 | Vector store creation API migration to extra_body pattern | High | Critical | Grounded |
| REQ-008 | Ingestion API migration from RAGDocument to Vector Store Files API | High | Critical | Grounded |
| REQ-009 | Query API migration from rag_tool.query to Responses API | High | Critical | Grounded |
| REQ-010 | Rename vector_db_id to vector_store_id throughout | High | High | Grounded |
| REQ-011 | SDK version requirement bump to 0.3.1 | Medium | High | Partial |
| REQ-012 | Update assembly to include FAISS overview at correct level | Medium | Medium | Grounded |
| REQ-013 | Add --enable-auto-tool-choice prerequisite for vLLM deployment | Medium | Medium | Grounded |
| REQ-014 | Clarify websearch and wolfram_alpha tool availability | Low | Low | Partial |

### Evidence status notes

- **REQ-011 (Partial)**: The SDK version string "0.3.1" was found in the three expected modules (ingesting, querying, Docling) but scored below the grounded threshold. The key_files correctly identify the three procedure modules. Full module specification is warranted with a note to verify prerequisite text against published output.
- **REQ-014 (Partial)**: The tool availability correction is a single-sentence change. The key_files correctly identify `deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc`. Full module specification is warranted given the change is already implemented in the codebase.

No requirements have absent evidence status. All 14 requirements proceed to module planning.

---

## 3. Relationship Analysis

### Theme clusters

#### Cluster A: FAISS Feature Addition
- **Summary**: New inline FAISS vector store as a third option across all RAG documentation
- **Issues included**: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-012
- **Overlap risk**: High
- **Recommended ownership**: Deploying a RAG stack assembly (`deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project.adoc`)

REQ-001 through REQ-006 and REQ-012 all describe adding FAISS content to various modules. They share substantial overlap because the same PR (#1046) implements all changes simultaneously. The per-requirement granularity reflects each individual module touched, but the documentation update is a single coordinated change.

#### Cluster B: SDK 0.3.1 API Migration (Breaking Changes)
- **Summary**: Five breaking API changes to the Llama Stack SDK affecting all vector store providers
- **Issues included**: REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011
- **Overlap risk**: High
- **Recommended ownership**: Same RAG assembly procedures (ingestion, querying, Docling)

These five requirements describe facets of a single SDK API migration. They affect the same three procedure modules and should be implemented as a coordinated update pass.

#### Cluster C: Deployment Prerequisites
- **Summary**: Minor prerequisite and admonition updates to the deployment procedure
- **Issues included**: REQ-013, REQ-014
- **Overlap risk**: Low
- **Recommended ownership**: `deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc`

### Relationship pairs

| Pair | Relationship | Note |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-001 / REQ-002 | Overlapping | Both create the same FAISS concept module |
| REQ-001 / REQ-003 | Complementary | Concept overview vs. comparison update |
| REQ-003 / REQ-004 / REQ-005 / REQ-006 | Parallel/Sibling | Adding FAISS Option 3 to four different procedures |
| REQ-007 / REQ-008 / REQ-009 / REQ-010 / REQ-011 | Overlapping | All are facets of the SDK 0.3.1 migration |
| REQ-004 / REQ-008 | Overlapping | Both modify the ingestion procedure module |
| REQ-005 / REQ-009 | Overlapping | Both modify the querying procedure module |
| REQ-013 / REQ-014 | Parallel/Sibling | Both update the deployment procedure prerequisites |

### Consolidation decisions

Given the high overlap within Clusters A and B, the module plan consolidates requirements by **target file** rather than by requirement ID. Each AsciiDoc file that needs changes becomes one module specification, regardless of how many requirements touch it.

---

## 4. Personas

| Persona | Role | Relevant Jobs |
|---|---|---|
| **Data Scientist / AI Engineer** | Develops and tests RAG workflows using Jupyter notebooks, the Llama Stack SDK, and vector stores. Selects vector store providers and writes Python code for ingestion and querying. | Ingest content into vector stores, query ingested content, choose a vector store provider, prepare documents with Docling |
| **OpenShift Cluster Administrator** | Deploys and configures the Llama Stack operator, creates LlamaStackDistribution CRs, manages cluster infrastructure including GPU enablement and model serving. | Deploy LlamaStackDistribution instances, activate Llama Stack Operator, configure vector store backends |

### Persona separation rationale

The deployment procedure (creating the LlamaStackDistribution CR with FAISS environment variables) targets the **Cluster Administrator** persona. The ingestion, querying, and Docling procedures (using the Llama Stack SDK in Jupyter notebooks) target the **Data Scientist** persona. The concept modules (FAISS overview, vector databases overview) serve both personas but primarily inform the data scientist's provider selection decision.

---

## 5. JTBD Hierarchy

### Category: Working with Llama Stack

#### Main Job 1: Deploy a RAG-capable Llama Stack environment

**Job statement**: When I need to set up a RAG stack for my team, I want to deploy a LlamaStackDistribution instance with the right vector store backend, so I can provide data scientists with a working retrieval-augmented generation environment.

**Persona**: OpenShift Cluster Administrator

**Content journey phase**: Configure

**User Stories**:
- As a cluster admin, I want to deploy a LlamaStackDistribution with inline FAISS, so I can provide a lightweight RAG environment without external database dependencies.
- As a cluster admin, I want to understand which vector store to choose (Milvus inline, Milvus remote, FAISS, pgvector), so I can select the right backend for my workload requirements.
- As a cluster admin, I want to know the vLLM prerequisites for tool-calling, so my deployment supports RAG knowledge_search features.

#### Main Job 2: Build and test RAG workflows with Llama Stack

**Job statement**: When I have a deployed Llama Stack environment, I want to ingest documents and query them using the Llama Stack SDK, so I can build retrieval-augmented generation applications.

**Persona**: Data Scientist / AI Engineer

**Content journey phase**: Use

**User Stories**:
- As a data scientist, I want to understand what FAISS is and when to use it, so I can choose the right vector store for my experimentation needs.
- As a data scientist, I want to create a FAISS vector store and ingest content using the updated SDK API, so I can prototype RAG workflows without external dependencies.
- As a data scientist, I want to query ingested content using the Responses API with file_search, so I can retrieve relevant context for my LLM applications.
- As a data scientist, I want to prepare and ingest documents using the Docling pipeline with FAISS, so I can process structured documents for RAG retrieval.
- As a data scientist, I want to understand the SDK 0.3.1 API changes (extra_body, vector_store_id, Vector Store Files API), so I can update my existing notebooks and scripts.

+== Example C: LlamaStackDistribution with *Inline FAISS*
+
+Use this example to enable the inline FAISS vector store. This configuration stores vector data locally within the Llama Stack container using an embedded SQLite database.
+
+. In the OpenShift web console, select *Administrator* → *Quick Create* (image:images/quick-create-icon.png[]) → *Import YAML*, and create a CR similar to the following:
++
+[source,yaml]
+----
+apiVersion: llamastack.io/v1alpha1
+kind: LlamaStackDistribution
+metadata:
+  name: lsd-llama-faiss-inline
+spec:
+  replicas: 1
+  server:
+    containerSpec:
+      resources:
+        requests:
+          cpu: "250m"
+          memory: "500Mi"
+        limits:
+          cpu: "8"
+          memory: "12Gi"
+      env:
+        # vLLM inference model configuration
+        - name: INFERENCE_MODEL
+          valueFrom:
+            secretKeyRef:
+              name: llama-stack-inference-model-secret
+              key: INFERENCE_MODEL
+        - name: VLLM_URL
+          valueFrom:
+            secretKeyRef:
+              name: llama-stack-inference-model-secret
+              key: VLLM_URL
+        - name: VLLM_TLS_VERIFY
+          valueFrom:
+            secretKeyRef:
+              name: llama-stack-inference-model-secret
+              key: VLLM_TLS_VERIFY
+        - name: VLLM_API_TOKEN
+          valueFrom:
+            secretKeyRef:
+              name: llama-stack-inference-model-secret
+              key: VLLM_API_TOKEN
+
+        # Enable inline FAISS with SQLite backend
+        - name: ENABLE_FAISS
+          value: faiss
+        - name: FAISS_KVSTORE_DB_PATH
+          value: /opt/app-root/src/.llama/distributions/rh/sqlite_vec.db
+
+        # Recommended workarounds for SQLite accessibility and version check
+        - name: LLAMA_STACK_CONFIG_DIR
+          value: /opt/app-root/src/.llama/distributions/rh
+      name: llama-stack
+      port: 8321
+    distribution:
+      name: rh-dev
+----
+
+[NOTE]
+====
+The `FAISS_KVSTORE_DB_PATH` environment variable defines the local path where the FAISS SQLite backend stores its index data. Ensure that this directory exists and is writable inside the container. Inline FAISS is only suitable for experimental or testing use cases. 
+====
+
 . Click *Create*.

_modified/.agent_workspace/rhaieng-1550/requirements/requirements.md
# Documentation Requirements

**Source**: Document FAISS vector store integration for RHOAI 3.0 Llama Stack runtime
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Release/Sprint**: rhoai-3.0

## Summary

- Total requirements analyzed: 14
- New modules needed: 8
- Existing modules to update: 29
- Breaking changes requiring docs: 5

## Requirements by priority

### Critical

#### REQ-001: New FAISS vector store overview concept module
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-1550](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550) | [RHAISTRAT-80](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-80) | [PR #1046 (opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation)](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046) | [MR !2105 (downstream RHOAI docs)](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2105)
- **Summary**: RHOAI 3.0 introduces FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) as an inline, in-process vector store provider in the Llama Stack Distribution, complementing the existing Milvus options. A new concept module (overview-of-faiss-vector-databases.adoc) must be created to explain what inline FAISS is, how it stores embeddings locally via an embedded SQLite backend, its benefits (no external database dependency, reduced latency, simplified setup), and its limitations (single-node only, no HA, not for production scale). Additionally, the parent overview-of-vector-databases.adoc must be updated to list FAISS as a supported vector store, and procedural modules for deployment, ingestion, and querying must include FAISS as an 'Option 3' alongside inline and remote Milvus.
- **User impact**: Users deploying RAG workloads in RHOAI 3.0 can now choose FAISS as a lightweight, zero-dependency vector store for experimentation, disconnected environments, or single-node deployments. Without clear documentation, users may not discover this option, misconfigure it, or incorrectly use it in production scenarios where Milvus is more appropriate.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `TBD` (CONCEPT) The PR diff shows this module is 21 lines of AsciiDoc. The JIRA acceptance criteria specify the module should be included in the assembly at leveloffset=+2, nested under the existing overview-of-vector-databases section.
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (CONCEPT) The PR diff shows overview-of-vector-databases.adoc already updated with an 'Inline FAISS' bullet and a decision-guidance bullet. The Milvus overview module leveloffset also changed from +1 to +2 to accommodate FAISS as a sibling.

#### REQ-002: FAISS deployment example in LlamaStackDistribution CR
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-1550](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550) | [PR #1046 (opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation)](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046) | [MR !2105 (RHOAI downstream)](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2105)
- **Summary**: RHOAI 3.0 introduces inline FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) as a third vector store option alongside inline Milvus Lite and remote Milvus. The LlamaStackDistribution CR gains a new 'Example C' deployment configuration that enables FAISS with three environment variables: ENABLE_FAISS (set to 'faiss'), FAISS_KVSTORE_DB_PATH (SQLite database path), and LLAMA_STACK_CONFIG_DIR (config directory path). This feature provides a lightweight, in-process vector store with SQLite-based persistence that requires no external database service, making it suitable for experimental, testing, disconnected, and single-node RAG deployments.
- **User impact**: Users can now deploy a self-contained RAG stack without any external vector database dependency by choosing inline FAISS in their LlamaStackDistribution CR. This simplifies setup for experimental, testing, and disconnected environments, but users must understand that inline FAISS is not suitable for production workloads requiring distributed storage or high availability.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `TBD` (CONCEPT) New module: overview-of-faiss-vector-databases.adoc already drafted in PR #1046. Nested under the existing 'Overview of vector databases' section at leveloffset=+2.
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (PROCEDURE) Module: deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc. Also adds --enable-auto-tool-choice prerequisite and updates disconnected environment note.
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (PROCEDURE) Affects modules: ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model.adoc, querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model.adoc, preparing-documents-with-docling-for-llama-stack-retrieval.adoc. The API pattern changes (extra_body, vector_store_id) are required for all vector store options, not just FAISS.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can deploy a LlamaStackDistribution CR with inline FAISS by following the Example C YAML configuration
  - [ ] The ENABLE_FAISS, FAISS_KVSTORE_DB_PATH, and LLAMA_STACK_CONFIG_DIR environment variables are documented with their values and purpose
  - [ ] Users understand that inline FAISS is suitable only for experimental/testing use cases, not production workloads
  - [ ] Users can register a FAISS vector store using provider_id='faiss' in the Llama Stack SDK (Option 3 in ingestion and query procedures)
  - [ ] The overview of vector databases section lists inline FAISS as a supported option with decision guidance alongside inline Milvus Lite and remote Milvus
  - [ ] All SDK code examples use the updated Vector Store Files API (client.vector_stores.files.create) and llama_stack_client version 0.3.1
  - [ ] The FAISS overview concept module explains benefits (no external dependencies, local persistence, reduced latency, OpenAI-compatible API) and limitations (no distributed storage, no high availability)
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-1550 Description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550): Full acceptance criteria and documentation impact list for FAISS integration
  - [RHAIENG-1614](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1614): Linked spike ticket: Investigate FAISS vector store integration in RHOAI 3.0
  - [RHAISTRAT-80](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-80): Linked strategy ticket: Include FAISS VectorIO provider in Llama Stack distro (Tech Preview)
  - [PR #1046 diff - deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): Example C YAML with ENABLE_FAISS=faiss, FAISS_KVSTORE_DB_PATH, LLAMA_STACK_CONFIG_DIR env vars; CR name lsd-llama-faiss-inline
  - [PR #1046 diff - overview-of-faiss-vector-databases.adoc](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): New concept module explaining FAISS benefits, SQLite backend, and experimental-use limitation
  - [PR #1046 diff - ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model.adoc](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): Added FAISS as Option 3 in vector store registration; migrated to Vector Store Files API (client.vector_stores.files.create)
  - [PR #1046 diff - querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model.adoc](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): Added FAISS as Option 3; migrated to Responses API (client.responses.create) and vector_store_ids

#### REQ-007: Vector store creation API migration to extra_body pattern
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-1550](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550) | [PR #1046 (opendatahub-documentation)](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046)
- **Summary**: The Llama Stack SDK version 0.3.1 introduces a breaking change to the vector store creation API. The parameters embedding_model, embedding_dimension, and provider_id must now be passed inside an extra_body dictionary rather than as top-level keyword arguments to client.vector_stores.create(). This change affects all three RAG procedure modules (ingestion, query, and Docling) and applies to every provider option (inline Milvus, remote Milvus, and the new inline FAISS). Users following existing code examples with SDK 0.3.1 will encounter errors unless they adopt the new extra_body pattern.
- **User impact**: Users upgrading to llama_stack_client 0.3.1 or later will find that existing vector store creation code using top-level embedding_model, embedding_dimension, and provider_id parameters no longer works. All code examples in the ingestion, query, and Docling procedures must be updated to use the extra_body dict pattern, or users' RAG workflows will break at the vector store registration step.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (PROCEDURE) This is a cross-cutting change affecting three separate procedure modules, each with multiple code blocks. The old pattern (embedding_model=..., embedding_dimension=..., provider_id=...) must be replaced with extra_body={"embedding_model": ..., "embedding_dimension": ..., "provider_id": ...} in every instance.
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (REFERENCE) The extra_body pattern aligns with the OpenAI-compatible Vector Store API endpoints (/v1/openai/v1/vector_stores/). The change consolidates provider-specific parameters into a passthrough dict to maintain compatibility with the upstream OpenAI client interface.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can create a vector store for any supported provider (inline Milvus, remote Milvus, inline FAISS) using the extra_body dictionary pattern shown in the updated code examples
  - [ ] No code examples in the ingestion, query, or Docling procedures use the deprecated top-level parameter pattern (embedding_model=, embedding_dimension=, provider_id= as keyword arguments to client.vector_stores.create())
  - [ ] Each updated code example captures the server-assigned vector store ID from vector_store.id and uses it in subsequent API calls (ingestion, query, agent configuration)
  - [ ] The variable naming consistently uses vector_store_name for the user-chosen display name and vector_store_id for the server-returned identifier across all three procedures
  - [ ] Users can verify a successful vector store creation by printing vector_store_id after calling client.vector_stores.create() with extra_body
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-1550 Acceptance Criteria](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550): Ticket acceptance criteria specify FAISS integration documentation and API usage examples; the extra_body migration is part of the SDK API update scope
  - [PR #1046 diff: ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model.adoc](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): Lines 206-294 of the diff show the migration of all three vector store creation options from top-level params to extra_body, plus the new items-based ingestion API
  - [PR #1046 diff: querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model.adoc](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): Lines 703-963 of the diff show the same extra_body migration for vector store creation in the query procedure, plus the Responses API migration
  - [PR #1046 diff: preparing-documents-with-docling-for-llama-stack-retrieval.adoc](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): Lines 460-702 of the diff show the extra_body migration for vector store creation in the Docling pipeline procedure
  - [Published RHOAI 3.0 ingestion docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.0/html/working_with_llama_stack/deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project_rag#ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model_rag): Live published documentation showing the updated extra_body pattern in production
  - [Published RHOAI 3.0 query docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.0/html/working_with_llama_stack/deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project_rag#querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model_rag): Live published documentation showing the updated query patterns
  - [Published RHOAI 3.0 Docling docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.0/html/working_with_llama_stack/deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project_rag#preparing-documents-with-docling-for-llama-stack-retrieval_rag): Live published documentation showing the updated Docling pipeline with extra_body pattern

#### REQ-008: Ingestion API migration from RAGDocument to Vector Store Files API
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-1550](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550) | [ODH PR #1046](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046) | [RHOAI Downstream MR #2105](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2105)
- **Summary**: The ingestion procedure for Llama Stack RAG workflows undergoes a breaking API change in RHOAI 3.0. The previous pattern using RAGDocument objects and client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert() is replaced entirely by the Vector Store Files API using client.vector_stores.files.create() with an items list of dicts. This change affects how users create documents for ingestion, how they pass content to the vector store, and removes the dependency on the RAGDocument class import. The migration aligns Llama Stack with OpenAI-compatible API patterns, requires llama_stack_client version 0.3.1 or later (up from 0.2.22), and simplifies the ingestion workflow by reducing steps.
- **User impact**: Users who have existing Jupyter notebooks or scripts that use the RAGDocument class and client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert() for content ingestion must rewrite their ingestion code. The old API is removed — not deprecated — so existing code will break immediately upon upgrading to llama_stack_client 0.3.1. Users must also stop importing RAGDocument from llama_stack_client, restructure their document data as items dicts with id/text/mime_type/metadata keys, and call client.vector_stores.files.create() instead.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (PROCEDURE) This is the core breaking change. The diff shows the complete before/after transformation across 7 code blocks in the ingestion module.
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (PROCEDURE) The Docling procedure uses pipeline-based ingestion rather than direct SDK calls, but parameter names and verification steps still reference the new API.
  - [ ] Create `TBD` (REFERENCE) The PR diff does not include explicit migration guidance — this is a gap that should be addressed to help users transitioning from 0.2.x SDK versions.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can ingest raw text content into a vector store by constructing an items list of dicts with id, text, mime_type, and metadata keys, then calling client.vector_stores.files.create(vector_store_id=..., items=..., chunk_size_in_tokens=...)
  - [ ] Users can ingest HTML content from a URL by providing the URL as the text value in an items dict with mime_type set to text/html
  - [ ] The RAGDocument class is no longer referenced anywhere in the ingestion procedure — no import statement, no object instantiation
  - [ ] The client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert() method is no longer referenced anywhere in the ingestion procedure
  - [ ] The import statement shows only 'from llama_stack_client import LlamaStackClient' (RAGDocument removed from import)
  - [ ] The prerequisite states llama_stack_client version 0.3.1 or later (not 0.2.22)
  - [ ] The pip install step installs only llama_stack_client (fire dependency is removed)
  - [ ] Each code example in the ingestion procedure is copy-pasteable and uses consistent variable names (vector_store_id, not vector_db_id)
  - [ ] The ingestion result is captured in a variable and printed for user verification (result = client.vector_stores.files.create(...))
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-1550 Description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550): JIRA ticket specifies documenting FAISS with Vector Stores API (/v1/openai/v1/vector_stores/) and ingestion workflows
  - [PR #1046 diff - ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model.adoc](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): Lines 123-387 of the diff show the complete before/after transformation of the ingestion procedure: RAGDocument removal, items dict pattern introduction, and rag_tool.insert to vector_stores.files.create migration
  - [Published RHOAI 3.0 ingestion docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.0/html/working_with_llama_stack/deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project_rag#ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model_rag): Published documentation showing the final state of the ingestion procedure after migration
  - [PR #1046 diff - preparing-documents-with-docling.adoc](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): Lines 460-703 show Docling pipeline parameter renames (vector_db_id to vector_store_id) and API pattern updates

#### REQ-009: Query API migration from rag_tool.query to Responses API
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-1550](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550) | [ODH PR #1046](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046) | [RHOAI MR #2105](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2105)
- **Summary**: The Llama Stack SDK 0.3.1 introduces breaking API changes for RAG query and ingestion workflows in RHOAI 3.0. The low-level query API `client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.query()` is replaced by the OpenAI-compatible Responses API `client.responses.create()` with a `file_search` tool type and `vector_store_ids` parameter. The ingestion API `client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert()` with `RAGDocument` objects is replaced by `client.vector_stores.files.create()` with plain dict items. Vector store creation parameters move from keyword arguments to an `extra_body` dictionary, and all references to `vector_db_id`/`vector_db_ids` are renamed to `vector_store_id`/`vector_store_ids` throughout the SDK.
- **User impact**: Users following existing RAG procedures with llama_stack_client 0.2.x will encounter broken code when upgrading to 0.3.1 or deploying against RHOAI 3.0. Every code example in the ingestion, querying, and Docling pipeline procedures must be updated. Users must also learn the new Responses API pattern (file_search tool type) for querying instead of the deprecated rag_tool.query method.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (PROCEDURE) Affects querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model.adoc
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (PROCEDURE) Affects ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model.adoc and preparing-documents-with-docling-for-llama-stack-retrieval.adoc
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (REFERENCE) Useful for users migrating existing custom code that uses the old API patterns
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can query ingested content using client.responses.create() with file_search tool type and vector_store_ids parameter following the updated procedure
  - [ ] Users can ingest content using client.vector_stores.files.create() with items dicts following the updated procedure
  - [ ] All code examples use vector_store_id/vector_store_ids instead of vector_db_id/vector_db_ids
  - [ ] All code examples pass embedding_model, embedding_dimension, and provider_id inside the extra_body parameter when creating vector stores
  - [ ] The SDK version prerequisite is listed as 0.3.1 or later in all affected procedures
  - [ ] The deprecated rag_tool.query and rag_tool.insert APIs are no longer shown in any procedure
  - [ ] The RAGDocument import and usage is removed from ingestion procedures, replaced with plain dict items
  - [ ] Users can create an inline FAISS vector store as a third vector store option alongside inline Milvus and remote Milvus
  - [ ] The Agent API examples use vector_store_ids in the builtin::rag/knowledge_search tool args
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-1550](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550): Main ticket: Document FAISS vector store integration for RHOAI 3.0. Closed. Acceptance criteria specify new concept module, configuration examples, and verification steps.
  - [ODH PR #1046 diff](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046): 963-line diff showing complete API migration across 7 AsciiDoc files: assembly restructuring, FAISS concept module, ingestion API rewrite, querying API rewrite, Docling pipeline updates, and vector store overview updates.
  - [RHAIENG-1614](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1614): Linked spike ticket: Investigate FAISS vector store integration in RHOAI 3.0
  - [RHAISTRAT-80](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-80): Linked strategy ticket: Include FAISS VectorIO provider in llama stack distro (Tech Preview)
  - [Published RHOAI 3.0 querying docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.0/html/working_with_llama_stack/deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project_rag#querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model_rag): Live published documentation for the querying procedure in RHOAI 3.0
  - [Published RHOAI 3.0 ingestion docs](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.0/html/working_with_llama_stack/deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project_rag#ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model_rag): Live published documentation for the ingestion procedure in RHOAI 3.0

- **Source**: [RHAIENG-1550](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550) | [PR #1046 (opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation)](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/1046) | [MR !2105 (RHOAI downstream)](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2105)
- **Summary**: RHOAI 3.0 introduces FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) as a third vector store option alongside Inline Milvus Lite and Remote Milvus for RAG workloads in Llama Stack. The PR adds a new 'Example C: Inline FAISS (SQLite backend)' deployment configuration to the LlamaStackDistribution module, and adds 'Option 3: Inline FAISS' to the vector store creation steps in the ingesting-content, querying-content, and Docling pipeline procedures. A new concept module (overview-of-faiss-vector-databases.adoc) is also introduced, and the overview-of-vector-databases module is updated to include FAISS in the supported vector database list.
- **User impact**: Users deploying RAG workloads in RHOAI 3.0 now have a lightweight, in-process FAISS vector store option that requires no external database service. This is particularly useful for experimental, testing, disconnected environments, or single-node RAG deployments. Users must select the correct provider_id ('faiss') and set ENABLE_FAISS and FAISS_KVSTORE_DB_PATH environment variables in the LlamaStackDistribution CR.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `TBD` (CONCEPT) New file: overview-of-faiss-vector-databases.adoc. The PR already creates this module with 21 lines of content.
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (PROCEDURE) The PR changes are extensive: besides adding FAISS options, it updates the SDK version requirement from 0.2.22 to 0.3.1, changes API calls throughout (vector_db_id -> vector_store_id, extra_body pattern for store creation), and removes the fire dependency.
  - [ ] Update `TBD` (REFERENCE) The assembly-level include also changes: overview-of-milvus moves to leveloffset=+2 and overview-of-faiss is added at the same level, both nested under the parent overview-of-vector-databases.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can deploy a LlamaStackDistribution CR with inline FAISS by following Example C, which includes ENABLE_FAISS, FAISS_KVSTORE_DB_PATH, and LLAMA_STACK_CONFIG_DIR environment variables
  - [ ] Users can create a FAISS vector store in a Jupyter notebook using client.vector_stores.create() with provider_id='faiss' in the extra_body parameter
  - [ ] Users can ingest content into a FAISS vector store using the Vector Store Files API (client.vector_stores.files.create) following Option 3
  - [ ] Users can query content from a FAISS vector store using both the Responses API and the Agent API
  - [ ] The FAISS concept overview explains that inline FAISS is a local, in-process store unsuitable for production workloads requiring scalability or HA
  - [ ] The vector database overview module includes FAISS in the supported databases list with selection guidance alongside Inline Milvus and Remote Milvus
  - [ ] Users can run the Docling pipeline procedure with FAISS as the vector store by selecting Option 3
  - [ ] All code samples use llama_stack_client version 0.3.1 or later and the updated Vector Store API (not the deprecated RAGDocument/rag_tool API)
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-1550 Description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550): Full acceptance criteria and documentation impact list from the JIRA ticket
  - [RHAIENG-1550 AC](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1550): Acceptance criteria specify: new AsciiDoc module, overview of FAISS, config parameters, example YAML, verification section, note about local/in-process nature

## Technical Review -- RHAIENG-1550: Llama Stack SDK 0.3.1 Migration and FAISS Documentation

**Reviewed files:**
1. `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc` -- new reference module
2. `overview-of-faiss-vector-databases.adoc` -- updated concept module
3. `deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project.adoc` -- updated assembly

**Doc types detected:** Reference, Concept, Assembly
**Reviewer lens applied:** Both (Developer for reference/procedures, Architect for concept/assembly)
**Overall technical confidence:** MEDIUM -- New SDK 0.3.1 API patterns are well-corroborated by the source repository (26/42 claims supported). Old SDK 0.2.x patterns correctly reflect removed code and are appropriately labeled. However, the migration reference has a table-vs-code inconsistency, the assembly diverges structurally from the source repo, and verification/failure guidance is absent from migration examples.

---

### Critical issues (must fix before publication)

**C1. Migration reference summary table contradicts the detailed code block for old vector store creation**

- **Location:** `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc`, line 22, summary table "Old API pattern (SDK 0.2.x)" column
- **Issue:** The table states the old pattern is `client.vector_dbs.register(vector_db_id=..., embedding_model=..., provider_id=...)`. However, the detailed code block at lines 53-58 shows `client.vector_dbs.register(vector_db_id=..., embedding_model=..., embedding_dimension=..., provider_id=...)`. The table omits the `embedding_dimension` parameter that is present in the code example. While this is a table summary, the omission of a required parameter could cause a developer searching for code patterns to miss a parameter during migration.
- **Impact:** A developer using the table as a find-and-replace guide may not realize `embedding_dimension` was also a parameter in the old API and needs to be moved into `extra_body` in the new API.
- **Suggestion:** Add `embedding_dimension=...` to the table cell for the old pattern, or add an ellipsis that makes clear the table is a summary: `client.vector_dbs.register(vector_db_id=..., embedding_model=..., ...)`.

**C2. Assembly `[id]` attribute is missing the `_{context}` suffix**

- **Location:** `deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project.adoc`, line 5
- **Issue:** The draft uses `[id="deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project"]` without the `_{context}` suffix. The source repository version uses `[id="deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project_{context}"]`. This assembly is included within `llama-stack-adv-examples.adoc` at `leveloffset=+1`, which means the context mechanism is needed to avoid anchor ID collisions.
- **Impact:** Duplicate IDs will cause Asciidoctor build warnings and broken cross-references when this assembly is included in another assembly.
- **Suggestion:** Change to `[id="deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project_{context}"]` to match the source repo convention.

**C3. Assembly include paths use `upstream-modules/` -- verify against build system**

- **Location:** `deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project.adoc`, lines 40-52
- **Issue:** All include directives use `include::upstream-modules/` paths, while the source repository version uses `include::modules/` paths. If the `upstream-modules/` path is only valid in the downstream self-managed worktree and does not resolve in all build contexts, includes will fail.
- **Impact:** Build failure if the path does not resolve in the target build environment.
- **Suggestion:** Confirm with the build engineer that `upstream-modules/` is the correct include path for the downstream self-managed build variant. If this draft will be merged into the upstream repo, the paths must use `modules/`.

---

### Significant issues (should fix)

**S1. Assembly is missing Qdrant and pgvector vector database overview includes**

- **Location:** `deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project.adoc`, between lines 43-44
- **Issue:** The source repo assembly includes four vector database overview modules (`overview-of-milvus-vector-databases`, `overview-of-qdrant-vector-databases`, `overview-of-faiss-vector-databases`, `overview-of-pgvector-vector-databases`). The draft only includes Milvus and FAISS. The migration reference and ingestion/querying procedures reference pgvector as a valid provider (`provider_id: "pgvector"`), but the assembly provides no overview of it.
- **Impact:** Readers choosing pgvector or Qdrant have no architectural overview in this assembly. The procedures offer pgvector as "Option 4" but the assembly does not introduce it.
- **Suggestion:** Add the missing includes or confirm with the doc owner that their omission from the downstream variant is intentional.

**S2. Migration reference: vague internal cross-reference**

- **Location:** `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc`, line 180
- **Issue:** The text says "For a more detailed example, see the querying procedure in this guide." This does not use an `xref:` directive and "this guide" is ambiguous -- it could mean the migration reference, the parent assembly, or the entire RAG deployment guide.
- **Impact:** Reader cannot navigate to the referenced procedure.
- **Suggestion:** Replace with an explicit AsciiDoc cross-reference: `xref:querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model_{context}[the querying procedure]`.

**S3. Migration reference: no verification steps for any migrated code pattern**

- **Location:** `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc`, all "New pattern" code blocks
- **Issue:** None of the new SDK 0.3.1 code blocks include verification steps, expected output, or success/failure indicators. The vector store creation pattern (lines 64-72) returns a `vector_store` object but does not show how to verify it was created. The ingestion pattern (lines 107-126) returns `vector_store_file` with no verification. The querying pattern (lines 157-169) prints `response.output_text` with no expected output.
- **Impact:** A developer performing migration cannot distinguish between successful migration and silent failures. This is especially important because the migration involves breaking changes.
- **Suggestion:** Add brief verification guidance after each new pattern block. For example: "Verify that `vector_store.id` returns a non-empty string" or "The `response.output_text` should contain a model-generated answer incorporating retrieved context."

**S4. Migration reference: URL-to-local-file migration path is mentioned but not demonstrated**

- **Location:** `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc`, lines 132-134
- **Issue:** The doc correctly notes that "URL-based document references...are no longer directly supported" and that developers "must download the file to local storage before uploading." However, it provides no code example for this download step. The source repo's ingestion procedure (`ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model.adoc`, lines 169-178) demonstrates the full download-then-upload pattern using `requests.get()`.
- **Impact:** Developers whose existing code uses URL-based ingestion (the old pattern's `content="https://..."`) lack a concrete migration example for the download step.
- **Suggestion:** Add a brief code snippet showing the download step, or add an explicit cross-reference to the ingestion procedure which demonstrates the full pattern.

**S5. Migration reference: `chunk_overlap_tokens: 400` with `max_chunk_size_tokens: 800` is a 50% overlap**

- **Location:** `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc`, lines 118-124
- **Issue:** The example uses 50% chunk overlap, which is unusually high. The source repo's OpenAI-compatible API example (`openai-compatible-apis-in-llama-stack.adoc`, line 243) uses `max_chunk_size_tokens: 700` and `chunk_overlap_tokens: 100` (~14% overlap), which is more typical. The doc mentions to "Tune the `chunk_overlap_tokens` value based on your use case" (line 136) but does not indicate that 400 is an aggressive setting.
- **Impact:** Developers who copy-paste this example may create unnecessarily large vector indexes, increasing storage costs and query latency.
- **Suggestion:** Either reduce the example overlap to a more typical value (e.g., 100-200) or add a note explaining that 400 is a high overlap value chosen to maximize retrieval quality at the cost of index size.

**S6. FAISS overview: no guidance on data persistence across container restarts**

- **Location:** `overview-of-faiss-vector-databases.adoc`, lines 20-23
- **Issue:** The doc states PostgreSQL is the default metadata backend but does not explain what happens to FAISS indexes when the Llama Stack container restarts. Since FAISS is described as "in-process" and "embedded," an architect needs to know whether the indexes survive container restarts (reconstructed from PostgreSQL) or are lost.
- **Impact:** Architects may choose FAISS without understanding the restart/recovery characteristics, leading to unexpected data loss during routine container lifecycle events.
- **Suggestion:** Add a sentence clarifying persistence behavior: e.g., "When the Llama Stack server container restarts, FAISS indexes are reconstructed from the PostgreSQL metadata store" (if true), or explain the recovery behavior.

---

### Minor issues (consider fixing)

**M1. Migration reference: SDK installation code blocks use `[source,python]` for `%pip` commands**

- **Location:** `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc`, lines 204-208 and 211-213
- **Issue:** The `%pip install` commands are annotated as `[source,python]` but `%pip` is a Jupyter magic command, not standard Python. The doc correctly notes this at line 217 ("The `%pip` command is a Jupyter notebook magic command"), but the language annotation is still misleading.
- **Impact:** Syntax highlighting will be incorrect; a developer copying into a Python script will get a NameError.
- **Suggestion:** Use `[source,bash]` or `[source,text]` for the install code blocks to avoid implying these are Python statements.

**M2. Migration reference: does not specify which Llama Stack server version requires SDK 0.3.1**

- **Location:** `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc`, entire document
- **Issue:** The document specifies the SDK version (0.3.1) but not the corresponding Llama Stack server version. A developer using an older server with the new SDK will encounter API incompatibilities.
- **Impact:** Users may update the SDK without updating their server, causing runtime errors.
- **Suggestion:** Add a note about the minimum Llama Stack server version compatible with SDK 0.3.1, or cross-reference the release notes.

**M3. Migration reference: old pattern's `chunk_size_in_tokens` has no overlap equivalent**

- **Location:** `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc`, lines 100-101
- **Issue:** The old pattern shows `chunk_size_in_tokens=800` but no overlap parameter. The new pattern introduces `chunk_overlap_tokens`. The doc does not clarify whether overlap is new functionality in 0.3.1 or was previously unavailable.
- **Impact:** Developers cannot determine whether `chunk_overlap_tokens` is a new feature or a renamed parameter.
- **Suggestion:** Add a note indicating whether chunk overlap control is new in 0.3.1.

**M4. FAISS overview: hardcoded version reference "{productname-short} 3.2"**

- **Location:** `overview-of-faiss-vector-databases.adoc`, line 20
- **Issue:** The version "3.2" is hardcoded rather than using a version attribute like `{vernum}`. If the version changes, this requires manual update.
- **Impact:** Stale version number if not updated during release cycle.
- **Suggestion:** Consider using `{vernum}` if this tracks the current release version, or keep hardcoded if this refers specifically to the version that introduced the feature.

**M5. FAISS overview: cross-reference link target anchor may not exist**

- **Location:** `overview-of-faiss-vector-databases.adoc`, lines 38-42
- **Issue:** The cross-reference targets `example_c_llamastackdistribution_with_inline_faiss`. This anchor needs to exist in the target assembly. If the example section was renamed or removed, the link will be broken.
- **Impact:** Broken link leading to a 404 or anchor-not-found error.
- **Suggestion:** Verify the target anchor exists in the current version of the linked assembly.

---

### SME verification needed

**SME1. Confirm `chunking_strategy` parameter structure against SDK 0.3.1 API**

- **Location:** `llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference.adoc`, lines 118-124

#!/bin/bash
# workflow-completion-check.sh
#
# Stop hook: blocks Claude from stopping while the ACTIVE workflow
# is still running. Only checks the workflow identified by the
# .active-workflow marker — stale workflows from other sessions
# are ignored.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 = allow stop
#   2 = block stop (reason sent to stderr)
#
# Requires: jq

set -u

INPUT=$(cat)

if ! cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Cannot access project directory; cannot verify workflow status." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Look for progress files
shopt -s nullglob
PROGRESS_FILES=(.agent_workspace/*/workflow/*.json)
shopt -u nullglob
if [ ${#PROGRESS_FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

MARKER=".agent_workspace/.active-workflow"

# No marker file → no active workflow → allow stop
if [ ! -f "$MARKER" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Read the marker — fail closed on parse errors
PROGRESS_FILE=$(jq -r '.progress_file // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_PF=$?
TICKET=$(jq -r '.ticket // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_TK=$?

if [ "$JQ_RC_PF" -ne 0 ] || [ "$JQ_RC_TK" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Failed to parse $MARKER; refusing to stop (fail closed)." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Marker parsed successfully but fields are empty → stale marker → clean up
if [ -z "$PROGRESS_FILE" ] || [ -z "$TICKET" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Progress file doesn't exist → stale marker → clean up and allow stop
if [ ! -f "$PROGRESS_FILE" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Check the workflow status — only block for in_progress workflows
WORKFLOW_STATUS=$(jq -r '.status' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ "$WORKFLOW_STATUS" != "in_progress" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

WORKFLOW_TYPE=$(jq -r '.workflow_type' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

# Anti-loop guard: per-workflow counter prevents infinite blocking
COUNTER_FILE="${PROGRESS_FILE}.stop_count"
if [ -f "$COUNTER_FILE" ]; then
  COUNT=$(cat "$COUNTER_FILE")
else
  COUNT=0
fi
if [ "$COUNT" -ge 5 ]; then
  rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Get step order from the progress file
mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.step_order[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#STEP_ORDER[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.steps | keys[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
fi

# Find the first incomplete step
NEXT_STEP=""
for step in "${STEP_ORDER[@]}"; do
  STEP_STATUS=$(jq -r --arg s "$step" '.steps[$s].status // "missing"' "$PROGRESS_FILE")
  case "$STEP_STATUS" in
    completed|skipped|deferred) continue ;;
    *) NEXT_STEP="$step"; break ;;
  esac
done

if [ -n "$NEXT_STEP" ]; then
  echo "$((COUNT + 1))" > "$COUNTER_FILE"
  echo "Documentation workflow '$WORKFLOW_TYPE' for $TICKET is not complete. Next step: $NEXT_STEP. Continue the workflow." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# All steps done — clean up and allow stop
rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
rm -f "$MARKER"
exit 0

[id="deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database_{context}"]
= Deploy a remote Milvus vector database

[role="_abstract"]
To use Milvus as a remote vector database provider for Llama Stack in {productname-short}, you must deploy Milvus and its required etcd service in your OpenShift project.
You can deploy Milvus as a standalone server without the Milvus Operator.

:feature-name: Remote Milvus vector database support
include::snippets/technology-preview.adoc[]

[NOTE]
====
The following example configuration is intended for testing or evaluation environments.
For production-grade deployments, see the link:https://milvus.io/docs[Milvus documentation^].
====

.Prerequisites
* {openshift-platform} {ocp-minimum-version} or later is installed.
* You have cluster administrator privileges for your {openshift-platform} cluster.
* You are logged in to {productname-long}.
* A `StorageClass` that can provision persistent volumes is available.
* The Milvus container image `milvusdb/milvus:v2.6.0` is accessible from your cluster. If you are using a disconnected environment, mirror the image to your private registry.
* You have created a root password to secure your Milvus service.
* You have deployed an inference model with vLLM, for example, the llama-3.2-3b-instruct model, and you have selected *Make deployed models available through an external route* and *Require token authentication* during model deployment.
* You have the correct inference model identifier, for example, `llama-3-2-3b`.
* You have the model endpoint URL, ending with `/v1`, such as `\https://llama-32-3b-instruct-predictor:8443/v1`.
* You have the API token required to access the model endpoint.
* The OpenShift command-line interface (`oc`) is installed, as described in link:https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/{ocp-latest-version}/html/cli_tools/openshift-cli-oc#installing-openshift-cli[Installing the OpenShift CLI^].

.Procedure
. In the {openshift-platform} console, click the *Quick Create* (image:images/quick-create-icon.png[Quick Create]) icon and then click the *Import YAML* option.
. Verify that your project is the selected project.
. In the *Import YAML* editor, paste the following manifest and click *Create*:
+
[source,yaml]
----
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: milvus-secret
type: Opaque
stringData:
  root-password: "<your_milvus_root_password>" <1>
---
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: milvus-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  # storageClassName: <your_storage_class> <2>
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
  volumeMode: Filesystem
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: etcd-deployment
  labels:
    app: etcd
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: etcd
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: etcd
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: etcd
          image: quay.io/coreos/etcd:v3.5.5
          command:
            - etcd
            - --advertise-client-urls=http://127.0.0.1:2379
            - --listen-client-urls=http://0.0.0.0:2379
            - --data-dir=/etcd
          ports:
            - containerPort: 2379
          volumeMounts:
            - name: etcd-data
              mountPath: /etcd
          env:
            - name: ETCD_AUTO_COMPACTION_MODE
              value: revision
            - name: ETCD_AUTO_COMPACTION_RETENTION
              value: "1000"
            - name: ETCD_QUOTA_BACKEND_BYTES
              value: "4294967296"
            - name: ETCD_SNAPSHOT_COUNT
              value: "50000"
      volumes:
        - name: etcd-data
          emptyDir: {}
      restartPolicy: Always
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: etcd-service
spec:
  ports:
    - port: 2379
      targetPort: 2379
  selector:
    app: etcd
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: milvus-standalone
  name: milvus-standalone
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: milvus-standalone
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: milvus-standalone
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: milvus-standalone
          image: milvusdb/milvus:v2.6.0
          args: ["milvus", "run", "standalone"]
          env:
            - name: DEPLOY_MODE
              value: standalone
            - name: ETCD_ENDPOINTS
              value: etcd-service:2379
            - name: COMMON_STORAGETYPE
              value: local
            - name: MILVUS_ROOT_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: milvus-secret
                  key: root-password
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 9091
            initialDelaySeconds: 90
            periodSeconds: 30
            timeoutSeconds: 20
            failureThreshold: 5
          ports:
            - containerPort: 19530
              protocol: TCP
            - containerPort: 9091
              protocol: TCP
          volumeMounts:
            - name: milvus-data
              mountPath: /var/lib/milvus
      restartPolicy: Always
      volumes:
        - name: milvus-data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: milvus-pvc
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: milvus-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: milvus-standalone
  ports:
    - name: grpc
      port: 19530
      targetPort: 19530
    - name: http
      port: 9091
      targetPort: 9091
----
+
<1> Replace `<your_milvus_root_password>` with a strong, unique password. Do not use the example value in production or testing environments.
<2> Optional: Uncomment and set `storageClassName` if your cluster does not have a default `StorageClass` or if you want to use a specific `StorageClass`.
+
[WARNING]
====
The etcd deployment uses ephemeral storage (`emptyDir`). Restarting the etcd pod deletes all Milvus metadata (collection state, indexes). For durable etcd storage, mount a PersistentVolumeClaim for the etcd data directory.
====
+
[NOTE]
====
* Use the gRPC port (`19530`) for the `MILVUS_ENDPOINT` setting in Llama Stack.
* The HTTP port (`9091`) is reserved for health checks.
* If you deploy Milvus in a different namespace, use the fully qualified service name in your Llama Stack configuration. For example:

:_mod-docs-content-type: CONCEPT

[id="overview-of-milvus-vector-databases_{context}"]
= Overview of Milvus vector databases

[role="_abstract"]
Milvus is an open source vector database designed for high-performance similarity search across large volumes of embedding data.
You can use Milvus as a vector store provider for Llama Stack in {productname-short} to run retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workloads that require efficient vector indexing, scalable search, and durable storage.

:feature-name: Remote Milvus vector database support
include::snippets/technology-preview.adoc[]

Production-grade Llama Stack deployments default to PostgreSQL for metadata persistence.
When Milvus is used as the vector store, PostgreSQL is typically used for Llama Stack metadata, while Milvus manages vector indexes and similarity search.

Milvus vector databases provide the following capabilities in {productname-short}:

* High-performance similarity search using Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms
* Efficient indexing and query optimization for dense embeddings
* Persistent storage of vector data
* Integration with Llama Stack through an OpenAI-compatible Vector Stores API

In a typical RAG workflow in {productname-short}, the following responsibilities are separated:

* *Embedding generation*
+
Embeddings are generated by the configured embedding provider.
Remote embedding models are the recommended and default option for production deployments.

* *Vector storage and retrieval*
+
Milvus stores embedding vectors and performs similarity search operations.

* *Metadata persistence*
+
Llama Stack stores vector store metadata, file references, and configuration state by using PostgreSQL in production deployments.

* *Llama Stack server*
+
Coordinates ingestion, retrieval, and model inference through a unified API surface.

In {productname-short}, Milvus can be used in the following operational modes:

* *Inline Milvus Lite*
+
Runs embedded within the Llama Stack Distribution pod.
Inline Milvus Lite is intended for experimentation, development, or small datasets.
It does not provide high availability or horizontal scalability and is not recommended for production use.

[NOTE]
====
The `ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS` environment variable is required to enable the `inline::milvus` provider.
Omitting it disables the inline Milvus vector store.
For configuration details, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag#deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance_rag[Deploying a LlamaStackDistribution instance].
====

* *Remote Milvus*
+
Runs as a standalone service within your {openshift-platform} project or as an external managed Milvus deployment.
Remote Milvus is recommended for production-grade RAG workloads.

A remote Milvus deployment typically includes the following components:

* A *Milvus service* that exposes a gRPC endpoint (port 19530) for client traffic
* An *etcd service* that Milvus uses for metadata coordination, collection state, and index management
* *Persistent storage* for durable vector data

Milvus requires a dedicated etcd instance for metadata coordination, even when running as a standalone server.
Do not use the OpenShift control plane etcd for this purpose.
For more information about etcd, see link:https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/{ocp-latest-version}/html/etcd/index[Providing redundancy with etcd^].

[IMPORTANT]
====
You must deploy a dedicated etcd service for Milvus or connect Milvus to an external etcd instance.
Do not share the OpenShift control plane etcd with application workloads.
====

Use *Remote Milvus* when you require scalable vector search, high-performance retrieval, and integration with production-grade Llama Stack deployments in {productname-short}.

For instructions on deploying Milvus as a remote vector database, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag#deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database_rag[Deploying a remote Milvus vector database].
