**Release**: rhoai-2.25 (content updated through 3.4)
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Output format**: AsciiDoc (adoc)
**Status**: Documentation already merged; plan covers verification, gap remediation, and quality improvements

---

## 1. Requirements summary

Six requirements were analyzed, all originating from RHAIENG-653 and its parent/linked tickets (RHAIENG-55, RHAISTRAT-13, RHAIENG-871, RHAIENG-1568). The requirements cover documenting Milvus Remote as a vector database provider for Llama Stack RAG workloads on OpenShift AI.

| ID | Title | Priority | Impact grade | Evidence status |
|----|-------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| REQ-001 | Document Milvus Remote overview in Llama Stack Operator | High | High | Grounded (score: 1.0044) |
| REQ-002 | Step-by-step procedure for enabling Milvus Remote on OpenShift | Critical | High | Grounded (score: 0.8773) |
| REQ-003 | Configuration examples for remote:milvus with remote:vllm distribution | Critical | High | Grounded (score: 0.8989) |
| REQ-004 | RAG chatbot setup example using Milvus Remote | High | High | Grounded (score: 0.6382) |
| REQ-005 | Prerequisites and limitations for Milvus Remote | High | Medium | Grounded (score: 1.0656) |
| REQ-006 | Technology Preview designation for Milvus Remote RAG feature | High | Medium | Grounded (score: 0.818) |

All six requirements are **grounded** in code evidence. No requirements are partial or absent.

### Requirement factual summaries

**REQ-001 (High)**: The Llama Stack Operator now supports remote Milvus as a vector database provider for production-grade RAG workloads. Requires a CONCEPT module explaining inline vs remote Milvus modes, a PROCEDURE for deploying standalone Milvus with etcd, and updates to the LlamaStackDistribution deployment procedure (Example B). All three modules already exist in the codebase.

**REQ-002 (Critical)**: Step-by-step procedure for deploying Milvus as a remote vector database on OpenShift, including Kubernetes manifests for Secret, PVC, etcd Deployment/Service, Milvus Deployment/Service. Also requires updates to ingestion and querying procedures to include remote Milvus as a vector store option. All content already implemented and merged.

**REQ-003 (Critical)**: Configuration examples pairing remote:milvus with remote:vllm in a LlamaStackDistribution CR. Includes Example B with MILVUS_ENDPOINT, MILVUS_TOKEN, MILVUS_CONSISTENCY_LEVEL via secrets. Also Example D for remote pgvector. Content already implemented.

**REQ-004 (High)**: End-to-end RAG chatbot setup using Milvus Remote, including deployment, ingestion with provider_id "milvus-remote", and querying. Also adds BEIR benchmarking scripts supporting inline and remote vector database backends. Content already implemented.

**REQ-005 (High)**: Prerequisites (OpenShift 4.19+, GPU, cluster admin, StorageClass, dedicated etcd, PostgreSQL, MILVUS_ENDPOINT) and limitations (Technology Preview, not on IBM Z, standalone only, gRPC 19530, evaluation-only configs). Content exists across multiple modules.

**REQ-006 (High)**: Technology Preview designation for Milvus Remote RAG. The TP admonition exists at the assembly level in `deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project.adoc` and in the Llama Stack overview. Individual modules lack explicit TP admonitions, relying on assembly-level inheritance. The provider support table lists TP status for both `inline::milvus` and `remote::milvus`.

| Requirement | Impact grade | Rationale |
|-------------|-------------|-----------|
| REQ-001 | High | New capability (remote Milvus) with conceptual overview, new architecture pattern, and deployment procedure |
| REQ-002 | High | New PROCEDURE with complete Kubernetes manifests, new workflow for deploying standalone Milvus with etcd |
| REQ-003 | High | New deployment configuration example (Example B) with secrets-based environment variable configuration |
| REQ-004 | High | New end-to-end RAG workflow path with remote Milvus, plus BEIR benchmarking integration |

| REQ-006 | Medium | Technology Preview annotation update: compliance check on TP admonitions across modules |

All six requirements have documentation impact and proceed to planning.

## 3. Relationship analysis

| Pair | Relationship | Notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| REQ-001 / REQ-002 | Complementary | REQ-001 is the conceptual overview; REQ-002 is the step-by-step procedure. Both create the same two new modules. |
| REQ-001 / REQ-003 | Complementary | REQ-001 covers architecture concepts; REQ-003 covers CR configuration examples. |
| REQ-002 / REQ-003 | Sequential | Milvus deployment (REQ-002) must precede LSD configuration (REQ-003). |
| REQ-002 / REQ-004 | Sequential | Milvus deployment (REQ-002) precedes RAG chatbot setup (REQ-004). |
| REQ-003 / REQ-004 | Sequential | LSD configuration (REQ-003) precedes ingestion/querying (REQ-004). |
| REQ-005 / REQ-001..004 | Overlapping | Prerequisites and limitations content spans all four preceding requirements. |
| REQ-006 / REQ-001..005 | Overlapping | TP designation applies to all Milvus Remote content. |

### Theme clusters

**Cluster 1: Milvus Remote Core Documentation**
- Summary: New concept and procedure modules for deploying and understanding remote Milvus as a vector database provider.
- Issues: REQ-001, REQ-002
- Overlap risk: High (both requirements produce the same two new modules)
- Recommended ownership: Assembly `deploying-a-rag-stack-in-a-project.adoc`

**Cluster 2: LlamaStackDistribution Configuration**
- Summary: CR configuration examples with remote Milvus, secrets management, and environment variable setup.
- Issues: REQ-003
- Overlap risk: Medium (overlaps with REQ-002 deployment procedure for secret creation)
- Recommended ownership: Module `deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc`

**Cluster 3: End-to-End RAG Workflow**
- Summary: Ingestion and querying procedures with remote Milvus as a vector store option, plus BEIR benchmarking.
- Issues: REQ-004
- Overlap risk: Low
- Recommended ownership: Modules `ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model.adoc` and `querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model.adoc`

**Cluster 4: Compliance and Governance**
- Summary: Prerequisites, limitations, and Technology Preview designations across all Milvus Remote content.
- Issues: REQ-005, REQ-006
- Overlap risk: Medium (TP status and prerequisites appear in multiple modules)
- Recommended ownership: Cross-cutting; applies to all modules in Clusters 1-3

## 4. JTBD analysis

### Personas

1. **Cluster Administrator (SysAdmin)**: Responsible for deploying and configuring infrastructure components on OpenShift, including operators, vector databases, and LlamaStackDistribution instances.
2. **Data Scientist / AI Engineer (Developer)**: Uses deployed RAG infrastructure via Jupyter notebooks and the Llama Stack SDK to ingest data, create vector stores, and query for contextual AI responses.

### Job statements

**Job 1 (Cluster Administrator)**:
_When I need to provide production-grade vector search infrastructure for AI teams building RAG applications, I want to deploy and configure a remote Milvus vector database with the Llama Stack Operator on OpenShift AI, so I can offer scalable, durable, and high-performance vector storage that meets enterprise requirements._

- JTBD Category: Configure / Administer
- Content journey phase: Adoption (deploying a new capability)
- Main Job: Deploy a RAG stack in a project

**Job 2 (Data Scientist / AI Engineer)**:
_When I am building a RAG-based AI application and need scalable vector search for production workloads, I want to create vector stores using the remote Milvus provider through the Llama Stack SDK, so I can ingest documents and retrieve contextually relevant content with production-grade performance and durability._

- JTBD Category: Develop / Use
- Content journey phase: Adoption (using a new capability)
- Main Job: Build RAG applications with Llama Stack

**Job 3 (Cluster Administrator)**:
_When I am evaluating whether to deploy Milvus Remote for my RAG workloads, I want to understand the prerequisites, limitations, platform constraints, and Technology Preview support scope, so I can make an informed deployment decision and set correct expectations with my teams._

- JTBD Category: Evaluate / Plan
- Content journey phase: Evaluation (assessing capability fit)
- Main Job: Assess RAG infrastructure options

### JTBD hierarchy

```
Category: Working with Llama Stack
└── Main Job: Deploy a RAG stack in a project
    ├── User Story (Admin): Understand Milvus vector database options
    │   └── Module: overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc [CONCEPT]
    ├── User Story (Admin): Deploy a remote Milvus vector database
    │   └── Module: deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc [PROCEDURE]
    ├── User Story (Admin): Deploy a LlamaStackDistribution with remote Milvus

    ├── User Story (Admin): Understand prerequisites and limitations
    │   └── Covered within: deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc [prerequisites section]
    │   └── Covered within: overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc [limitations section]
    │   └── Covered within: llama-stack-providers-support.adoc [REFERENCE]
    └── User Story (Admin): Verify Technology Preview support scope
        └── Covered within: assembly TP admonition + overview-of-llama-stack.adoc

Category: Working with Llama Stack

    │   └── Module: ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model.adoc [PROCEDURE] (Option 2)
    ├── User Story (Developer): Query ingested content using remote Milvus
```

Note: No new parent topics are needed. All content fits within the existing "Working with Llama Stack" section, specifically under the "Deploying a RAG stack in a project" assembly. This avoids topic proliferation.

All existing modules reflect the current state of the codebase (through version 3.4). The requirements note that content was originally delivered for RHOAI 2.25 and has been updated. Milvus version v2.6.0 is current in the deployment manifests.

# Documentation Requirements

**Source**: Document Milvus Remote enablement in Llama Stack Operator for RAG chatbot setup on RHOAI
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Release/Sprint**: rhoai-2.25

## Summary

- Total requirements analyzed: 6
- New modules needed: 8
- Existing modules to update: 10
- Breaking changes requiring docs: 0

## Requirements by priority

### Critical

#### REQ-002: Step-by-step procedure for enabling Milvus Remote on OpenShift
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-653](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-653) | [MR !1939](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/1939) | [MR !1940](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/1940) | [ODH PR #982](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/982)
- **Summary**: This requirement covers documenting how a cluster administrator enables and deploys Milvus as a remote vector database provider for Llama Stack on Red Hat OpenShift AI. The documentation introduces a new PROCEDURE module for deploying standalone Milvus with etcd on OpenShift (including Kubernetes manifests for Secret, PVC, etcd Deployment/Service, Milvus Deployment/Service), new CONCEPT modules explaining Milvus and vector database options, a new LlamaStackDistribution deployment example (Example B) showing remote Milvus configuration with MILVUS_ENDPOINT/MILVUS_TOKEN environment variables, and updates to the ingestion and querying procedures to include remote Milvus as a vector store option alongside inline Milvus, inline FAISS, and pgvector.
- **User impact**: Cluster administrators gain a documented, production-recommended path for deploying Milvus as a scalable remote vector database for RAG workloads, replacing the development-only inline Milvus option. Data scientists and AI engineers can then use remote Milvus through the Llama Stack SDK for ingestion and querying with improved performance, durability, and scalability.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc` (PROCEDURE) — Step-by-step procedure for deploying a remote Milvus vector database on OpenShift, including etcd deployment, PVC provisioning, Milvus standalone deployment with Kubernetes manifests, service exposure on gRPC port 19530, and verification steps. Module already exists at modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc with complete YAML manifests, prerequisites, and verification.
  - [ ] Create `modules/overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc` (CONCEPT) — Overview of Milvus vector databases in OpenShift AI explaining inline Milvus Lite vs remote Milvus operational modes, architecture components (Milvus service, etcd, persistent storage), production guidance, and the requirement for a dedicated etcd instance. Module exists at modules/overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc and modules/overview-of-vector-databases.adoc covering all four vector store options.
  - [ ] Update `modules/deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc` (PROCEDURE) — Update the LlamaStackDistribution deployment procedure to include Example B (Remote Milvus with inline sentence-transformers embeddings) showing milvus-secret creation with MILVUS_ENDPOINT, MILVUS_TOKEN, MILVUS_CONSISTENCY_LEVEL and the corresponding LlamaStackDistribution CR configuration; also update ingestion and querying procedures to include remote Milvus as a vector store option with provider_id 'milvus-remote'. Updates exist in deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc (Example B), ingesting-content-into-a-llama-model.adoc (Option 2), and querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model.adoc (Option 2).
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can deploy a standalone remote Milvus vector database on OpenShift by following the documented procedure with provided Kubernetes manifests for Secret, PVC, etcd, and Milvus deployments
  - [ ] Users can verify the Milvus deployment by checking pod status, service endpoints, and health check output as described in the verification section
  - [ ] Users can create a milvus-secret with MILVUS_ENDPOINT (gRPC port 19530), MILVUS_TOKEN, and MILVUS_CONSISTENCY_LEVEL and reference it from a LlamaStackDistribution custom resource
  - [ ] Users can deploy a LlamaStackDistribution with remote Milvus using the documented Example B CR configuration
  - [ ] Users can create a remote Milvus vector store from a Jupyter notebook using provider_id 'milvus-remote' in the ingestion and querying procedures
  - [ ] Documentation clearly distinguishes between inline Milvus (development/testing) and remote Milvus (production) with guidance on when to use each
  - [ ] Prerequisites document all required components: OpenShift version, GPU support, cluster admin privileges, StorageClass, Milvus root password, vLLM model deployment, and oc CLI
  - [ ] The IMPORTANT note about using a dedicated etcd instance (not the OpenShift control plane etcd) is documented in both the overview and deployment procedure
  - [ ] The Llama Stack providers support reference table lists remote::milvus with the MILVUS_ENDPOINT enablement variable and Technology Preview status
- **References**:
  - [RHAIENG-653 Description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-653): JIRA story specifying documentation scope: overview, step-by-step enablement, configuration examples, updated RAG chatbot examples, prerequisites and limitations
  - [RHAIENG-55 (Parent)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-55): Parent epic for RHAI RAG Technology Preview feature
  - [RHAISTRAT-13 (Ancestor)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-13): Strategy ticket for enhancing enterprise-readiness and usability for RAG & Llama Stack in secure environments

#### REQ-003: Configuration examples for remote:milvus with remote:vllm distribution
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-653](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-653) | [RHAIENG-871](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-871) | [Spike doc (Google Doc)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1SIqQngqWmqpNk2skzDimQyRcr-jUCiIXvYbf_b2hJrA/edit?tab=t.0) | [GitLab MR !1937](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/1937) | [GitLab MR !1938](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/1938) | [GitLab MR !1939](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/1939) | [GitLab MR !1940](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/1940) | [ODH PR #982](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/982)
- **Summary**: This requirement covers documenting how to deploy a LlamaStackDistribution custom resource that pairs remote:milvus (an external Milvus vector database) with remote:vllm (an external vLLM inference model) on Red Hat OpenShift AI. The documentation has already been implemented and merged into the repository. It includes a new concept module explaining Milvus vector database modes (inline vs remote), a new procedure for deploying a standalone remote Milvus service with etcd on OpenShift, and Example B in the LlamaStackDistribution deployment procedure showing a complete CR YAML with MILVUS_ENDPOINT, MILVUS_TOKEN, and MILVUS_CONSISTENCY_LEVEL configured via secrets. The ingestion and querying procedures were also updated to include remote Milvus as a vector store option alongside inline Milvus, inline FAISS, and remote pgvector.
- **User impact**: Cluster administrators can now deploy production-grade RAG stacks using an external Milvus vector database service instead of relying solely on the embedded inline Milvus. This enables high availability, horizontal scalability, and isolation of vector storage from the Llama Stack server pod, which is critical for production RAG workloads on OpenShift AI.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `modules/overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc` (CONCEPT) — Overview of Milvus vector databases explaining inline vs remote operational modes, architecture components (Milvus service, etcd, persistent storage), gRPC port usage, and production recommendations. Already implemented.
  - [ ] Create `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc` (PROCEDURE) — Step-by-step procedure for deploying a remote Milvus vector database on OpenShift, including etcd deployment, PVC setup, Milvus standalone deployment, service configuration, and verification steps. Already implemented.
  - [ ] Update `modules/deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc` (PROCEDURE) — Update the LlamaStackDistribution deployment procedure to include Example B showing remote Milvus configuration with milvus-secret, MILVUS_ENDPOINT, MILVUS_TOKEN, and MILVUS_CONSISTENCY_LEVEL environment variables alongside the existing inline Milvus example. Already implemented. Also includes Example D for remote pgvector.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Documentation outlines the process for enabling Milvus Remote on an OpenShift cluster, including deploying etcd and Milvus standalone services
  - [ ] At least one LlamaStackDistribution CR example demonstrates deploying a distribution with remote:milvus and remote:vllm, showing MILVUS_ENDPOINT, MILVUS_TOKEN, and MILVUS_CONSISTENCY_LEVEL configuration via secrets
  - [ ] RAG chatbot ingestion and querying procedures include remote Milvus as a vector store option with correct provider_id (milvus-remote)
  - [ ] Prerequisites are documented including: vLLM model deployment, GPU enablement, StorageClass for PVCs, Milvus root password, gRPC port 19530 requirement, and PostgreSQL for Llama Stack metadata
  - [ ] Notes explain that inline Milvus is for development/testing while remote Milvus is recommended for production-grade deployments
  - [ ] The Llama Stack providers support reference table includes remote:milvus with its enablement variable (MILVUS_ENDPOINT) and Technology Preview status
  - [ ] Users can follow the remote Milvus deployment procedure and verify both etcd and milvus-standalone pods are running before proceeding to LlamaStackDistribution deployment

Data scientists benefit from improved vector indexing performance, durability, and horizontal scalability when building RAG-based AI applications.

  - [ ] Users can create vector stores using the remote Milvus provider (provider_id: milvus-remote) in ingestion and querying workflows

#### REQ-004: RAG chatbot setup example using Milvus Remote

The documentation also adds BEIR benchmarking scripts that let users evaluate embedding model quality against standardized information retrieval datasets, supporting both inline and remote vector database backends.
- **User impact**: Cluster administrators and data scientists gain a production-ready alternative to inline Milvus for RAG workloads. Remote Milvus provides high availability, horizontal scalability, and persistent vector storage, enabling enterprise-grade RAG chatbot deployments. The BEIR benchmarking integration helps users select the best embedding model for their retrieval accuracy requirements.

#### REQ-005: Prerequisites and limitations for Milvus Remote
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-653](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-653) | [RHAISTRAT-13](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-13) | [RHAIENG-871](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-871) | [RHAIENG-1568](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1568) | [ODH PR #982](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/opendatahub-documentation/pull/982)
- **Summary**: The Milvus Remote provider (remote::milvus) is a new vector store option for Llama Stack in OpenShift AI, enabling production-grade RAG workloads by running Milvus as a standalone external service rather than embedded inline. Documentation must clearly specify the prerequisites (OpenShift 4.19+, GPU support, cluster admin privileges, a deployed vLLM inference model, StorageClass for PVCs, dedicated etcd, PostgreSQL for metadata, and the MILVUS_ENDPOINT environment variable) and limitations (Technology Preview status, not supported on IBM Z, standalone deployment only without Milvus Operator, gRPC port 19530 required for client traffic, example configs are for testing/evaluation not production, dedicated etcd required separate from OpenShift control plane etcd).
- **User impact**: Cluster administrators deploying RAG workloads need to understand the full set of prerequisites before deploying Milvus Remote, including infrastructure requirements (etcd, PVCs, GPU, PostgreSQL) and configuration requirements (secrets, environment variables, gRPC endpoints). Missing prerequisites can cause deployment failures or data loss; undocumented limitations could lead users to deploy in unsupported configurations.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc` (REFERENCE) — Ensure the prerequisites section is complete and accurate, covering OpenShift version, GPU enablement, cluster admin privileges, StorageClass availability, Milvus root password, deployed vLLM inference model, model endpoint URL, API token, and the oc CLI. Verify limitations notes include Technology Preview status, IBM Z non-support, standalone-only deployment, dedicated etcd requirement, and production guidance.
  - [ ] Update `modules/overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc` (CONCEPT) — Verify the overview clearly documents operational modes (Inline Milvus Lite vs Remote Milvus), their limitations, production-readiness guidance, dedicated etcd requirement, and port usage (19530 for gRPC, 9091 for health).
  - [ ] Update `modules/llama-stack-providers-support.adoc` (REFERENCE) — Ensure the provider support table accurately reflects remote::milvus enablement via MILVUS_ENDPOINT, disconnected environment support (Yes), and Technology Preview support status.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can identify all infrastructure prerequisites (OpenShift version, GPU support, cluster admin privileges, StorageClass, dedicated etcd) before attempting a Remote Milvus deployment
  - [ ] Users can identify all configuration prerequisites (vLLM model deployment with external route and token auth, model endpoint URL, API token, Milvus root password, oc CLI) from the documentation
  - [ ] Users can determine the supported Milvus version (v2.6.0) and deployment mode (standalone without Milvus Operator)
  - [ ] Users can find that Remote Milvus requires gRPC port 19530 for client traffic and that port 9091 is reserved for health checks only
  - [ ] Users can find that a dedicated etcd instance is required for Milvus and must not share the OpenShift control plane etcd
  - [ ] Users can determine that Milvus Remote is a Technology Preview feature and understand the support scope implications
  - [ ] Users can find platform limitations: not supported on IBM Z, limited functionality on IBM Power (ppc64le)
  - [ ] Users can distinguish between the example evaluation/testing configuration and production-grade deployment requirements, with a pointer to upstream Milvus docs for production

#### REQ-006: Technology Preview designation for Milvus Remote RAG feature
- **Source**: [RHAIENG-55](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-55) | [RHAISTRAT-13](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-13) | [RHAIENG-1568](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-1568) | [RHAIENG-871](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIENG-871)
- **Summary**: The Milvus Remote vector database provider for Llama Stack RAG workloads was introduced as a Technology Preview feature in RHOAI 2.25. Documentation must clearly mark all Milvus Remote RAG content with the standard Red Hat Technology Preview designation, including support scope disclaimers, to set correct user expectations about production readiness and SLA coverage. The feature enables production-grade RAG deployments using a standalone Milvus service rather than the embedded Milvus Lite, and includes deployment procedures, LlamaStackDistribution configuration examples, and integration with the broader Llama Stack ecosystem.
- **User impact**: Users deploying Milvus Remote for RAG workloads must understand that the feature is a Technology Preview without production SLA support. Without clear Technology Preview markers, users might incorrectly assume full production support and deploy Milvus Remote in production environments, leading to unmet expectations around Red Hat support coverage and feature completeness.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc` (PROCEDURE) — Ensure the procedure includes the standard Technology Preview admonition snippet. The existing module currently lacks an explicit TP admonition, though the parent assembly has one.
  - [ ] Update `modules/overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc` (CONCEPT) — Verify and ensure the overview carries consistent Technology Preview designations for Milvus Remote specifically, distinct from inline Milvus.
  - [ ] Update `modules/llama-stack-providers-support.adoc` (REFERENCE) — Ensure the provider support table clearly indicates Technology Preview status for remote::milvus and inline::milvus, and that the technology-preview-features reference module includes an entry for Milvus Remote RAG.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users encounter a Technology Preview admonition when reading the procedure for deploying a remote Milvus vector database
  - [ ] Users can identify from the Llama Stack API provider support table that remote::milvus is a Technology Preview feature
  - [ ] Users can find Milvus Remote RAG listed in the Technology Preview features reference for the applicable release
  - [ ] The Technology Preview admonition uses the standard Red Hat snippet format including SLA exclusion, recommendation against production use, and link to Technology Preview Features Support Scope
  - [ ] Users can distinguish between inline Milvus Lite (for development) and remote Milvus (for production-grade workloads) and understand that both carry Technology Preview status
  - [ ] The LlamaStackDistribution deployment examples (Example B with remote Milvus) reference the Technology Preview status

The codebase already contains all documented content including: (1) concept module for Milvus overview with inline vs remote modes, (2) procedure module for deploying remote Milvus standalone with etcd, (3) LSD deployment example B with remote Milvus configuration, (4) updated ingestion and querying procedures with remote Milvus options, (5) updated provider support reference table. The documentation was originally delivered for RHOAI 2.25 and has since been updated through version 3.4.
- The Google Docs spike document could not be accessed (401 authentication error) but the JIRA description and existing codebase provided complete coverage of the requirement.
- Four GitLab MRs were created: !1938 (primary downstream MR), !1937 (BEIR benchmarking), !1939 and !1940 (cherry-picks into stage-2.25). GitLab MRs on gitlab.cee.redhat.com were inaccessible due to SSL certificate verification failure (self-signed certificate in certificate chain).
- The BEIR benchmarking documentation (modules/benchmarking-embedding-models-with-beir-datasets-and-llama-stack.adoc and modules/benchmarking-embedding-models-with-beir-datasets-and-llama-stack-command-line-options.adoc) supports both inline and remote vector database backends.
- FIPS compatibility is mentioned in RHAISTRAT-13 as a concern but no FIPS-specific notes appear in the Milvus Remote prerequisites — this should be verified.
- The example config is explicitly marked as evaluation-only, with a pointer to upstream Milvus docs for production deployments.
- Technology Preview status applies to the entire Llama Stack integration, with individual procedure modules relying on the assembly-level TP admonition.

## Technical Review -- RHAIENG-653: Remote Milvus vector database for Llama Stack RAG

**Doc type detected:** Concept (overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc), Procedure (deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc), Reference (technology-preview-features.adoc), Snippet (technology-preview.adoc)
**Reviewer lens applied:** Both (Developer lens for the procedure, snippet, and reference entry; Architect lens for the concept overview)
**Overall technical confidence:** MEDIUM -- The upstream draft YAML manifests are structurally valid and resource names chain correctly to the LlamaStackDistribution CR Example B. However, the source repo copy of the procedure has several discrepancies from the upstream draft that would cause deployment failures if published in that state, and multiple verification details require SME confirmation against a running Milvus v2.6.0 instance.

**Files reviewed:**

- `/Users/dobrenna/Documents/PROJECTS/redhat-docs-agent-tools/eval/dataset/cases/case-010-rhaieng-653/.docs-worktree/upstream/opendatahub-documentation-main/modules/overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc` (upstream draft, concept)
- `/Users/dobrenna/Documents/PROJECTS/redhat-docs-agent-tools/eval/dataset/cases/case-010-rhaieng-653/.docs-worktree/upstream/opendatahub-documentation-main/modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc` (upstream draft, procedure)
- `/Users/dobrenna/Documents/PROJECTS/redhat-docs-agent-tools/eval/dataset/cases/case-010-rhaieng-653/.docs-worktree/modules/technology-preview-features.adoc` (downstream reference)
- `/Users/dobrenna/Documents/PROJECTS/redhat-docs-agent-tools/eval/dataset/cases/case-010-rhaieng-653/.docs-worktree/snippets/technology-preview.adoc` (shared snippet)

**Cross-referenced against source repo:** `/private/var/folders/vq/tpv__2gx00s5fn6yh57k86cc0000gn/T/agent-eval/2026-06-11-opus-full/cases/case-010-rhaieng-653/.agent_workspace/rhaieng-653/code-repo/openshift-ai-documentation`

---

### Critical issues (must fix before publication)

**C1. Hardcoded password in the source repo copy of the Secret manifest**

- **Location:** Source repo `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, line 40 -- `root-password: "MyStr0ngP@ssw0rd"`
- **Issue:** The source repo version ships a literal password string in the Kubernetes Secret manifest. The upstream draft correctly uses a placeholder (`<your_milvus_root_password>`) with a callout annotation (`<1>`) and explicit guidance to replace it. If the source repo copy is the version that reaches publication, readers will deploy Milvus with a well-known example password.
- **Impact:** Security risk. Passwords published in documentation examples get reused. Even in testing and evaluation environments, a known password can be exploited if the service is exposed.
- **Suggestion:** Ensure the published version uses the upstream draft's approach: a placeholder value `"<your_milvus_root_password>"` with the callout `<1>` and the note "Replace `<your_milvus_root_password>` with a strong, unique password. Do not use the example value in production or testing environments."

**C2. Liveness probe approach differs between upstream draft and source repo -- `exec`+`curl` may cause crash loops**

- **Location:** Source repo `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, lines 144-150 (liveness probe uses `exec` with `command: ["curl", "-f", "http://localhost:9091/healthz"]`). Upstream draft lines 150-156 (uses `httpGet` with `path: /healthz` and `port: 9091`).
- **Issue:** The source repo version relies on `curl` being available inside the `milvusdb/milvus:v2.6.0` container. If `curl` is not present (common in minimal container images), the liveness probe will always fail and Kubernetes will restart the pod in a perpetual crash loop. The upstream draft correctly uses `httpGet`, where Kubernetes performs the HTTP request itself without any dependency on container-internal binaries.
- **Impact:** If the `exec`+`curl` version is published and `curl` is not in the image, the Milvus pod will never reach steady state. The reader will see repeated restarts with no clear error message, because liveness probe failures only appear in `kubectl describe pod` events, not in container logs.
- **Suggestion:** The upstream draft's `httpGet` approach is the correct pattern. It also matches the Qdrant deployment procedure already in the repo (`modules/deploying-a-qdrant-vector-database.adoc`, lines 95-100), providing consistency across vector database deployment procedures. Ensure the source repo copy is updated to match the upstream draft.

**C3. Cross-namespace service URL uses wrong protocol in source repo copy**

- **Location:** Source repo `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, line 186 -- `http://milvus-service.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:19530`
- **Issue:** The source repo copy uses `http://` as the URI scheme for the cross-namespace Milvus endpoint. The upstream draft (line 201) correctly uses `tcp://`. The `deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc` Example B (line 247 in source repo) also uses `tcp://milvus-service:19530` for `MILVUS_ENDPOINT`. Port 19530 is Milvus's gRPC port -- gRPC uses HTTP/2 framing but the `MILVUS_ENDPOINT` configuration in Llama Stack expects a `tcp://` scheme, not `http://`.
- **Impact:** A reader deploying Milvus in a namespace different from Llama Stack who follows the source repo version's `http://` URL will get connection failures from the Llama Stack `remote::milvus` provider. The code-grounded review confirms `tcp://` is the supported scheme (claim verdict: `supported`).
- **Suggestion:** Align the source repo copy to match the upstream draft: `tcp://milvus-service.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:19530`.

---

### Significant issues (should fix)

**S1. GPU prerequisite is inappropriate for the Milvus deployment procedure**

- **Location:** Source repo `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, prerequisites list, line 16
- **Issue:** The source repo copy includes "You have enabled GPU support in OpenShift AI. This includes installing the Node Feature Discovery operator and NVIDIA GPU Operators" as a prerequisite. The upstream draft correctly omits this. Milvus and etcd are CPU-only workloads and do not require GPU acceleration. This prerequisite was likely copied from the LlamaStackDistribution procedure where GPU support is genuinely needed for vLLM inference.
- **Impact:** Readers without GPU hardware provisioned may skip the Milvus deployment, believing GPUs are required. This incorrectly gates a CPU-only deployment on GPU availability.
- **Suggestion:** Remove the GPU prerequisite. GPU support is already properly listed as a prerequisite in `deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc` where it applies.

**S2. Source repo procedure lacks Technology Preview snippet include**

- **Location:** Source repo `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, top of file
- **Issue:** The upstream draft correctly includes the Technology Preview snippet (lines 10-11: `:feature-name: Remote Milvus vector database deployment` followed by `include::snippets/technology-preview.adoc[]`). The source repo copy omits this snippet include entirely. It jumps directly to a NOTE admonition about the example being for testing environments.
- **Impact:** The published procedure may lack the required Red Hat Technology Preview support scope disclaimer, which is a documentation compliance requirement for all TP features.
- **Suggestion:** Add the Technology Preview snippet include to the source repo copy, matching the upstream draft pattern.

**S3. Missing `storageClassName` guidance in source repo PVC definition**

- **Location:** Source repo `modules/deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, PVC manifest (lines 42-52)
- **Issue:** The source repo PVC definition omits the commented-out `storageClassName` line and corresponding callout that the upstream draft provides (upstream lines 54 and 189). In clusters without a default StorageClass, the PVC will remain `Pending` indefinitely with no error message.
- **Impact:** Readers on clusters without a default StorageClass will have the PVC stuck in Pending, and the verification steps will show the milvus-standalone pod cannot start (no volume to mount).
- **Suggestion:** Include the commented-out `storageClassName` with the callout annotation as the upstream draft does.

**S4. Health check response format conflict between upstream and source repo**

- **Location:** Upstream draft line 225 says response is `OK`. Source repo line 210 says response is `{"status": "healthy"}`.
- **Issue:** The two versions document contradictory expected responses for `curl http://localhost:9091/healthz` against Milvus v2.6.0. Only one can be correct.
- **Impact:** The incorrect version will cause readers to believe the health check failed when it actually succeeded, or vice versa. This undermines confidence in the verification steps.
- **Suggestion:** Test against a running `milvusdb/milvus:v2.6.0` instance and use the actual response in both versions. See SME1.

**S5. Technology Preview feature name inconsistency between modules**

- **Location:** Upstream `overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc` line 10: `:feature-name: Remote Milvus vector database support`. Upstream `deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc` line 10: `:feature-name: Remote Milvus vector database deployment`.
- **Issue:** The two modules set different `:feature-name:` values, which renders as different Technology Preview admonition text. "Support" vs. "deployment" suggests these might be different Technology Preview features, but they refer to the same feature (RHAIENG-653).
- **Impact:** Readers may wonder whether "Remote Milvus vector database support" and "Remote Milvus vector database deployment" are distinct features with separate TP scopes.
- **Suggestion:** Align on a single feature name across both modules. "Remote Milvus vector database support" is more appropriate since it encompasses the entire feature, not just the deployment procedure.

**S6. Ephemeral etcd storage warning should be more prominent**

- **Location:** Upstream `deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, lines 191-194 (WARNING block after the YAML)
- **Issue:** The WARNING that "Restarting the etcd pod deletes all Milvus metadata (collection state, indexes)" appears after the YAML manifest and its callout annotations. By the time a reader reaches this warning, they may have already pasted the YAML and clicked Create. This is a significant operational risk for a doc that targets "testing or evaluation environments" where pod restarts are common (node recycling, cluster updates, resource limits).
- **Impact:** Users may deploy the evaluation setup, ingest data into Milvus, and then lose everything when etcd restarts -- without having understood this was expected.
- **Suggestion:** Move the ephemeral storage warning to the prerequisites section or immediately before the YAML block, and consider adding inline YAML comments in the etcd Deployment's `emptyDir: {}` line.

**S7. Upstream procedure missing "Next steps" section**

- **Location:** Upstream `deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, end of file (line 229)
- **Issue:** The upstream draft ends after the verification steps with no "Next steps" section. The source repo copy includes a "Next steps" linking to the LlamaStackDistribution deployment (Example B). The upstream draft should also include this critical next step since deploying Milvus alone is not useful without configuring Llama Stack to use it.
- **Impact:** Readers who complete the Milvus deployment have no guidance on the next required action.
- **Suggestion:** The source repo copy handles this correctly with the `.Next steps` section. Add the equivalent to the upstream draft.

---

### Minor issues (consider fixing)

**M1. Both container images need disconnected-environment mirroring guidance**

- **Location:** Upstream `deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, prerequisites (line 24) and YAML (lines 80, 137)
- **Issue:** The prerequisites mention mirroring for the Milvus image (`milvusdb/milvus:v2.6.0`) but not for the etcd image (`quay.io/coreos/etcd:v3.5.5`). Both images are from external registries and both need to be mirrored for disconnected environments.
- **Impact:** Disconnected-environment users will successfully mirror Milvus but the etcd Deployment will fail to pull its image.
- **Suggestion:** Extend the disconnected-environment prerequisite to list both images that need mirroring.

**M2. Missing `readinessProbe` on Milvus standalone Deployment**

- **Location:** Upstream `deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, Milvus Deployment definition (lines 130-166)
- **Issue:** The Deployment defines a `livenessProbe` but no `readinessProbe`. The `milvus-service` Service will route traffic to the Milvus pod as soon as it starts, before Milvus has finished initialization (which takes ~90 seconds per the `initialDelaySeconds`). The Qdrant deployment example in the same repository includes both readiness and liveness probes.
- **Impact:** Llama Stack may attempt to connect to Milvus before it is ready, causing transient "connection refused" errors during startup.
- **Suggestion:** Add a `readinessProbe` with the same `httpGet` path but shorter timing (e.g., `initialDelaySeconds: 30, periodSeconds: 10`), matching the Qdrant pattern.

**M3. Concept module source repo copy refers to "YAML below" but contains no YAML**

- **Location:** Source repo `modules/overview-of-milvus-vector-databases.adoc`, line 39 -- "The ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS environment variable shown in the YAML below"
- **Issue:** This is a standalone concept module with no YAML content. The YAML is in the separate `deploying-a-llamastackdistribution-instance.adoc` module. The upstream draft (line 52) correctly says "is required to enable the `inline::milvus` provider" without referring to nonexistent YAML.
- **Impact:** Readers navigating directly to this module via search or cross-reference will look for YAML that does not exist.
- **Suggestion:** Adopt the upstream draft wording, or change to "shown in the LlamaStackDistribution deployment example."

**M4. No namespace specification in any resource manifest**

- **Location:** Upstream `deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, all resource manifests
- **Issue:** None of the resource definitions include `metadata.namespace`. Step 2 instructs the reader to verify the selected project in the web console, which implicitly sets the namespace. However, if a reader applies this manifest via `oc apply -f` from the CLI, resources deploy to whatever namespace is active in their kubeconfig context.
- **Impact:** CLI users may deploy resources to the wrong namespace.
- **Suggestion:** Add a note that CLI users should ensure the correct namespace is active (`oc project <namespace>`) or add `metadata.namespace` as a placeholder to the resource definitions.

**M5. etcd Service port lacks a name**

- **Location:** Upstream `deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database.adoc`, etcd Service definition (lines 107-112)
- **Issue:** The etcd Service does not name its port (`name: client`), while the milvus-service explicitly names its ports (`grpc`, `http`). Port naming is a Kubernetes best practice and is required for Istio/service mesh compatibility.
- **Impact:** Minor; functions correctly in most environments but may cause issues in service mesh environments.
- **Suggestion:** Add `name: client` to the etcd Service port definition.

---

### SME verification needed

**SME1. Milvus v2.6.0 health endpoint response format**

- **Issue:** The upstream draft says the response from `curl http://localhost:9091/healthz` is `OK`. The source repo says it is `{"status": "healthy"}`. Only one is correct for Milvus v2.6.0.
- **Action needed:** Run `curl http://localhost:9091/healthz` against a running `milvusdb/milvus:v2.6.0` container and report the actual response body.

**SME2. Confirm `curl` availability in `milvusdb/milvus:v2.6.0`**

- **Issue:** The source repo liveness probe depends on `curl` being present in the container. If it is not present, the `httpGet` approach in the upstream draft is the correct fallback.
- **Action needed:** Run `docker exec <container> which curl` or inspect the image layers to confirm binary availability.

**SME3. Verify `MILVUS_ROOT_PASSWORD`, `DEPLOY_MODE`, `ETCD_ENDPOINTS` environment variable names for Milvus v2.6.0**

- **Issue:** The code-grounded review found `no_evidence_found` for these three environment variables in the documentation source repo. This is expected (they are Milvus container image variables, not OpenShift AI variables), but their names and behavior should be confirmed against Milvus v2.6.0 documentation. In particular, `MILVUS_ROOT_PASSWORD` may have been renamed in recent versions.
- **Action needed:** Verify against Milvus v2.6.0 environment variable configuration documentation at https://milvus.io/docs.

**SME4. Verify etcd v3.5.5 compatibility with Milvus v2.6.0**

- **Issue:** The manifest pins `quay.io/coreos/etcd:v3.5.5` (late 2022). Milvus v2.6.0 is a 2025 release. While etcd has strong backward compatibility, the Milvus project may recommend a newer version. The `quay.io/coreos/etcd` registry path is also the legacy CoreOS-maintained image.
- **Action needed:** Check the Milvus v2.6.0 release notes or docker-compose files for their recommended etcd version.

---

### Strengths

1. **Complete, self-contained YAML manifest.** The upstream deployment procedure provides a single multi-resource YAML block (Secret, PVC, two Deployments, two Services) that can be pasted in one operation. This reduces the chance of readers missing resources or applying them out of order.

2. **Accurate resource name chaining across documents.** Resource names (`milvus-secret`, `milvus-pvc`, `milvus-standalone`, `milvus-service`, `etcd-deployment`, `etcd-service`) are consistent across the Milvus deployment procedure and the LlamaStackDistribution Example B, where `milvus-secret` is referenced in `oc create secret generic milvus-secret`. The code-grounded review confirms all resource names as `supported`.

3. **Strong etcd isolation warning.** Both the concept and procedure modules explicitly warn against using the OpenShift control plane etcd. The IMPORTANT admonition block makes this unmissable. This prevents a genuinely dangerous operational mistake.

4. **Thorough verification steps.** The procedure includes six verification steps covering Deployment status, Pod state, Milvus startup logs, Service exposure, and an optional health check command. This is significantly more thorough than typical Red Hat deployment procedures.

5. **Well-separated concept and procedure modules.** The concept module explains the "why" (operational modes, component responsibilities, architectural separation of concerns) while the procedure module provides the exact "how." This follows modular documentation best practices and allows readers to enter at the appropriate level.

6. **Correct Technology Preview handling in the upstream draft.** Both upstream modules use the shared snippet pattern (`:feature-name:` + `include::snippets/technology-preview.adoc[]`), which ensures consistent TP language and automatic updates if the standard disclaimer changes.

7. **Good cross-referencing in the technology-preview-features.adoc entry.** The RHAIENG-653 entry links to both the concept overview and the deployment procedure, providing two entry points depending on whether the reader wants understanding or action.

8. **Upstream draft correctly fixes all critical source repo issues.** The upstream draft uses `httpGet` instead of `exec`+`curl`, `tcp://` instead of `http://`, a placeholder password instead of a literal, and includes the Technology Preview snippet. This suggests the upstream is ahead of the source repo in accuracy.

Severity counts: critical=3 significant=7 minor=5 sme=4

= Technology Preview features

[role='_abstract']

ifdef::self-managed[]
[IMPORTANT]
====
This section describes Technology Preview features in {productname-long} {vernum}.
Technology Preview features are not supported with Red{nbsp}Hat production service level agreements (SLAs) and might not be functionally complete.
Red{nbsp}Hat does not recommend using them in production.
These features provide early access to upcoming product features, enabling customers to test functionality and provide feedback during the development process.

For more information about the support scope of Red{nbsp}Hat Technology Preview features, see link:https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview/[Technology Preview Features Support Scope].
====
endif::[]

ifdef::cloud-service[]
[IMPORTANT]
====
This section describes Technology Preview features in {productname-long}.
Technology Preview features are not supported with Red{nbsp}Hat production service level agreements (SLAs) and might not be functionally complete.
Red{nbsp}Hat does not recommend using them in production.
These features provide early access to upcoming product features, enabling customers to test functionality and provide feedback during the development process.

For more information about the support scope of Red{nbsp}Hat Technology Preview features, see link:https://access.redhat.com/support/offerings/techpreview/[Technology Preview Features Support Scope].
====
endif::[]
//

//RHOAISTRAT-512
Build Generative AI Apps with Llama Stack on {productname-short}::
With this release, the Llama Stack Technology Preview feature on {productname-short} enables Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and agentic workflows for building next-generation generative AI applications. It supports remote inference, built-in embeddings, and vector database operations. It also integrates with providers such as the TrustyAI provider for safety and the TrustyAI LM-Eval provider for evaluation.
+
This preview includes tools, components, and guidance for enabling the Llama Stack Operator, interacting with the RAG Tool, and automating PDF ingestion and keyword search capabilities to enhance document discovery.

// RHOAISTRAT-575
Centralized platform metrics and tracing::
Centralized platform metrics and tracing are now available as a Technology Preview feature in {productname-short}. This feature enables integration with the Cluster Observability Operator (COO), {org-name} build of OpenTelemetry, and Tempo Operator, and provides optional preconfigured observability configurations for {productname-short}. It also introduces a dedicated observability stack. Future releases will collect infrastructure and customer workload signals in the dedicated observability stack.

//RHOAIENG-603
Support for Llama Stack Distribution version 0.2.17::
The Llama Stack Distribution now includes Llama-stack version 0.2.17 as Technology Preview. This feature brings several capabilities, including:
+
* Model providers: Self-hosted providers such as vLLM are now automatically registered, so you no longer need to manually set `INFERENCE_MODEL` variables.
* Infrastructure and backends: Improved the OpenAI inference and added support for the Vector Store API.
* Error handling: Errors are now standardized, and library client initialization has been improved.
* Access Control: The Vector Store and File APIs now enforce access control, and telemetry read APIs are gated by user roles.
* Bug fixes.

// RHAIENG-653
Remote Milvus vector database for Llama Stack RAG::
Remote Milvus (`remote::milvus`) is available as a Technology Preview vector store provider for Llama Stack RAG workloads in {productname-short} {vernum}.
Remote Milvus enables production-grade vector search with a standalone Milvus service and a dedicated etcd instance for metadata coordination.
This deployment mode is recommended for workloads that require scalable vector indexing, durable storage, and high-performance similarity search.
+
For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag#overview-of-milvus-vector-databases_rag[Overview of Milvus vector databases] and link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_llama_stack/llama-stack-adv-examples_rag#deploying-a-remote-milvus-vector-database_rag[Deploying a remote Milvus vector database].

// RHOAIENG-30965
Support for IBM Power accelerated Triton Inference Server::
You can now enable Power architecture support for Triton inference server (CPU only) with Python and ONNX backend. You can deploy Triton inference server as a custom model serving runtime on IBM Power architecture as a Technology Preview feature in {productname-long}.
+
For details, see link:https://quay.io/repository/powercloud/tritonserver[Triton Inference Server image].

Support for IBM Z accelerated Triton Inference Server::
You can now enable Z architecture support for the Triton Inference Server (Telum I/Telum II) with multiple backend options, including ONNX-MLIR, Snap ML (C++), and PyTorch. The Triton Inference Server can be deployed as a custom model serving runtime on IBM Z architecture as a Technology Preview feature in {productname-long}.
+
For details, see link:https://ibm.github.io/ibm-z-oss-hub/containers/ibmz-accelerated-for-nvidia-triton-inference-server.html[IBM Z accelerated Triton Inference Server].

// RHOAISTRAT-520
Support for Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling (KEDA)::
{productname-short} now supports Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling (KEDA) in its KServe RawDeployment mode. This Technology Preview feature enables metrics-based autoscaling for inference services, allowing for more efficient management of accelerator resources, reduced operational costs, and improved performance for your inference services.
+
To set up autoscaling for your inference service in KServe RawDeployment mode, you need to install and configure the OpenShift Custom Metrics Autoscaler (CMA), which is based on KEDA. 
+
For more information about this feature, see: link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/managing_and_monitoring_models/managing_and_monitoring_models_on_the_single_model_serving_platform#configuring-metrics-based-autoscaling_cluster-admin[Configuring metrics-based autoscaling]. 

// RHOAIENG-26716
LM-Eval model evaluation UI feature::
TrustyAI now offers a user-friendly UI for LM-Eval model evaluations as Technology Preview. You can input evaluation parameters for a given model and view an evaluation-results page, all from the UI.

// RHOAISTRAT-610
Use Guardrails Orchestrator with LlamaStack::
You can now run detections using the Guardrails Orchestrator tool from TrustyAI with Llama Stack as a Technology Preview feature, using the built-in detection component. To use this feature, ensure TrustyAI is enabled, the FMS Orchestrator and detectors are set up, and KServe RawDeployment mode is in use for full compatibility if needed. There is no manual set up required.
+
Then, in the `DataScienceCluster` custom resource for the {productname-long} Operator, set the `spec.llamastackoperator.managementState` field to `Managed`.
+
For more information, see the following resources on GitHub:
+
* link:https://github.com/trustyai-explainability/llama-stack-provider-trustyai-fms[Trusty AI FMS Provider]

//RHOAISTRAT-289
Define and manage pipelines with Kubernetes API::
You can now define and manage data science pipelines and pipeline versions by using the Kubernetes API, which stores them as custom resources in the cluster instead of the internal database. This Technology Preview feature makes it easier to use OpenShift GitOps (Argo CD) or similar tools to manage pipelines, while still allowing you to manage them through the {productname-short} user interface, API, and `kfp` SDK.  
+
This option, enabled by default, is configurable with the *Store pipeline definitions in Kubernetes* checkbox when you create or edit a pipeline server. Cluster administrators can also configure this option by setting the `spec.apiServer.pipelineStore` field to `kubernetes` or `database` in the `DataSciencePipelinesApplication` (DSPA) custom resource. For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_data_science_pipelines/managing-data-science-pipelines_ds-pipelines#defining-a-pipeline-by-using-the-kubernetes-api_ds-pipelines[Defining a pipeline by using the Kubernetes API].

ifdef::self-managed[]

endif::[]

Model customization with LAB-tuning::

LAB-tuning is now available as a Technology Preview feature, enabling data scientists to run an end-to-end workflow for customizing large language models (LLMs). The link:https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01081[LAB (Large-scale Alignment for chatBots)] method offers a more efficient alternative to traditional fine-tuning by leveraging taxonomy-guided synthetic data generation (SDG) and a multi-phase training approach.
+
Data scientists can run LAB-tuning workflows directly from the {productname-short} dashboard by using the new preconfigured InstructLab pipeline, which simplifies the tuning process. For details on enabling and using LAB-tuning, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/enabling_lab-tuning[Enabling LAB-tuning] and link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/customizing_models_with_lab-tuning[Customizing models with LAB-tuning].
+
[IMPORTANT]
====
The LAB-tuning feature is not currently supported for disconnected environments.
====

// RHOAISTRAT-79
New Feature Store component::

You can now install and manage Feature Store as a configurable component in the {productname-long} Operator. Based on the open-source link:https://feast.dev/[Feast] project, Feature Store acts as a bridge between ML models and data, enabling consistent and scalable feature management across the ML lifecycle.
+
This Technology Preview release introduces the following capabilities:
+
* Centralized feature repository for consistent feature reuse
* Python SDK and CLI for programmatic and command-line interactions to define, manage, and retrieve features for ML models
* Feature definition and management
* Support for a wide range of data sources
* Data ingestion via feature materialization
* Feature retrieval for both online model inference and offline model training
* Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to protect sensitive features
* Extensibility and integration with third-party data and compute providers
* Scalability to meet enterprise ML needs
* Searchable feature catalog
* Data lineage tracking for enhanced observability
+
For configuration details, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_machine_learning_features/configuring_feature_store[Configuring Feature Store].


ifdef::self-managed[]
// RHOAISTRAT-439 and RHOAIENG-20214

IBM Power and IBM Z architecture support::

IBM Power (ppc64le) and IBM Z (s390x) architectures are now supported as a Technology Preview feature. Currently, you can only deploy models in *KServe RawDeployment* mode on these architectures.  

//RHOAIENG-20214

Support for vLLM in IBM Power and IBM Z architectures::
vLLM runtime templates are available for use in IBM Power and IBM Z architectures as Technology Preview.

endif::[]

//RHOAISTRAT-269
Enable targeted deployment of workbenches to specific worker nodes in {productname-long} Dashboard using node selectors::

Hardware profiles are now available as a Technology Preview. With hardware profiles, you can target specific worker nodes for workbenches or model-serving workloads, including specific accelerator types or CPU-only nodes.
+
This feature replaces the current accelerator profiles feature and container size selector field, offering a broader set of capabilities for targeting different hardware configurations. While accelerator profiles, taints, and tolerations provide some capabilities for matching workloads to hardware, they do not ensure that workloads land on specific nodes, especially if some nodes lack the appropriate taints. 
+
The hardware profiles feature supports both accelerator and CPU-only configurations, along with node selectors, to enhance targeting capabilities for specific worker nodes. Administrators can configure hardware profiles in the settings menu. Users can select the enabled profiles using the UI for workbenches, model serving, and Data Science Pipelines where applicable. 

RStudio Server workbench image::

With the RStudio Server workbench image, you can access the RStudio IDE, an integrated development environment for R. The R programming language is used for statistical computing and graphics to support data analysis and predictions.
+
To use the RStudio Server workbench image, you must first build it by creating a secret and triggering the `BuildConfig`, and then enable it in the {productname-short} UI by editing the `rstudio-rhel9` image stream. 
For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/getting_started_with_{url-productname-long}/creating-a-workbench-select-ide_get-started#building-the-rstudio-server-workbench-images_get-started[Building the RStudio Server workbench images].
+
[IMPORTANT] 
====
*Disclaimer:* 
{org-name} supports managing workbenches in {productname-short}. However, {org-name} does not provide support for the RStudio software. RStudio Server is available through link:https://rstudio.org[rstudio.org] and is subject to their licensing terms. You should review their licensing terms before you use this sample workbench.
====

CUDA - RStudio Server workbench image::

With the CUDA - RStudio Server workbench image, you can access the RStudio IDE and NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit. 
The RStudio IDE is an integrated development environment for the R programming language for statistical computing and graphics. 
With the NVIDIA CUDA toolkit, you can enhance your work by using GPU-accelerated libraries and optimization tools.
+
To use the CUDA - RStudio Server workbench image, you must first build it by creating a secret and triggering the `BuildConfig`, and then enable it in the {productname-short} UI by editing the `rstudio-rhel9` image stream. 
For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/getting_started_with_{url-productname-long}/creating-a-workbench-select-ide_get-started#building-the-rstudio-server-workbench-images_get-started[Building the RStudio Server workbench images].
+
[IMPORTANT]

{org-name} supports managing workbenches in {productname-short}. However, {org-name} does not provide support for the RStudio software. RStudio Server is available through link:https://rstudio.org[rstudio.org] and is subject to their licensing terms. You should review their licensing terms before you use this sample workbench.

The CUDA - RStudio Server workbench image contains NVIDIA CUDA technology. CUDA licensing information is available in the link:https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/[CUDA Toolkit] documentation. You should review their licensing terms before you use this sample workbench.

Support for multinode deployment of very large models::
Serving models over multiple graphical processing unit (GPU) nodes when using a single-model serving runtime is now available as a Technology Preview feature. 
Deploy your models across multiple GPU nodes to improve efficiency when deploying large models such as large language models (LLMs). 
For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/managing_and_monitoring_models/managing_and_monitoring_models_on_the_single_model_serving_platform#deploying-models-using-multiple-gpu-nodes_cluster-admin[Deploying models across multiple GPU nodes].

#!/bin/bash
# workflow-completion-check.sh
#
# Stop hook: blocks Claude from stopping while the ACTIVE workflow
# is still running. Only checks the workflow identified by the
# .active-workflow marker — stale workflows from other sessions
# are ignored.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 = allow stop
#   2 = block stop (reason sent to stderr)
#
# Requires: jq

set -u

INPUT=$(cat)

if ! cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Cannot access project directory; cannot verify workflow status." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Look for progress files
shopt -s nullglob
PROGRESS_FILES=(.agent_workspace/*/workflow/*.json)
shopt -u nullglob
if [ ${#PROGRESS_FILES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

MARKER=".agent_workspace/.active-workflow"

# No marker file → no active workflow → allow stop
if [ ! -f "$MARKER" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Read the marker — fail closed on parse errors
PROGRESS_FILE=$(jq -r '.progress_file // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_PF=$?
TICKET=$(jq -r '.ticket // empty' "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null)
JQ_RC_TK=$?

if [ "$JQ_RC_PF" -ne 0 ] || [ "$JQ_RC_TK" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Failed to parse $MARKER; refusing to stop (fail closed)." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Marker parsed successfully but fields are empty → stale marker → clean up
if [ -z "$PROGRESS_FILE" ] || [ -z "$TICKET" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Progress file doesn't exist → stale marker → clean up and allow stop
if [ ! -f "$PROGRESS_FILE" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Check the workflow status — only block for in_progress workflows
WORKFLOW_STATUS=$(jq -r '.status' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ "$WORKFLOW_STATUS" != "in_progress" ]; then
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

WORKFLOW_TYPE=$(jq -r '.workflow_type' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

# Anti-loop guard: per-workflow counter prevents infinite blocking
COUNTER_FILE="${PROGRESS_FILE}.stop_count"
if [ -f "$COUNTER_FILE" ]; then
  COUNT=$(cat "$COUNTER_FILE")
else
  COUNT=0
fi
if [ "$COUNT" -ge 5 ]; then
  rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
  rm -f "$MARKER"
  exit 0
fi

# Get step order from the progress file
mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.step_order[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

if [ ${#STEP_ORDER[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  mapfile -t STEP_ORDER < <(jq -r '.steps | keys[]' "$PROGRESS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
fi

# Find the first incomplete step
NEXT_STEP=""
for step in "${STEP_ORDER[@]}"; do
  STEP_STATUS=$(jq -r --arg s "$step" '.steps[$s].status // "missing"' "$PROGRESS_FILE")
  case "$STEP_STATUS" in
    completed|skipped|deferred) continue ;;
    *) NEXT_STEP="$step"; break ;;
  esac
done

if [ -n "$NEXT_STEP" ]; then
  echo "$((COUNT + 1))" > "$COUNTER_FILE"
  echo "Documentation workflow '$WORKFLOW_TYPE' for $TICKET is not complete. Next step: $NEXT_STEP. Continue the workflow." >&2
  exit 2
fi

# All steps done — clean up and allow stop
rm -f "$COUNTER_FILE"
rm -f "$MARKER"
exit 0

[id="configuring-oci-storage-backend_{context}"]
= Configure the OCI storage backend for Model Registry

[role="_abstract"]
You can configure the OCI storage backend so that data scientists can register and store model artifacts as OCI images in your organization's container registry.
Configuring the backend involves enabling the OCI storage feature, creating registry credentials, and setting up a data connection to the target registry.

.Prerequisites

* You have `cluster-admin` privileges on the {openshift-platform} cluster.
* You have access to an OCI-compliant registry, such as Red Hat Quay or a registry that supports the OCI Distribution Specification.
* The {productname-short} operator is installed and the Model Registry component is enabled.
* The OCI registry is reachable from the cluster network.
* The base image used for `ModelCar` construction, such as `busybox`, is accessible from the cluster.

.Procedure

// TODO: SME verification required (RHOAIENG-16840 tech review C1).
// The `registryOciStorage` feature flag does not exist in the odh-dashboard
// source code (frontend/src/k8sTypes.ts, CRD schema, backend defaults).
// The Register and Store toggle appears by default without any flag.
// Confirm whether this flag exists in a downstream RHOAI operator component.
// If it does not exist, remove this step entirely and update the
// Verification and Troubleshooting sections accordingly.
. Enable the `registryOciStorage` feature flag in the dashboard configuration.

.. Log in to the {openshift-platform} web console with `cluster-admin` privileges.

.. In the *Administrator* perspective, click *Home* -> *API Explorer*.

.. Search for `OdhDashboardConfig` and open the resource.

.. Click the *Instances* tab and select the dashboard configuration instance for your deployment.

.. Click the *YAML* tab and locate the `spec.dashboardConfig` section.

.. Add or set the `registryOciStorage` field to `true`:
+
[source,yaml]
----
spec:
  dashboardConfig:
    registryOciStorage: true
----

.. Click *Save*.
+
After you save the configuration, the *Register and Store* option becomes available in the Model Registry UI.

. Create a Kubernetes Secret that contains your OCI registry credentials.
+
The Secret must be of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`.
The `.dockerconfigjson` field must contain base64-encoded authentication data for the target registry.
+
You must have `admin` or `edit` permissions in the target namespace to create Secrets.
Create the Secret in the namespace where the model transfer job will run.
+
In the following command, replace `<secret_name>` with a name for the Secret, `<namespace>` with the namespace where the model transfer job will run, and `<path_to_dockerconfigjson>` with the path to your Docker configuration file:
+
[source,terminal]
----
$ oc create secret docker-registry <secret_name> \
  --namespace <namespace> \
  --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=<path_to_dockerconfigjson>
----
+
Alternatively, you can create the Secret by specifying the registry server, username, and password directly:
+
[source,terminal]
----
$ oc create secret docker-registry <secret_name> \
  --namespace <namespace> \
  --docker-server=<registry_url> \
  --docker-username=<username> \
  --docker-password=<password>
----

. Configure a data connection to the OCI registry in the {productname-short} dashboard.
+
You can choose between two connection types depending on whether the registry requires authentication:

* *OCI compliant registry v1*: Use this connection type for private registries that require authentication.
The connection stores credentials in a Kubernetes Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`.
* *URI v1*: Use this connection type for public OCI registries that do not require authentication.

// TODO: SME verification required (RHOAIENG-16840 tech review S2).
// Verify whether OCI connection types (OCI compliant registry v1, URI v1)
// are pre-installed with the RHOAI operator or must be created manually.
// If pre-installed, update this step to guide users to create a connection
// instance at the project level using the existing type, rather than
// clicking "Add connection type".
.. In the {productname-short} dashboard, click *Settings* -> *Environment setup* -> *Connection types*.

.. Click *Add connection type*.

.. Select the appropriate connection type for your registry.

.. Provide the required connection details, including the registry URL and any authentication credentials.

.. Click *Add*.

.Verification

. Verify that the Kubernetes Secret was created with the correct type:
+
[source,terminal]
----
$ oc get secret <secret_name> -n <namespace> -o jsonpath='{.type}'
----
+
The expected output is `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`.

. In the {productname-short} dashboard, verify that the data connection for the OCI registry is displayed under the connection configuration.

. In the {productname-short} dashboard, click *AI hub* -> *Models* -> *Registry*.
. Click *Register model*.
. In the *Model location and storage* section, verify that the *Register and Store* option is available.
+
// TODO: SME verification required (RHOAIENG-16840 tech review C1).
// Remove reference to registryOciStorage if the flag does not exist.
If the option is not available, verify that the `registryOciStorage` feature flag is set to `true` in the dashboard configuration and that the dashboard has restarted.

.Troubleshooting

// TODO: SME verification required (RHOAIENG-16840 tech review C1).
// Remove registryOciStorage references if the flag does not exist downstream.
If the *Register and Store* option is not displayed:

* Verify that the `registryOciStorage` feature flag is enabled by checking the `OdhDashboardConfig` resource.
* Verify that the dashboard pods have restarted after the configuration change.

If model transfer jobs fail:

* Check that the OCI registry credentials are correct and that the Secret is in the expected namespace.
* Verify network connectivity between the cluster and the OCI registry.
* Check the Kubernetes events for the transfer job pods for error details.

.Additional resources
* xref:oci-compliant-storage-for-model-registry_{context}[OCI-compliant storage for Model Registry]
* xref:oci-storage-prerequisites_{context}[OCI-compliant storage prerequisites]
* xref:registering-model-as-oci-image_{context}[Register and store a model as an OCI image]

[id="configuring-quay-for-model-registry_{context}"]
= Configure Red Hat Quay as the OCI storage backend

[role="_abstract"]
You can configure Red Hat Quay as the OCI-compliant registry for storing model artifacts.
Using Quay provides built-in OCI artifact support, role-based access control, and image vulnerability scanning for your model images.

Red Hat Quay supports OCI artifacts by default in Quay 3.11 and later.
You can use robot accounts for automated service authentication, which avoids embedding user credentials in transfer jobs.

.Prerequisites

* Red Hat Quay is deployed and accessible from the {openshift-platform} cluster.
* You have administrator access to a Quay organization.
* You have `cluster-admin` privileges on the {openshift-platform} cluster.
* The OCI storage feature is enabled in {productname-short}.
For more information, see xref:configuring-oci-storage-backend_{context}[Configure the OCI storage backend for Model Registry].

.Procedure

. Log in to the Red Hat Quay web console.

. Create an organization for model artifacts, or use an existing organization.

.. Click *Create New Organization*.

.. Enter a name for the organization, for example, `model-artifacts`.

.. Click *Create Organization*.

. Create a repository within the organization to store model images.

.. Navigate to the organization, and click *Create New Repository*.

.. Enter a name for the repository, for example, `models`.

.. Set the visibility to *Private* if authentication is required.

.. Click *Create Private Repository* or *Create Public Repository*.

. Create a robot account for service authentication.
+
Robot accounts provide credentials that are suitable for automated processes such as model transfer jobs.

.. In the organization settings, click *Robot Accounts*.

.. Click *Create Robot Account*.

.. Enter a name for the robot account, for example, `model-transfer`.

.. Click *Create robot account*.

.. Grant the robot account *Write* permission on the repository that you created.

. Export the robot account credentials.

.. Click the robot account name to view its details.

.. Click the *Docker Configuration* tab to view the credentials in `.dockerconfigjson` format.

.. Save the credentials to a file, for example, `quay-dockerconfigjson`.

. Create a Kubernetes Secret with the robot account credentials.
+
In the following command, replace `<namespace>` with the target namespace and `<path_to_credentials>` with the path to the file that contains the robot account credentials:
+
[source,terminal]
----
$ oc create secret docker-registry quay-model-registry \
  --namespace <namespace> \
  --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=<path_to_credentials>
----

. Configure the Quay connection in the {productname-short} dashboard.

// TODO: SME verification required (RHOAIENG-16840 tech review S2).
// Verify whether OCI connection types are pre-installed or must be
// created manually. Update this step accordingly.
.. In the {productname-short} dashboard, click *Settings* -> *Environment setup* -> *Connection types*.

.. Click *Add connection type*.

.. Select *OCI compliant registry v1* as the connection type.

.. Enter the Quay registry URL, for example, `quay.io`.

.. Provide the robot account credentials.

.. Click *Add*.

.Verification

* Verify that the Kubernetes Secret was created with the correct type:
+
[source,terminal]
----
$ oc get secret quay-model-registry -n <namespace> -o jsonpath='{.type}'
----
+
The expected output is `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`.

* Register a test model by using the *Register and Store* flow in the {productname-short} dashboard and verify that the model transfer job completes successfully.
+
You can check the status of the transfer job by running the following command:
+
[source,terminal]
----
$ oc get jobs -n <namespace> -l app=model-transfer
----

* In the Quay web console, navigate to the organization and repository and verify that the model image is present with the expected tag.

.Additional resources
* xref:configuring-oci-storage-backend_{context}[Configure the OCI storage backend for Model Registry]
* xref:oci-compliant-storage-for-model-registry_{context}[OCI-compliant storage for Model Registry]
* link:https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_quay/3.11/html/use_red_hat_quay/oci-intro[Red Hat Quay OCI support]
