[id="oci-compliant-storage-for-model-registry_{context}"]
= OCI-compliant storage for Model Registry

[role="_abstract"]
You can register and store model artifacts as Open Container Initiative (OCI) images in OCI-compliant registries such as Red Hat Quay.
Storing models as OCI images enables fast deployment with `KServe` by using the `ModelCar` format, which reduces startup times and disk usage compared to traditional S3-based storage.

[id="modelcar-format_{context}"]
== `ModelCar` format

The `ModelCar` format packages model files into a lightweight OCI container image that `KServe` can deploy directly.
Instead of downloading model files from object storage after a container starts, `KServe` pulls the OCI image as part of pod scheduling.
After the initial pull, container runtimes cache the image on the node, so later deployments of the same model version start without an additional download step.

A `ModelCar` image consists of the following layers:

* A minimal base image, such as `busybox`
* Model files layered on top by using OCI Layers On Top (`olot`), a library that the transfer job and Python client use internally to construct the image layers

When you register and store a model as an OCI image, {productname-short} creates the `ModelCar` image automatically.
The resulting artifact URI uses the `oci://` scheme, for example, `oci://quay.io/myorg/granite-7b:v1`.

[id="benefits-of-oci-storage_{context}"]
== Benefits of OCI storage

Storing model artifacts as OCI images provides the following advantages over S3-based or URI-based storage:

Reduced startup times::
`KServe` pulls the OCI image as part of pod scheduling rather than downloading files from an external source after the pod starts.

Lower disk usage::
Pre-fetched OCI images remove the need for local copies of model files on each serving node.

Image caching::
Container runtimes cache OCI images on nodes, so later deployments of the same model version start faster.

Versioned artifacts::
OCI registries offer tagging and versioning for model images, which aligns with container lifecycle management practices.

`KServe` integration::
`KServe` natively supports the `ModelCar` format, so you can deploy models stored as OCI images without additional configuration.

[id="supported-oci-registries_{context}"]
== Supported OCI registries

You can use the following OCI-compliant registries to store model artifacts:

* Red Hat Quay
* Customer-provided OCI-compliant registries that support the OCI Distribution Specification

For Quay destinations, {productname-short} automatically uses `quay.io/quay/busybox:latest` as the base image for `ModelCar` construction.
For other registries, the base image depends on the default configured in the model-sync container.

[id="oci-storage-architecture_{context}"]
== Storage architecture

Model Registry separates model metadata from model artifact storage.
The metadata database stores the model name, version, format, author, and artifact URI, while the actual model files are stored in a separate storage backend.

When you use OCI-compliant storage, the model artifacts are stored as OCI images in a container registry.
The Model Registry metadata entry points to the artifact by using an `oci://` URI.
This separation means you can manage model metadata (versioning, lifecycle, access control) independently from the underlying storage infrastructure.

The model transfer job is a background Kubernetes Job that handles the conversion and push process.
When you register and store a model by using the dashboard, {productname-short} creates a Job in the selected namespace that performs the following steps:

. Downloads the model files from the source location (S3 object storage, URL, or Hugging Face Hub).
. Packages the model files as a `ModelCar` OCI image by layering them on top of a base image.
. Pushes the OCI image to the destination registry.
. Calls the Model Registry API to create the model artifact entry with the `oci://` URI.

The Job creates supporting Kubernetes resources (ConfigMap for model metadata, Secrets for source and destination credentials) that are owned by the Job and garbage-collected when the Job is deleted.

[id="registration-paths_{context}"]
== Registration paths

{productname-short} provides two paths for registering and storing models as OCI images:

Dashboard UI (Register and Store)::
Use the {productname-short} dashboard to register a model from an existing source location, such as S3 object storage or a URL, and transform it into an OCI `ModelCar` image.
The dashboard creates a background Kubernetes Job that copies the model files, packages them as a `ModelCar` image, and pushes the image to the OCI registry.
+
Use this path when your model files are already in S3 storage, a URL, or a model catalog.

Python client SDK::
Use the `model-registry` Python package to upload locally-trained model files directly from your workbench or local environment to an OCI registry.
The Python client uses the `skopeo` or `oras` CLI tool to push the `ModelCar` image.
+
Use this path when your model files are on local disk and are not yet in external storage.

* xref:uploading-model-using-python-client_{context}[Upload a locally-trained model using the Python client]

[id="oci-storage-configuration-parameters_{context}"]
= OCI storage configuration and connection parameters

[role="_abstract"]
You can configure OCI-compliant storage for Model Registry by using the following parameters.
The parameters are organized by scope: administrator configuration parameters for the storage backend and user-facing parameters for the OCI image format and authentication.

[id="admin-configuration-parameters_{context}"]
== Administrator configuration parameters

Administrators use the following parameters to enable and configure OCI storage for Model Registry.

// TODO: SME verification required (RHOAIENG-16840 tech review C1).
// The `registryOciStorage` parameter does not exist in the odh-dashboard
// source code. If confirmed non-existent downstream, remove the first row.
.Administrator configuration parameters for OCI storage
[cols="1,1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Parameter
|Type
|Default
|Description

|`registryOciStorage`
|Boolean
|`false`
|Enables the OCI storage feature in the {productname-short} dashboard. Set this parameter to `true` in the `spec.dashboardConfig` section of the `OdhDashboardConfig` custom resource.

|Registry endpoint URL
|String
|None
|The URL of the OCI-compliant registry, for example `quay.io` or your self-hosted registry hostname.

|Authentication credential format
|Secret
|None
|A Kubernetes Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` that contains base64-encoded authentication data for the target OCI registry.

|Connection type
|String
|None
|The type of OCI connection. Use `OCI compliant registry v1` for private registries that require authentication, or `URI v1` for public registries that do not require authentication.
|===

[id="model-transfer-job-parameters_{context}"]
== Model transfer job parameters

The model transfer job is a background Kubernetes Job that copies model files from a source location, packages them as a `ModelCar` OCI image, and pushes the image to the OCI registry.

.Model transfer job parameters
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Parameter
|Type
|Description

|Job display name
|String
|A human-readable name for the transfer job, for example `Upload granite-7b to Quay`.

|Job resource name
|String
|A valid Kubernetes resource name for the Job, autogenerated from the display name. You can edit this value.

|Namespace
|String
|The Kubernetes namespace where the transfer job runs. The namespace must have access to the model registry instance.
|===

[id="oci-uri-format-parameters_{context}"]
== OCI URI format

After a model is stored as an OCI image, the artifact URI in Model Registry uses the following format:

----
oci://<registry>/<organization>/<repository>:<tag>
----

For example: `oci://quay.io/myorg/granite-7b:v1`.

For Quay destinations, {productname-short} automatically uses `quay.io/quay/busybox:latest` as the base image for `ModelCar` construction.
For other registries, the base image depends on the default configured in the model-sync container.

[id="supported-oci-registries-reference_{context}"]
== Supported registries

.Supported OCI registries for model storage
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Registry
|Version requirement
|Notes

|Red Hat Quay
|3.11 or later
|OCI artifact support is enabled by default. Supports robot accounts for service authentication.

|Customer-provided OCI-compliant registries
|Must support the OCI Distribution Specification
|Requires a container image such as `busybox:latest` to be accessible as the `ModelCar` base image.
|===

[id="oci-authentication-methods_{context}"]
== Authentication methods

You can authenticate to the OCI registry by using one of the following methods:

.OCI registry authentication methods
[cols="1,2,1", options="header"]
|===
|Method
|Description
|Use case

|Kubernetes Secret (`.dockerconfigjson`)
|A Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` stores base64-encoded registry credentials. The dashboard creates this Secret automatically when you configure an *OCI compliant registry v1* connection.
|Dashboard UI transfer jobs

|Pre-existing login
|Authenticate to the registry by using `skopeo login` or `podman login` before running the Python client. The existing credentials are used automatically.
|Python client (workbench environments)

|Environment variable
|Set an environment variable that points to a file containing credentials in `.dockerconfigjson` format. Pass the variable name to `oci_auth_env_var` in `OCIParams`.
|Python client (automated pipelines)

|Username and password
|Pass the registry username and password directly to the `oci_username` and `oci_password` parameters in `OCIParams`.
|Python client (interactive use)
|===

[id="backend-cli-tools_{context}"]
== Backend CLI tools for the Python client

The Python client uses an external CLI tool to push OCI images to the registry.

.Supported backend CLI tools
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Tool
|OCIParams value
|Notes

|`skopeo`
|`skopeo` (default)
|The default backend. Must be installed and available in your `PATH`.

|`oras`
|`oras`
|An alternative backend. Must be installed and available in your `PATH`.
|===

* xref:python-client-upload-parameters_{context}[Python client upload parameters]

[id='overview-of-model-registries_{context}']
= Overview of the model catalog and model registries

[role='_abstract']

The model catalog provides a curated library where data scientists and AI engineers can discover and evaluate the available generative AI (gen AI) models to find the best fit for their use cases.

A model registry acts as a central repository for administrators, data scientists, and AI engineers to register, version, and manage the lifecycle of AI models before configuring them for deployment. A model registry is a key component for AI model governance.

== Model catalog

Data scientists and AI engineers can use the model catalog to discover and evaluate the gen AI models that are available and ready for their organization to register, deploy, and customize. 

The model catalog provides models from different providers that you can search, discover, and evaluate before you register models in a model registry and deploy them to a model serving runtime. Third-party gen AI models are benchmarked by {org-name} for performance and quality by using open source evaluation datasets. You can compare performance metrics for specific hardware configurations and determine the most suitable option for deployment.

{productname-short} provides a default model catalog that includes models from different source providers. {productname-short} administrators can manage and govern model catalog sources to control which models are available to data scientists and AI engineers. For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/manage_and_govern_model_catalog_sources[Manage and govern model catalog sources].

For more information about how data scientists and AI engineers discover and evaluate models in the catalog, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_the_model_catalog[Working with the model catalog].

== Model registry

A model registry is an important component in the lifecycle of an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model, and is a vital part of any machine learning operations (MLOps) platform or workflow. A model registry acts as a central repository, storing metadata related to machine learning models from development to deployment. This metadata ranges from high-level information such as the deployment environment and project, to specific details such as training hyperparameters, performance metrics, and deployment events.

A model registry acts as a bridge between model experimentation and serving, offering a secure, collaborative metadata store interface for stakeholders in the ML lifecycle. Model registries provide a structured and organized way to store, share, version, deploy, and track models.

{productname-short} supports three storage backends for model artifacts:

* *S3-compatible object storage*: Store model artifacts in S3-compatible storage such as Amazon S3 or MinIO.
* *URI*: Reference model artifacts by URL.
* *OCI-compliant registries*: Store model artifacts as OCI images in container registries such as Red Hat Quay.
OCI storage uses the `ModelCar` format for fast deployment with `KServe` and enables unified versioning with your existing container infrastructure.
You can register and store models as OCI images by using the {productname-short} dashboard or upload locally-trained models programmatically by using the `model-registry` Python client.

{productname-short} administrators can create model registries in {productname-short} and grant model registry access to data scientists and AI engineers. For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/managing_model_registries[Managing model registries].

Data scientists and AI engineers with access to a model registry can use it to store, share, version, deploy, and track models. For more information, see link:{rhoaidocshome}{default-format-url}/working_with_model_registries[Working with model registries].
//[role="_additional-resources"]
//.Additional resources
//*

# Documentation Plan

**Project**: OCI-Compliant Storage Layer for Model Registry — Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Ticket**: [RHOAIENG-16840](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16840)

## What is the support status of the feature(s) being used to complete the user's JTBD (Job To Be Done)?

General Availability. The OCI-compliant storage feature for Model Registry shipped in Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4 (published 2026-05-14). The `registryOciStorage` feature flag defaults to off and must be explicitly enabled by an administrator.

## Why is this content important?

Data scientists and ML engineers need a reliable, unified way to store, version, and deploy model artifacts alongside the container images they already manage. The OCI-compliant storage feature for Model Registry eliminates the need for separate S3 object storage by allowing users to push model artifacts as OCI ModelCar images to their existing container registries (e.g., Quay). Without clear documentation, administrators cannot configure the storage backend, data scientists cannot discover or use the register-and-store workflow, and the programmatic upload path for locally-trained models remains hidden — reducing adoption of a feature that simplifies the model deployment pipeline.

## Who is the target persona(s)?

* **Data Scientist**: Primary end user who registers model artifacts and uploads locally-trained models to OCI-compliant storage via the dashboard UI or the model-registry Python client.
* **SysAdmin**: Configures the OCI storage backend (registry endpoint, credentials, feature flag), manages Kubernetes Secrets, and ensures the model transfer jobs can execute.
* **Developer**: Uses the model-registry Python client programmatically to integrate model upload into automated training pipelines and CI/CD workflows.

## What is the main JTBD? What user goal is being accomplished? What pain point is being avoided?

**Data Scientist / Developer job:**
When I have trained a model and need to make it available for serving, I want to register it and store the artifacts in an OCI-compliant registry, so that I can leverage my organization's existing container registry infrastructure for model versioning and fast KServe deployment, while avoiding the complexity of provisioning and managing separate S3-compatible object storage.

**SysAdmin job:**
When my organization adopts OCI-based model storage for OpenShift AI, I want to configure the OCI storage backend and registry credentials for Model Registry, so that data scientists can use the register-and-store workflow without storage configuration blocking them, while avoiding misconfigured credentials or registry connectivity failures that break the model transfer pipeline.

## How does the JTBD(s) relate to the overall real-world workflow for the user?

The OCI-compliant storage feature fits into a three-phase real-world workflow:

1. **Platform setup (SysAdmin)**: The administrator enables the `registryOciStorage` feature flag in the dashboard configuration CRD, configures a data connection to the target OCI registry (e.g., Quay), and creates the necessary Kubernetes Secrets for registry authentication. This is a prerequisite — without it, the OCI storage option does not appear in the dashboard UI.

2. **Model registration and storage (Data Scientist / Developer)**: After training a model, the user registers it via the OpenShift AI dashboard "Register and Store" flow (selecting an S3 or URI source, configuring the OCI destination registry, and initiating the transfer job) or programmatically via the model-registry Python client's `upload_artifact_and_register_model` function. The model is converted to ModelCar OCI format and pushed to the configured registry.

3. **Model deployment (Data Scientist)**: Once stored as an OCI image, the model can be deployed via KServe using the OCI URI directly, benefiting from faster startup times through ModelCar's sidecar-less approach and leveraging the registry's existing RBAC and versioning mechanisms.

The documentation must cover phases 1 and 2 completely, with cross-references to existing deployment documentation for phase 3.

## What high-level steps does the user need to take to accomplish the goal?

### Administrator path (prerequisite):
1. Ensure access to an OCI-compliant registry (Red Hat Quay or BYO OCI registry)
2. Enable the `registryOciStorage` feature flag in the `odhdashboardconfig` CRD
3. Create registry authentication credentials as Kubernetes Secrets (`.dockerconfigjson` format)
4. Configure a data connection in the OpenShift AI dashboard pointing to the OCI registry
5. Verify the storage backend configuration by confirming the OCI option appears in the UI

### Data scientist path (UI):
1. Prerequisites: Model artifacts accessible in S3-compatible or URI storage; OCI storage backend configured by an administrator
2. Navigate to Model Registry in the OpenShift AI dashboard
3. Select "Register and Store" and choose model source (S3/URI)
4. Configure OCI destination: registry URL, image name, tag
5. Select namespace for the transfer job and submit
6. Monitor the background Kubernetes transfer job until completion
7. Verify the registered OCI image in the registry

### Developer path (Python client):
1. Install the model-registry Python package with OCI extras: `pip install model-registry[olot]`
2. Install a supported OCI backend CLI tool (skopeo or oras)
3. Authenticate to the OCI registry (pre-login, environment variable, or direct credentials)
4. Initialize a `ModelRegistry` client connection
5. Call `upload_artifact_and_register_model()` with `OCIParams` to upload and register the model
6. Verify the model is registered and the OCI image exists in the registry

## Is there a demo available or can one be created?

No demo link was found in the JIRA tickets or references. A Figma mockup of the UI flow is available at the [RHOAIUX-1286 design](https://www.figma.com/design/uOd61yeyzg7Mna1lNR01PH/OCI-storage-for-MR?node-id=2523-109216).

## Are there special considerations for disconnected environments?

Yes. In disconnected (air-gapped) environments:
- The OCI registry must be accessible within the cluster network
- The model transfer job requires network connectivity to both the source storage (S3/URI) and the destination OCI registry
- Container registry mirror configurations may need to be applied
- Backend CLI tools (skopeo/oras) must be available in the transfer job container image
- These considerations should be flagged for SME verification during the writing phase

## Who can provide information and answer questions?

- **Doc author**: Participant A (RHOAIENG-16840 assignee, authored MR 2680, published the 3.4 docs)
- **Technical SMEs**: Adysen Rothman, Manaswini Das (provided doc input per JIRA comment), Matteo Mortari, Ramesh Reddy (reviewers on MR 2680)
- **Backend engineering**: Federico Mosca (tagged for doc PR review)
- **UX/UI**: RHOAIUX-1286 and RHOAIUX-1455 design owners (for microcopy and call-out verification)

## Release Note needed?

Yes.

Draft release note: In Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4, you can register model artifacts and store them as OCI-compliant images in container registries such as Red Hat Quay. The new "Register and Store" flow in the Model Registry dashboard converts models from S3 or URI sources into OCI ModelCar images and pushes them to your configured OCI registry, enabling faster model deployment with KServe and unified versioning with your existing container infrastructure. You can also upload locally-trained models programmatically using the model-registry Python client.

## Documentation impact assessment

| Requirement | Grade | Rationale |
|-------------|-------|-----------|
| REQ-001: Register model as OCI image | **High** | Major new feature — new UI workflow, new storage paradigm for Model Registry, new API surface |
| REQ-002: OCI storage layer configuration | **High** | Prerequisite infrastructure configuration — blocks user workflows if misconfigured |
| REQ-003: Programmatic upload via Python client | **High** | New API-driven workflow — the UI explicitly directs users to this documentation |
| REQ-004: UX microcopy for Register and Store flow | **Medium** | UI text alignment — important for accuracy but depends on REQ-001 and REQ-003 content |

All four requirements warrant documentation planning. None are graded as None or Low.

## Relationship analysis

| Pair | Relationship | Notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| REQ-001 ↔ REQ-002 | **Complementary** | REQ-001 covers the data scientist's registration workflow; REQ-002 covers the administrator's storage backend setup. Same feature, different personas and jobs. |
| REQ-001 ↔ REQ-003 | **Overlapping** | Both cover model registration for OCI storage. REQ-001 covers the UI path; REQ-003 covers the Python client path. The concept module `proc-registering-model-oci-python-client.adoc` in REQ-001 and `proc-uploading-models-programmatically-using-python-client.adoc` in REQ-003 overlap — consolidation needed. |
| REQ-001 ↔ REQ-004 | **Complementary** | REQ-004 ensures REQ-001's procedures match actual UI microcopy labels and field names. |
| REQ-002 ↔ REQ-003 | **Sequential** | REQ-002 (admin configures backend) must be documented before REQ-003 (developer uses it programmatically). |
| REQ-002 ↔ REQ-004 | **Complementary** | REQ-004's admin settings microcopy updates relate to REQ-002's admin configuration scope. |
| REQ-003 ↔ REQ-004 | **Complementary** | REQ-004's UI call-out for locally-trained models points users to REQ-003's Python client procedure. |

### Overlap risk: REQ-001 and REQ-003 Python client procedure

REQ-001 proposes `proc-registering-model-oci-python-client.adoc` and REQ-003 proposes `proc-uploading-models-programmatically-using-python-client.adoc`. These cover the same capability — uploading models via the model-registry Python client. **Recommendation**: Consolidate into a single procedure module that covers both OCI and S3 upload paths, titled to reflect the broader upload capability. REQ-001's Python client procedure should be replaced by a cross-reference to the consolidated module.

### Overlap risk: Concept modules (REQ-001 and REQ-002)

REQ-001 proposes `con-oci-compliant-storage-model-registry.adoc` and REQ-002 proposes `con-oci-storage-layer-overview.adoc`. Both explain what OCI storage is for Model Registry. **Recommendation**: Consolidate into a single concept module that covers both the user-facing "what and why" and the architectural overview of the storage layer. The single concept serves both personas by providing layered content: high-level benefits first (data scientist audience), then architecture details (admin audience).

### Overlap risk: Reference modules (REQ-001 and REQ-002)

REQ-001 proposes `ref-oci-storage-parameters.adoc` and REQ-002 proposes `ref-oci-storage-configuration-parameters.adoc`. These cover overlapping parameter sets. **Recommendation**: Consolidate into a single reference module organized by parameter scope (admin configuration parameters vs. user-facing storage parameters).

## Theme clustering

### Theme 1: OCI storage concepts and architecture

- **Summary**: Foundational understanding of OCI-compliant storage for Model Registry — what it is, how it works, why users would choose it, and how the storage layer is structured.
- **Issues included**: REQ-001 (concept), REQ-002 (concept)
- **Overlap risk**: High — both requirements call for concept modules explaining OCI storage
- **Recommended ownership**: "Store and manage model artifacts" main job assembly, as a shared prerequisite concept

### Theme 2: Administrator storage configuration

- **Summary**: Procedures and reference material for administrators to configure the OCI storage backend, registry credentials, feature flag, and Quay-specific setup.
- **Issues included**: REQ-002 (procedures, reference), REQ-004 (admin settings reference)
- **Overlap risk**: Medium — admin settings microcopy (REQ-004) supplements the configuration procedure (REQ-002)
- **Recommended ownership**: "Configure OCI storage for Model Registry" main job assembly (admin persona)

### Theme 3: Model registration and upload workflows

- **Summary**: End-user procedures for registering models as OCI images via the dashboard UI and uploading models programmatically via the Python client.
- **Issues included**: REQ-001 (UI procedure, Python client procedure), REQ-003 (Python client procedure), REQ-004 (UI field reference)
- **Overlap risk**: High — Python client procedures overlap between REQ-001 and REQ-003
- **Recommended ownership**: "Register and store models as OCI images" main job assembly (data scientist/developer persona)

### Theme 4: Reference material

- **Summary**: Parameter tables, UI field descriptions, and configuration option references.
- **Issues included**: REQ-001 (OCI parameters), REQ-002 (configuration parameters), REQ-003 (Python client parameters), REQ-004 (UI fields)
- **Overlap risk**: Medium — parameter tables from REQ-001 and REQ-002 overlap
- **Recommended ownership**: Distributed across assemblies as supporting reference modules

## JTBD analysis

### Job Map Stage: Configure

**Main Job**: Configure OCI storage for Model Registry

**Job statement (internal planning only)**: When my organization wants to use OCI-compliant registries for model artifact storage in OpenShift AI, I want to configure the storage backend, credentials, and feature flag, so that data scientists can use the register-and-store workflow to push models to our container registry without encountering storage configuration errors.

**Persona**: SysAdmin

**User Stories**:
1. As a SysAdmin, I want to understand what OCI-compliant storage is and how it relates to Model Registry, so that I can evaluate whether to enable it for my organization.
2. As a SysAdmin, I want to enable the OCI storage feature flag and configure the storage backend, so that the register-and-store option appears in the dashboard for data scientists.
3. As a SysAdmin, I want to configure Red Hat Quay as the OCI storage backend, so that I can use my existing Quay infrastructure for model storage.
4. As a SysAdmin, I want to verify the OCI storage configuration, so that I can confirm the model transfer pipeline works before handing off to data scientists.

### Job Map Stage: Develop

**Main Job**: Register and store models as OCI images

**Job statement (internal planning only)**: When I have trained or located a model that I want to make available for serving, I want to register it and store its artifacts as an OCI image in my organization's container registry, so that I can deploy it efficiently via KServe ModelCar without managing separate S3 object storage.

**Persona**: Data Scientist, Developer

[id="register-and-store-ui-fields_{context}"]
= Register and Store UI field reference

[role="_abstract"]
You can use the *Register and Store* form in the {productname-short} dashboard to register a model and store it as an OCI image.
The following tables describe the fields in each section of the form.

[id="model-location-and-storage-fields_{context}"]
== Model location and storage

The *Model location and storage* section determines whether the model is registered with metadata only or registered and stored as an OCI image.

.Model location and storage options
[cols="1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Option
|Description

|*Register*
|Registers model metadata only. Points to an artifact that is already stored in an external location. Use this option when the model is already in OCI format or stored in S3/URI storage.

|*Register and Store*
|Registers model metadata and starts a background Kubernetes Job that copies the model from the source location, packages it as a `ModelCar` OCI image, and pushes it to the OCI registry.
|===

[NOTE]
====
If you register a model catalog model whose source is already an `oci://` URI, the UI selects *Register* mode only because the model is already stored in OCI format.
====

[id="transfer-job-fields_{context}"]
== Model transfer job fields

When you select *Register and Store*, the following fields configure the transfer job.

.Model transfer job fields
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Field
|Required
|Description

|*Model transfer job name*
|Yes
|A human-readable display name for the background transfer job, for example `Upload granite-7b to Quay`.

|*Edit resource name*
|No
|Click to edit the autogenerated Kubernetes Job resource name. The resource name must be a valid Kubernetes name.

|*Project*
|Yes
|The Kubernetes namespace where the transfer job runs. You can select only projects to which you have access. The UI validates that the selected namespace can access the model registry instance. If access cannot be confirmed, a warning indicates that the namespace might not have connectivity to the model registry. You can still proceed, but the transfer job might fail if the namespace cannot reach the registry. For more information, see xref:registering-model-as-oci-image_{context}[Register and store a model as an OCI image].
|===

[id="model-origin-fields_{context}"]
== Model origin location fields

The *Model origin location* section specifies where the model files are stored.

.Object storage (S3-compatible) fields
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Field
|Required
|Description

|*Endpoint*
|Yes
|The S3 or MinIO endpoint URL, for example `https://s3.amazonaws.com`.

|*Bucket*
|Yes
|The bucket name that contains the model files, for example `ods-ci-s3`.

|*Region*
|No
|The AWS region, if applicable, for example `us-east-1`.

|*Path*
|Yes
|The prefix or path to the model files in the bucket, for example `/kserve-openvino-test/openvino-example-model`.

|*Access Key ID*
|Yes
|The access key ID for the source S3 bucket.

|*Secret Access Key*
|Yes
|The secret access key for the source S3 bucket.
|===

.URI fields
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Field
|Required
|Description

|*URI*
|Yes
|A direct URL to the model files. Supported schemes are `https://`, `http://`, and `hf://` (for Hugging Face Hub, which uses `snapshot_download`).
|===

[NOTE]
====
For catalog models, the URI is pre-filled from the catalog source and cannot be changed.
====

[id="model-destination-fields_{context}"]
== Model destination location fields

The *Model destination location* section specifies the OCI registry where the `ModelCar` image is stored.

.OCI destination fields
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Field
|Required
|Description

|*Registry*
|Yes
|The OCI registry host, for example `quay.io` or your self-hosted registry hostname.

|*URI*
|Yes
|The image reference without a scheme, for example `myorg/granite-7b:v1`.

|*Username*
|Yes
|The username for OCI registry authentication. For Quay robot accounts, use the robot account username in the format `<organization>+<robot_name>`.

|*Password*
|Yes
|The password or token for OCI registry authentication. For Quay robot accounts, use the robot account token. For more information about creating robot accounts, see xref:configuring-quay-for-model-registry_{context}[Configure Red Hat Quay as the OCI storage backend].
|===

[id="model-metadata-fields_{context}"]
== Model metadata fields

The remaining fields capture metadata for the registered model and version.
These fields include the model name, version name, model format, and description.
For more information about registering models, see xref:registering-model-as-oci-image_{context}[Register and store a model as an OCI image].

.Additional resources
* xref:registering-model-as-oci-image_{context}[Register and store a model as an OCI image]
* xref:oci-compliant-storage-for-model-registry_{context}[OCI-compliant storage for Model Registry]
* xref:oci-storage-configuration-parameters_{context}[OCI storage configuration and connection parameters]

The RHAISTRAT-813 comments reveal the feature has both Option 1 and Option 2 flows (likely referring to different storage configuration approaches), and the backend work includes an async-upload job (RHOAIENG-32603) that was modified per UI team requests — this job likely implements the model transfer mechanism. # Documentation Requirements

**Source**: Document the OCI Compliant Storage layer for Model Registry -- covers docs updates for the model registry OCI-compliant storage feature enabling users to register artifacts and store metadata in OCI-compliant storage (e.g., Quay)
**Date**: 2026-06-11
**Release/Sprint**: rhoai-3.4

## Summary

- Total requirements analyzed: 4
- New modules needed: 11
- Existing modules to update: 9
- Breaking changes requiring docs: 0

## Requirements by priority

### Critical

#### REQ-001: Document registering a model as an OCI image in Model Registry
- **Source**: [RHOAIENG-16840](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16840) | [RHAISTRAT-813](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-813) | [MR 2680 (internal GitLab)](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2680) | [Feature Refinement Doc (Google Doc)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14KW7duspne5D9n9vcMcZABoY_JENe9EQO_LEX741OeA/edit) | [Initial Draft Doc (Google Doc)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FZVvbEArwbfzPvufTWHasG_SbEHc8PF-v88jcCtWPH0/edit)
- **Summary**: Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4 introduces OCI-compliant storage as a new storage backend for Model Registry, enabling users to register model artifacts and store them as OCI images in container registries (e.g., Quay). This feature adds a 'Register and Store' flow in the OpenShift AI dashboard UI where users can transform model artifacts from S3/URI sources into OCI ModelCar images and push them to OCI-compliant registries. The feature also includes a Python client programmatic path via the model-registry package. Documentation was published on 2026-05-14 via MR 2680.
- **User impact**: Data scientists and ML engineers gain a new model storage option that eliminates the need for separate S3 buckets by leveraging existing OCI container registry infrastructure (e.g., Quay) for model artifacts. This enables faster model deployment through KServe ModelCar integration, unified versioning with container images, and leverages existing registry authentication and RBAC mechanisms. Users interact with the feature via a new UI flow in the OpenShift AI dashboard and optionally via the model-registry Python client.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `con-oci-compliant-storage-model-registry.adoc` (CONCEPT) Concept module explaining what OCI-compliant storage is for Model Registry, how it differs from S3/URI storage, the ModelCar approach, benefits (faster startup, unified versioning, existing infrastructure reuse), and supported OCI registries (Quay, BYO OCI-compliant registry).
  - [ ] Create `proc-registering-model-as-oci-image.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Step-by-step procedure for registering a model as an OCI image using the OpenShift AI dashboard UI. Covers the Register and Store flow: selecting model source (S3/URI), configuring OCI registry destination, providing authentication credentials, and verifying the registered OCI image. Prerequisites include an accessible OCI-compliant registry and appropriate credentials.
  - [ ] Create `proc-registering-model-oci-python-client.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Procedure for programmatically registering and uploading model artifacts to OCI storage using the model-registry Python client (upload_artifact_and_register_model with OCIParams). Covers installation (pip install model_registry[olot]), authentication options (skopeo/oras login, env var, direct credentials), and backend selection.
  - [ ] Create `ref-oci-storage-parameters.adoc` (REFERENCE) Reference table documenting OCI storage configuration parameters: OCI URI format (oci://registry-host/repository:tag), base_image requirement, authentication methods (.dockerconfigjson, username/password), backend CLI tools (skopeo, oras), connection type options (URI v1, OCI compliant registry v1), and the Registry OCI Storage feature flag in odhdashboardconfig CRD.
  - [ ] Update `assembly-working-with-model-registries.adoc` (ASSEMBLY) Update the existing model registries assembly to include the new OCI storage concept, registration procedure, and reference modules. Add cross-references from the existing model registration and deployment topics.
  - [ ] Update `con-overview-of-model-registries.adoc` (CONCEPT) Update the model registries overview to mention OCI-compliant storage as a storage backend option alongside S3-compatible and URI storage.
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can understand what OCI-compliant storage is and why they might choose it over S3/URI storage after reading the concept module
  - [ ] Users can register a model as an OCI image through the OpenShift AI dashboard UI by following the procedure, including configuring OCI registry credentials
  - [ ] Users can register and upload a model to OCI storage programmatically using the model-registry Python client by following the Python client procedure
  - [ ] The OCI URI format (oci://registry-host/repository:tag) is documented with examples using Quay
  - [ ] Prerequisites for OCI storage are documented, including: accessible OCI-compliant registry, appropriate credentials/secrets, and the Registry OCI Storage feature flag enabled in the dashboard configuration
  - [ ] Authentication methods for OCI registries are documented: pre-existing login (skopeo/podman login), pull secret JSON (.dockerconfigjson), and direct username/password credentials
  - [ ] The two connection type options (URI v1 for public registries, OCI compliant registry v1 for private registries) are explained with guidance on when to use each
  - [ ] The relationship between ModelCar format and OCI storage is explained so users understand how model artifacts are packaged as OCI images for KServe deployment
- **References**:
  - [RHOAIENG-16840 comment (2026-05-11)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16840): Doc review request with Jenkins preview link and MR 2680 reference. Indicates doc input from Adysen and Manaswini.
  - [RHOAIENG-16840 comment (2026-05-19)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16840): Confirms updated docs published for 3.4 release on May 14.
  - [RHOAIENG-16838 comment (2026-04-22)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16838): Initial draft documentation link with step-by-step walkthrough of UI configuration process.
  - [Published docs (3.4)](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html/working_with_model_registries/working-with-model-registries_model-registry#registering-model-as-oci-image_model-registry): Published docs for this feature. Returns 403 -- may require internal access or VPN.
  - [model-registry Python client docs](https://model-registry.readthedocs.io/en/stable/): Upstream model-registry Python client docs. Contains OCIParams API, upload_artifact_and_register_model method, and authentication options.
  - [ODH Dashboard PR #6581](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/odh-dashboard/releases): Adds Registry OCI Storage feature flag to odhdashboardconfig CRD. Shipped in v3.4.0.

#### REQ-002: Document OCI-compliant storage layer configuration for Model Registry
- **Source**: [RHOAIENG-16840](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16840) | [RHAISTRAT-813](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-813) | [ADR (Google Doc)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZuihqjxKOJYd7vdYeyJyc3wacRTDkou4T6LI7ZK31UA/edit) | [Working Document (Google Doc)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rOvpQAjAwz_fWS4UG74-fwXhU8sU1SW3C73k88qTM08/edit)
- **Summary**: OpenShift AI 3.4 introduces an OCI-compliant storage layer for Model Registry that enables users to register models from S3-compatible or URI sources, transform them into OCI ModelCar images, and store them in an OCI registry such as Quay. Administrators must configure the OCI storage backend -- including the target OCI registry endpoint, authentication credentials, and connection types -- before users can leverage the register-and-store workflow. The model transfer runs as a background Kubernetes Job, converting models to ModelCar OCI format for fast deployment with KServe.
- **User impact**: Administrators must configure the OCI-compliant storage backend (e.g., Quay or a BYO OCI registry) before data scientists can use the register-and-store workflow to push models as OCI images to the registry. Without proper administrator configuration of the storage layer, the model transfer job will not function, blocking the entire OCI-based model registration pipeline.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `con-oci-storage-layer-overview.adoc` (CONCEPT) Explain the OCI-compliant storage architecture for Model Registry: how it stores metadata plus artifacts, the role of OCI registries (Quay, BYO), the ModelCar format, and the relationship between Model Registry metadata storage (database) and artifact storage (OCI registry)
  - [ ] Create `proc-configuring-oci-storage-backend.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Step-by-step procedure for administrators to configure the OCI storage backend: setting up the target OCI registry, creating connection credentials (Kubernetes Secrets), configuring the data connection in OpenShift AI dashboard, and verifying the storage configuration
  - [ ] Create `ref-oci-storage-configuration-parameters.adoc` (REFERENCE) Reference table of all OCI storage configuration parameters: registry endpoint URL, authentication credentials format (.dockerconfigjson), connection type (OCI compliant registry - v1), supported registries (Quay, generic OCI), and model transfer job configuration options
  - [ ] Create `proc-configuring-quay-for-model-registry.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Procedure for configuring Red Hat Quay as the OCI storage backend: Quay prerequisites, creating a Quay organization/repository, setting up robot accounts for service authentication, and configuring OCI artifact support
  - [ ] Update `proc-creating-model-registry.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Update existing model registry creation procedure to include OCI storage backend configuration as part of registry setup, alongside the existing database backend configuration
  - [ ] Update `ref-model-registry-prerequisites.adoc` (REFERENCE) Update prerequisites to include OCI registry access requirements: cluster-admin privileges for storage configuration, access to an OCI-compliant registry, registry credentials, and network connectivity requirements
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Administrators can identify the supported OCI-compliant registries (Quay, BYO OCI) for use as Model Registry storage backends
  - [ ] Administrators can follow a documented procedure to configure an OCI registry as the storage backend for Model Registry, including setting up endpoint URL, authentication credentials, and connection types
  - [ ] Administrators can create the required Kubernetes Secrets for OCI registry authentication using documented credential formats (.dockerconfigjson or .json)
  - [ ] Administrators can verify that the OCI storage backend is correctly configured and the model transfer job can push OCI images to the configured registry
  - [ ] Administrators can configure Red Hat Quay as the OCI storage backend following a documented procedure that covers Quay-specific prerequisites and setup
  - [ ] The documentation clearly distinguishes between Model Registry metadata storage (database backend) and artifact storage (OCI storage layer)
  - [ ] Prerequisites for OCI storage configuration are documented including cluster-admin privileges, OCI registry access, and network requirements
  - [ ] The documentation explains the model transfer job mechanism (background Kubernetes Job) and how to monitor its status from the OpenShift AI dashboard
- **References**:
  - [RHOAIENG-16840 comments](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16840): MR 2680 review request and published docs confirmation (May 14 2026)
  - [RHAISTRAT-813 status updates](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-813): Extensive feature status history: backend implemented Option 1 and Option 2 flows, UX/UI designs finalized (RHOAIUX-1286), signoffs completed, shipped in 3.4 stable
  - [MR 2680 (docs implementation)](https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/documentation-red-hat-openshift-data-science-documentation/openshift-ai-documentation/-/merge_requests/2680): Merge request with published doc content -- could not access (SSL cert verification failed for internal GitLab)

#### REQ-003: Document programmatic model upload via Python client
- **Source**: [RHAIRFE-156](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIRFE-156) | [RHOAIENG-16838](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16838)
- **Summary**: Data scientists who train models locally or in workbenches need documentation for the Python client's upload_artifact_and_register_model function, which uploads model files directly to Model Registry storage (OCI or S3). The current UI 'Register and Store' flow only surfaces paths for models already in external storage, and the UI team decided (Dec 2025) to add call-outs pointing users to docs for the programmatic upload path rather than embedding code snippets in the dashboard. This requirement covers creating that target documentation.
- **User impact**: Without this documentation, data scientists who train models locally are unaware that a supported programmatic upload path exists via the Python client. They may abandon the registration flow or use manual workarounds, reducing adoption of Model Registry. The UI will include a call-out directing users to this documentation, making it a critical landing page for the 'Register and Store' user journey.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Create `proc-uploading-models-programmatically-using-python-client.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Step-by-step procedure for uploading locally-trained models to Model Registry storage using the Python client's upload_artifact_and_register_model function, covering both OCI (OCIParams with skopeo/oras) and S3 (S3Params with boto3) storage backends
  - [ ] Create `ref-python-client-upload-parameters.adoc` (REFERENCE) Reference table for upload_artifact_and_register_model parameters, OCIParams fields (base_image, oci_ref, backend, oci_auth_env_var, oci_username, oci_password), S3Params fields (bucket_name, s3_prefix), and authentication methods
  - [ ] Update `proc-registering-model-as-oci-image.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Add cross-reference to the new Python client upload procedure from the existing OCI registration procedure, ensuring users discover both the UI-based and programmatic registration paths
  - [ ] Update `con-model-registry-storage-options.adoc` (CONCEPT) Update the storage options overview to mention the programmatic upload path alongside the UI-based registration flow, with a link to the new procedure
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can follow the procedure to install the model-registry Python package with the appropriate extras (model-registry[olot] for OCI, model-registry[s3] for S3)
  - [ ] Users can follow the procedure to initialize a ModelRegistry client connection to their deployed registry
  - [ ] Users can follow the procedure to upload a local model directory or single model file to OCI storage using upload_artifact_and_register_model with OCIParams
  - [ ] Users can follow the procedure to upload a local model to S3 storage using upload_artifact_and_register_model with S3Params
  - [ ] Users can identify the prerequisite CLI tools (skopeo or oras) required for OCI uploads from the prerequisites section
  - [ ] Users can configure OCI registry authentication using one of three documented methods: pre-authenticated login, environment variable, or direct credentials
  - [ ] The reference table documents all parameters for upload_artifact_and_register_model, OCIParams, and S3Params with types, defaults, and descriptions
  - [ ] The existing OCI registration procedure cross-references the new Python client upload procedure
  - [ ] The UI call-out text in the Register and Store flow links to the new procedure (verifiable against RHOAIUX-1455 mockup)
- **References**:
  - [RHAIRFE-156 description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIRFE-156): Primary problem statement: data scientists need to discover the programmatic upload path for locally-trained models
  - [RHAIRFE-156 Dec 2025 decision](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIRFE-156): Decision: no code snippets in dashboard; generic call-out about Python client + specific call-out near storage section pointing to documentation
  - [RHOAIUX-1455 mockup](https://www.figma.com/design/i7k7FnqqVi47JAUwmNQuCc/Model-Registry-2025?node-id=3193-2284&t=pYvANWC070oByvmP-1): Figma mockup showing the UI call-out design that will link to this documentation
  - [RHOAIENG-16838](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16838): Parent CCS epic -- Closed, docs published for 3.4 on 2026-05-14
  - [RHOAIENG-16840](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16840): Sibling task: Document registering a model as OCI image -- published at docs.redhat.com for 3.4
  - [RHAISTRAT-813](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAISTRAT-813): Strategy ticket: Phase 2 OCI Compliant Storage layer for Model Registry -- RHAIRFE-156 is folded into this work

#### REQ-004: Document UX microcopy for OCI storage in Register and Store flow
- **Source**: [RHOAIENG-16838](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16838) | [UX microcopy Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cnaisZft4PbGNlcPtKbHpO3JHdm6WxNJvoArHar9HyU/edit) | [RHAIRFE-156](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIRFE-156) | [RHOAIENG-16840](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16840) | [odh-dashboard PR #6441](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/odh-dashboard/pull/6441) | [odh-dashboard PR #6581](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/odh-dashboard/pull/6581) | [odh-dashboard PR #6743](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/odh-dashboard/pull/6743)
- **Summary**: The Register and Store flow in the OpenShift AI Model Registry dashboard allows users to register models from S3-compatible storage or URIs and optionally store them as OCI-compliant images. The UX microcopy requirement addresses the need for clear in-UI guidance text that surfaces the OCI artifact registry storage option alongside S3-compatible buckets, and that informs users about the programmatic upload path (upload_artifact_and_register_model Python client method) for locally-trained models. Microcopy updates have already been implemented in the admin settings screen (PR #6441), and the OCI storage feature flag (PR #6581) controls whether the OCI option appears in the dashboard. Documentation must reflect these UI text changes and guide users through the available storage options presented in the flow.
- **User impact**: Users working in the Model Registry Register and Store flow need clear in-UI guidance to understand that OCI artifact registry storage is available as an alternative to S3-compatible object storage, and that locally-trained models can be uploaded programmatically via the Python client. Without accurate documentation matching the UI microcopy, users may not discover supported storage options or the programmatic upload path, leading to confusion and reduced feature adoption.
- **Documentation action**:
  - [ ] Update `proc-registering-model-as-oci-image.adoc` (PROCEDURE) Ensure the procedure for registering a model as an OCI image accurately reflects UI labels, field names, popover text, and guidance microcopy from the dashboard Register and Store flow -- including the OCI artifact registry destination option, namespace selection, and transfer job configuration
  - [ ] Update `con-model-registry-storage-options.adoc` (CONCEPT) Document the available storage options (S3-compatible buckets, URIs, OCI-compliant registries) as presented in the Register and Store UI, with accurate descriptions matching the dashboard microcopy; include a note about the programmatic upload path for locally-stored models via the Python client
  - [ ] Update `ref-model-registry-admin-settings.adoc` (REFERENCE) Update admin settings reference to reflect the new microcopy from PR #6441 -- updated configuration tips alert ('Configuration tips: Grant UI access, connect workbenches, and set up model storage'), popover text for 'No project permissions' label, and guidance about granting project permissions for model storage that relies on project-scoped transfer jobs
  - [ ] Create `ref-register-and-store-ui-fields.adoc` (REFERENCE) Create or update a reference describing the UI fields in the Register and Store form -- origin S3 credentials, OCI destination fields (registry URL, image name, tag), transfer job name, and namespace selector -- with field descriptions matching the actual UI microcopy
- **Acceptance criteria**:
  - [ ] Users can identify the OCI artifact registry storage option in the documented Register and Store flow and understand when to select it versus S3-compatible object storage
  - [ ] The documented UI field names, labels, and guidance text match the actual OpenShift AI 3.4 dashboard microcopy for the Register and Store flow
  - [ ] The admin settings documentation reflects the updated microcopy from PR #6441, including the 'Configuration tips' alert title, 'No project permissions' label, and popover guidance text
  - [ ] Users who have locally-trained models can find guidance directing them to the Python client upload_artifact_and_register_model method as an alternative to the UI-based registration flow
  - [ ] The registryOciStorage feature flag is documented as an admin-controlled toggle that enables or disables the OCI storage option in the Model Registry dashboard
  - [ ] Documentation references the correct OCI URI format (e.g., oci://quay.io/my-org/model-name:version) as shown in the UI
- **References**:
  - [RHOAIENG-16838 description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16838): Epic description links to refinement doc and UX microcopy doc
  - [RHAIRFE-156 description](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHAIRFE-156): Detailed feature request describing the UX gap -- suggested microcopy: 'Is your model stored locally? Use the upload_artifact_and_register_model function to upload it directly into the Model Registry storage.'
  - [RHOAIENG-16840 comment (May 19 2026)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16840): Confirms docs published for 3.4 release on May 14, 2026
  - [odh-dashboard PR #6441 diff](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/odh-dashboard/pull/6441/files): Actual microcopy changes: ModelRegistriesTable.tsx and ModelRegistriesTableRow.tsx -- configuration tips, project permissions label, popover text
  - [odh-dashboard PR #6581 description](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/odh-dashboard/pull/6581): registryOciStorage feature flag implementation -- CRD-based flag defaults to false, controls OCI storage UI visibility
  - [odh-dashboard PR #6743 description](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/odh-dashboard/pull/6743): E2E test confirms register-and-store flow fields: namespace selector, origin S3 credentials, OCI destination fields, form submission
  - [Parent epic initial draft comment (Apr 22 2026)](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHOAIENG-16838): Links to initial draft documentation with step-by-step walkthrough of the configuration process in the UI
  - [model-registry Python client docs](https://model-registry.readthedocs.io/en/stable/): Documents upload_artifact_and_register_model method with OCIParams for OCI registry storage

## Notes

**REQ-001**: Documentation for this feature has already been published (2026-05-14) via MR 2680 at the URL https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai_self-managed/3.4/html/working_with_model_registries/working-with-model-registries_model-registry#registering-model-as-oci-image_model-registry. Several primary sources were inaccessible during analysis: (1) Google Doc specs returned 401 (authentication required), (2) internal GitLab MR 2680 DNS resolution failed, (3) published Red Hat docs returned 403. Analysis was constructed from JIRA ticket metadata and comments, upstream ODH and model-registry Python client documentation, community guides, and web search results. The Feature Refinement doc, UX microcopy doc, initial draft doc, and MR diff could not be verified -- the documentation_actions and acceptance_criteria below are based on the best available information from public sources and should be validated against the actual published content and MR diff when internal access is available.

**REQ-002**: Two key source documents (ADR and working document) could not be accessed due to Google Docs authentication failures (401). The published 3.4 documentation also returned 403. The MR 2680 could not be accessed due to SSL cert verification failure for internal GitLab. These gaps mean the analysis relies on JIRA ticket content, web search findings, and upstream Open Data Hub documentation. The ADR document is particularly important for REQ-002 as it likely contains architectural decisions about supported OCI registry types, credential management patterns, and storage layer configuration options. If these sources become accessible, the requirement should be re-analyzed to capture additional configuration details. The RHAISTRAT-813 comments reveal the feature has both Option 1 and Option 2 flows (likely referring to different storage configuration approaches), and the backend work includes an async-upload job (RHOAIENG-32603) that was modified per UI team requests -- this job likely implements the model transfer mechanism. The OCI storage configuration is distinct from model deployment from OCI registries (which existed earlier) -- this is about configuring the storage destination where Model Registry pushes converted ModelCar images.

**REQ-003**: The parent epic RHOAIENG-16838 is Closed and the related task RHOAIENG-16840 has published docs for 3.4. However, the published content could not be verified (403 from docs.redhat.com) -- it is unclear whether the Python client programmatic upload documentation was included in the published content or remains a gap. The RHAIRFE-156 RFE was flagged for human review with a note that it may already be delivered as part of RHAISTRAT-813/RHOAIUX-1455. The documentation writer should verify: (1) whether the published 3.4 docs already cover the Python client upload path, and (2) whether the RHOAIUX-1455 UI call-out has been implemented and points to the correct documentation. Additionally, the upstream model-registry Python client has Alpha status and the Kubeflow SDK v0.4.0 introduces a potentially competing ModelRegistryClient -- the documentation should clarify which client is supported in RHOAI 3.4.

**REQ-004**: The UX microcopy Google Doc (1cnaisZft4PbGNlcPtKbHpO3JHdm6WxNJvoArHar9HyU) could not be fetched due to authentication failure (401). This is the primary source for the exact microcopy text to be used in the Register and Store flow. The published RHOAI 3.4 docs also returned 403. Analysis is based on: (1) JIRA ticket descriptions including RHAIRFE-156 which provides suggested microcopy text, (2) odh-dashboard PR #6441 diff showing actual admin screen microcopy changes, (3) PR #6581 describing the registryOciStorage feature flag, (4) PR #6743 E2E tests confirming the register-and-store OCI flow UI fields, and (5) upstream model-registry Python client documentation for upload_artifact_and_register_model. The feature is already shipped in RHOAI 3.4 (docs published May 14, 2026).
